title: Abel-Ruffini Theorem
description: The Abel-Ruffini theorem: there is no general algebraic solution in radicals to polynomial equations of degree five or higher. First proved by Abel (1824), building on Ruffini's incomplete 1799 attempt, and later recast by Galois (1832) via the profound connection between field theory and group theory — the symmetric group S₅ is not solvable because A₅ is simple. Wiedijk 100 theorem #16, presented as a pedagogical walkthrough composing Mathlib's Galois theory infrastructure (solvableByRad.isSolvable', Equiv.Perm.not_solvable, alternatingGroup.isSimpleGroup_five) into an accessible seven-part development.

title: Abel-Ruffini Galois Theory Extensions
description: Extends the Abel-Ruffini formalization with the complete solvability classification of symmetric groups. Proves S₀–S₄ are solvable, S_n is solvable if and only if n ≤ 4, A₅ is simple (the key obstruction), and non-commutativity witnesses for S₃, S₄, S₅, A₄, A₅. Verifies group orders |S₇|=5040, |A₈|=20160. 57 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Abel-Ruffini Proof Chain: From A₅ Simplicity to Non-Solvability
description: Exposes the key group-theoretic steps of the Abel-Ruffini proof chain with each step as a named theorem: A₅ is simple → Sₙ (n≥5) not solvable, plus a 2-line type-coercion bridge from Mathlib's cardinal-level statement to natural numbers. Steps 4–5 (Galois bridge, generic quintic Galois group) are documented but not formalized here. Part of Wiedijk's 100 Theorems (#16, Insolvability of General Higher Degree Equations). Fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms.

title: Concrete Abel-Ruffini: Gal(x⁵ - 4x + 2) ≅ S₅ and Unsolvability by Radicals
description: Proves that the polynomial x⁵ - 4x + 2 over ℚ has Galois group S₅, completing the Abel-Ruffini proof chain with a concrete witness. The roots of this polynomial cannot be expressed using radicals. Irreducibility proved via Eisenstein at p=2; |Gal|=120 proved axiom-free via Vandermonde discriminant (Gal⊄A₅), complex conjugation (transposition exists), and Sylow theory to rule out orders 5, 10, 15, 20, 30, 40, 60. Realizes S₅ as a Galois group over ℚ.

title: S₂, S₃, S₄ Are Solvable: Complete Classification
description: Proves that the symmetric groups S₂, S₃, S₄ are solvable, completing the degree-by-degree picture alongside S₅ not solvable from the parent. The highlight is the bidirectional theorem: Sₙ is solvable if and only if n ≤ 4.

title: Finite Groups of Order < 60 Are Solvable
description: Formalizes the key building blocks for proving all finite groups of order < 60 are solvable. Proves the p-group chain: IsPGroup p G → IsNilpotent G → IsSolvable G, covering all prime-power orders below 60. Proves S₅ is not solvable (the threshold at 60 = |A₅|). Documents the classification: order 1 (trivial), prime (cyclic→abelian), prime power (p-group→nilpotent→solvable), two distinct primes (Burnside), three distinct primes (30 and 42 via direct argument). 4 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Galois's Solvability Criterion
description: A root of an irreducible polynomial is solvable by radicals iff its Galois group is solvable. Forward direction proved (Mathlib), reverse axiomatized (needs Kummer theory).

title: Bring-Jerrard Reduction: Tschirnhaus Transform and Bring Radical
description: Formalizes the Bring-Jerrard reduction: the linear Tschirnhaus substitution y = x + a₄/5 that eliminates the x⁴ term from any monic quintic (proved via polynomial identity). Defines and characterizes the Bring radical BR(t) — the unique real root of x⁵ + x + t = 0 — proving existence via the intermediate value theorem and uniqueness via strict monotonicity of x ↦ x⁵ + x (using Odd.strictMono_pow). The full Bring-Jerrard reduction (eliminating x³ and x² terms via quadratic/cubic Tschirnhaus substitutions) is axiomatized. The Bring radical is strictly anti-monotone, odd, and satisfies BR(0) = 0, providing a 'closed-form' quintic solution not expressible in radicals.

title: Arithmetic Mean - Geometric Mean Inequality
description: The AM-GM inequality (Wiedijk #38): $(a+b)/2 \geq \sqrt{ab}$ with equality iff $a=b$. A dual-path formalization in Lean 4 — the elementary two-variable proof via $(\sqrt{a}-\sqrt{b})^2 \geq 0$ is an original construction, while the general weighted form $\prod z_i^{w_i} \leq \sum w_i z_i$ delegates to Mathlib's Jensen-based `geom_mean_le_arith_mean_weighted`. Includes equality characterization, product-sum corollary, QM-AM-GM chain, and three-variable specialization.

title: Maclaurin's Inequalities via Elementary Symmetric Polynomials
description: Maclaurin's inequalities state that the normalized means M₁ ≥ M₂ ≥ ... ≥ Mₙ formed from elementary symmetric polynomials eₖ give a chain between AM and GM. This formalization proves: elementary symmetric polynomial infrastructure, AM ≥ GM for n=2,3,4, C(n,2)·(∑xᵢ)² ≥ n²·e₂ via Cauchy-Schwarz (general n), and AM-GM from Mathlib. Newton's log-concavity and the full Maclaurin chain are axiomatized.

title: Newton-Girard Identity: Square of Sum Decomposition
description: Proves the n=2 Newton-Girard identity: (Σxᵢ)² = Σxᵢ² + Σ_{i≠j} xᵢxⱼ, i.e., p₂ = e₁² - 2·e₂. Formalizes the double sum decomposition into diagonal (Σxᵢ²) and off-diagonal (Σ_{i≠j} xᵢxⱼ) parts for any Finset in a CommRing. Includes two-variable identities (a+b)² and (a-b)², and the explicit 3-variable case. 5 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Maclaurin Chain from Newton's Log-Concavity
description: Derives the Maclaurin mean chain Mₖ ≥ Mₖ₊₁ from Newton's log-concavity of normalized elementary symmetric polynomials, eliminating the maclaurin_step axiom.

title: Power Mean Interpolation: How Do Weighted Power Means Relate to AM and GM?
description: The weighted power mean M_r(z,w) = (∑ wᵢzᵢ^r)^(1/r) forms a continuous monotone family as r varies: HM = M_{-1} ≤ GM = lim_{r→0} M_r ≤ AM = M_1 ≤ M_2 ≤ ... This formalization proves HM ≤ GM directly via AM-GM on inverse values, M_r ≤ M_s for 0 < r ≤ s via Jensen's inequality, and M_r ≤ M_s for r ≤ s < 0 via the duality identity M_r(z) = M_{-r}(z⁻¹)⁻¹. Core building blocks (AM-GM, Jensen) from Mathlib; original proofs for HM ≤ GM and power mean monotonicity. 0 sorries and 0 axioms.

title: Negative Power Mean Monotonicity: M_r ≤ M_s for r ≤ s < 0
description: For negative exponents r ≤ s < 0, the weighted power mean M_r(z,w) = (∑ wᵢzᵢ^r)^(1/r) satisfies M_r ≤ M_s. The proof uses a duality argument: via the identity M_r(z) = M_{-r}(z⁻¹)⁻¹, the negative-exponent case reduces to the positive case applied to inverse values. Since r ≤ s < 0 implies 0 < -s ≤ -r, we get M_{-s}(z⁻¹) ≤ M_{-r}(z⁻¹) by the positive monotonicity theorem, and inverting reverses the inequality.

title: Power Mean Limit: lim_{r→0} M_r = GM (Geometric Mean as a Limit)
description: The weighted power mean M_r(z,w) = (∑ wᵢzᵢ^r)^(1/r) has a well-known singularity at r = 0. The classical theorem states that lim_{r→0} M_r(z,w) = ∏ zᵢ^wᵢ = GM(z,w). This is the continuous extension making the chain HM = M_{-1} ≤ M_0 = GM ≤ M_1 = AM complete. Fully verified with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. The proof uses the exp/log representation: M_r = exp(f(r)/r) where f(r) = log(∑ wᵢzᵢ^r), then f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = ∑ wᵢ log zᵢ so f(r)/r → ∑ wᵢ log zᵢ = log GM.

title: Power Mean Extreme Cases: Limits as r → ±∞
description: Formalizes the power mean family and proves special cases: M₁ = arithmetic mean, M₋₁ = harmonic mean. Documents the extreme cases M_r → max as r → +∞ and M_r → min as r → -∞, completing the continuous interpolation from min to max.

title: Gauss AGM Iteration and Elliptic Integrals
description: Formalizes the Gauss arithmetic-geometric mean (AGM) iteration: aₙ₊₁ = (aₙ+bₙ)/2, bₙ₊₁ = √(aₙbₙ). Proves convergence of both sequences to a common limit M(a,b) via monotone convergence and gap contraction. Axiomatizes Gauss's connection to elliptic integrals: M(a,b) = aπ/(2K(k')).

title: Impossibility of Trisecting an Angle
description: The three classical Greek impossibility problems resolved in one file (Wiedijk #8): angle trisection, cube doubling, and circle squaring. Wantzel's 1837 algebraic criterion ($\cos(20°)$ satisfies an irreducible cubic $8x^3-6x-1$, degree 3 $\neq 2^n$) settles the first two; Lindemann's transcendence of $\pi$ (1882, axiomatized in companion file) settles the third. 383 lines, 1 axiom (from PiTranscendental.lean), 0 sorries.

title: Minimal Polynomial Degree for Non-Constructibility
description: Proves that a geometric degree d guarantees non-constructibility if and only if d has an odd prime factor, equivalently d is not a power of 2. Classifies constructible regular polygons for n=3..20, verifies all 5 known Fermat primes, and proves that constructible degrees are exactly powers of 2. Fully verified: 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

title: Constructible Algebraic Numbers and Galois Groups (OQ-02)
description: A complete characterization: an algebraic number α is constructible by compass and straightedge if and only if the Galois group of its minimal polynomial over ℚ is a 2-group. This Wantzel-Galois theorem refines the degree criterion (OQ-01) from 'necessary condition' to 'if and only if', explaining precisely which algebraic numbers live in the constructible world.

title: Wantzel-Galois Characterization from Mathlib (OQ-02-OQ-01)
description: Connects the Galois-theoretic constructibility criterion to Mathlib's Polynomial.Gal infrastructure. Proves natDegree divides |Gal| for all irreducible polynomials (generalizing Mathlib's prime-degree-only result), then derives that 2-group Galois groups force degree to be a power of 2 — eliminating 1 of 6 axioms from the parent OQ-02 formalization.

title: Mathlib Contribution: natDegree_dvd_card for Polynomial Galois Groups
description: Demonstrates that Mathlib's prime_degree_dvd_card has an unnecessary hypothesis: the Prime condition on natDegree can be dropped. The generalized natDegree_dvd_card works for ALL irreducible polynomials over CharZero fields.

title: Gauss-Wantzel Theorem: n-gon Constructibility
description: The Gauss-Wantzel theorem: a regular n-gon is constructible by compass and straightedge if and only if φ(n) is a power of 2, equivalently n = 2^a · p₁ · … · pₘ where p₁, …, pₘ are distinct Fermat primes. Proved: Fermat prime recognition, φ(p) = 2^(2^k) for Fermat primes, and constructibility/non-constructibility for all regular polygons up to 17 sides. Axiomatized: the cyclotomic field degree connection.

title: Gauss-Wantzel Theorem: Regular n-Gon Constructibility
description: A regular n-gon is constructible by compass and straightedge if and only if Euler's totient φ(n) is a power of 2. Equivalently, n = 2^k · p₁ · ... · p_r where p₁,...,p_r are distinct Fermat primes. This is the third level of the constructibility OQ chain: OQ01 (degree criterion) → OQ02 (Galois criterion) → OQ02-OQ03 (regular polygon characterization).

title: Gauss-Wantzel Theorem via Cyclotomic Fields
description: Bridges the Gauss-Wantzel constructibility theorem to Mathlib's cyclotomic field infrastructure. Proves ζₙ = exp(2πi/n) properties, Chebyshev polynomial connections, complex conjugation as order-2 automorphism via galCyclotomicEquivUnitsZMod, and derives cos(2π/n) algebraicity from cyclotomic theory. 740 lines, 0 axioms, 0 sorries — all former axioms eliminated.

title: Hierarchy of Constructibility Criteria
description: Formalizes the three-level hierarchy of constructibility criteria: degree criterion (necessary), Galois 2-group criterion (iff), and tower criterion (equivalent). Proves key properties and implications.

title: Tower-Galois Equivalence via Mathlib Correspondence
description: Formalizes the equivalence between quadratic tower constructibility and the Galois 2-group criterion, with a proper inductive tower definition and feasibility analysis for Mathlib's Galois correspondence

title: Computational Complexity of Determining Constructibility
description: Decidability and computational complexity of compass-and-straightedge constructibility. Proves that constructibility (given the minimal polynomial degree) is decidable, characterizes the power-of-2 divisibility condition, and shows that n-gon constructibility reduces to checking whether Euler's totient is a power of 2.

title: Origami Constructibility via Huzita-Hatori Axioms (OQ-05)
description: Formalizes the seven Huzita-Hatori axioms of origami as a Lean 4 structure, proves that origami CAN solve cubic and quartic equations via the Beloch fold (HH-6), and establishes that angle trisection and cube doubling ARE possible with paper folding. Proves the Alperin-Lang algebraic equivalence between origami and neusis constructibility, classifies origami-constructible degrees up to 12, and distinguishes single-fold from multi-fold origami power. 695 lines, 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

title: Algebraic Characterization of k-Fold Origami Constructibility
description: Formalizes the conjectured algebraic characterization of k-fold origami constructibility: k simultaneous folds can construct exactly the p_{k+1}-smooth degrees (all prime factors ≤ the (k+1)-th prime). Proves strict hierarchy (each fold level adds one prime), monotonicity, and algebraic completeness (every degree is eventually constructible).

title: Area of a Circle
description: The area of a circle with radius r is πr², formalized as Lebesgue measure of a disk in ℂ ≅ ℝ². Wiedijk 100 theorem #9 — one of the most fundamental formulas in geometry, rigorously proved by Archimedes around 250 BCE using the method of exhaustion.

title: Circumference Formula via Area Differentiation
description: The circumference C = 2πr derived by differentiating the area formula A = πr². Formalizes the fundamental relationship that the boundary length equals the rate of change of area with respect to radius, using Mathlib's power rule (hasDerivAt_pow). Includes corollaries for differentiability, monotonicity, scaling, and the algebraic identity C² = 4πA.

title: Area from Circumference Integration
description: The area of a circle A = πr² derived by integrating the circumference C(ρ) = 2πρ from 0 to r. Formalizes Archimedes' geometric vision of the disk as a sum of concentric rings via the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.

title: N-Dimensional Volume from Surface Area Integration
description: Generalizes A(r) = ∫₀ʳ C(ρ) dρ to n dimensions: V_n(r) = ∫₀ʳ S_n(ρ) dρ, where S_n is the sphere surface area. Proves the derivative relation, FTC integral formula, shell volumes, scaling, and surface-to-volume ratio n/r.

title: Recursive Computation of Unit Ball Volumes
description: Proves the recurrence ω_{n+2} = (2π/(n+2))·ω_n for computing unit n-ball volumes from base cases ω_0 = 1 and ω_1 = 2, using the Gamma function identity Γ(z+1) = z·Γ(z).

title: IBP for Fourier Coefficients of Periodic Functions
description: Proves the integration by parts formula for Fourier coefficients: for a C¹ periodic function f with period 2π, the Fourier coefficient of the derivative satisfies ĉₙ(f') = i·n·ĉₙ(f). This is key infrastructure for the Fourier-analytic proof of the isoperimetric inequality.

title: Isoperimetric Inequality from IBP + Wirtinger + Parseval (Hurwitz 1901)
description: Clean formalization of Hurwitz's 1901 Fourier-analytic proof of the isoperimetric inequality C² ≥ 4πA. Chains three analytical ingredients: integration by parts for Fourier coefficients, Parseval's identity, and Wirtinger's inequality. The arithmetic kernel (from Wirtinger bounds to 4πA ≤ L²) is fully proved. Concrete examples verify C² = 4πA for circles and C² > 4πA for squares.

title: Archimedes' Exhaustion Meets the FTC
description: Formally connects Archimedes' classical method of exhaustion (inscribed n-gon areas converging to πr²) with the modern FTC-based proof (∫₀ʳ 2πρ dρ = πr²). Both limiting processes converge to the same value; by limit uniqueness in ℝ, they are equal. 10 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Isoperimetric Inequality: C² ≥ 4πA
description: For any regular closed curve with circumference C enclosing area A, the isoperimetric inequality C² ≥ 4πA holds, with equality iff the curve is a circle. Proves 60+ theorems/lemmas (0 sorries, 0 axioms) including arc-length reparametrization infrastructure, Wirtinger's inequality (proved from Fourier decomposition), Parseval's identity, the general isoperimetric inequality (for regular curves), equality characterization, and concrete verification for circles, squares, regular n-gons, and equilateral triangles.

title: Arc-Length Reparametrization for Smooth Closed Curves
description: Proves the arc-length reparametrization theorem: every regular smooth closed curve admits a constant-speed reparametrization preserving circumference and area. The key results are: (1) the periodic integral shift ∫_t^{t+T} f = ∫_0^T f for T-periodic f (proved via Mathlib's integral_comp_add_left and periodicity); (2) quasi-periodicity s(t+2π) = s(t)+L (proved from (1)); (3) surjectivity of arc-length via IVT; (4) bijectivity and the C¹ inverse via IFT (axiomatized); (5) the change-of-variables formula for circumference and area (axiomatized). Completes the analytic infrastructure for the isoperimetric inequality (area-of-circle-oq-01-oq-03).

title: n-Dimensional Ball Volume: Generalization of Area of Circle
description: Generalizes the area-of-circle formula A=πr² to n dimensions: Vol(Bⁿ(r)) = πⁿ/²·rⁿ/Γ(n/2+1). Proves the n=1,2,3 cases directly from Mathlib's volume_ball lemmas, establishes the Gamma function recurrence relation, and connects all cases via one axiom for the general scaling law rⁿ·Vol(Bⁿ(1)).

title: Archimedes' Method of Exhaustion: Area of a Circle
description: Formalizes Archimedes' method of exhaustion: regular inscribed and circumscribed n-gons sandwich the circle area πr², with both converging to πr² as n → ∞. The limits sin(2π/n)·n → 2π and tan(π/n)·n → π follow from HasDerivAt sin 1 0 and HasDerivAt tan 1 0. All 17 theorems proved with 0 sorries.

title: Convergence Rate of Inscribed Polygon Area to πr²
description: Proves that the area of a regular inscribed n-gon converges to πr² at rate O(1/n²): specifically 0 ≤ πr² - Aₙ ≤ 2π³r²/(3n²). The proof uses the chain sin(x) ≥ x - x³/6 (derived via MVT and half-angle identities) to bound the error. Also proves the error is strictly positive for n≥3. 9 theorems, 0 axioms.

title: Archimedes Pi Bounds: 223/71 < π < 22/7
description: Archimedes' classical bounds on π from inscribed and circumscribed 96-gons: 223/71 < π < 22/7. Both bounds proved from Mathlib's pi_gt_d4/pi_lt_d4. Fully verified: 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Dalzell-Niven Integral: π < 22/7 via Integration
description: The Dalzell-Niven integral ∫₀¹ x⁴(1-x)⁴/(1+x²) dx = 22/7 - π provides an elegant alternative proof that π < 22/7. The integrand is strictly positive on (0,1), so the integral is positive, giving 22/7 - π > 0. Proved via FTC with polynomial long division and arctan integration.

title: Method of Exhaustion for Ellipses and Parabolas
description: Generalizes Archimedes' method of exhaustion to ellipses (via affine scaling from circles) and parabolic segments (via geometric series 1 + 1/4 + 1/16 + ... = 4/3). Proves convergence rates and the general exhaustion principle.

title: The Gaussian Integral and the Area of a Circle
description: The Gaussian integral ∫ e^{-x²} dx = √π, proved via Mathlib's integral_gaussian. The appearance of π is explained by the polar-coordinate proof: squaring the integral gives a double integral ∫∫ e^{-(x²+y²)} dx dy that evaluates to the area of a circle.

title: Sum of an Arithmetic Series
description: Gauss's formula for the sum of the first n natural numbers: 1 + 2 + ... + n = n(n+1)/2. A classic result with a famous anecdote about young Gauss.

title: Simplicial Numbers: Higher-Dimensional Arithmetic Series
description: The Hockey Stick Identity: the k-th simplicial number S_k(n) = C(n+k,k) satisfies ∑_{i=0}^n S_k(i) = S_{k+1}(n). This generalizes Gauss's arithmetic series formula to all dimensions: triangular numbers (k=2), tetrahedral (k=3), and beyond.

title: q-Hockey Stick Identity for Gaussian Binomial Coefficients
description: Defines Gaussian (q-)binomial coefficients via q-Pascal's rule and proves the q-hockey stick identity: Σ_{j=0}^N q^{(N-j)(k+1)} · [j+k choose k]_q = [N+k+1 choose k+1]_q. Proves boundary cases, vanishing when k > n, the diagonal [n choose n]_q = 1, and that specializing q=1 recovers ordinary binomial coefficients. Also defines q-simplicial numbers and their recurrence. 10 theorems, 2 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: 2D Hockey Stick Identity
description: The 2D hockey stick identity: summing products of simplicial numbers over a triangular region gives higher-dimensional simplicial numbers. Proved via the parallel Vandermonde convolution identity using nested induction with Pascal's recurrence.

title: k-Dimensional Hockey Stick Identity
description: Proves the k-dimensional hockey stick identity by induction on dimension k. Defines multiHockeySum [a₁,...,aₖ] n = Σ_{i₁+...+iₖ ≤ n} C(i₁+a₁,a₁)·...·C(iₖ+aₖ,aₖ) and proves it equals C(n + Σaⱼ + k, Σaⱼ + k). The induction step applies the parallel Vandermonde convolution from the parent file. Includes 1D, 2D, 3D special cases and concrete numerical verification. 8 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms.

title: Parallel Vandermonde via Generating Functions
description: Proves the parallel Vandermonde identity Σ C(i+a,a)·C(j+b,b) = C(n+a+b+1,a+b+1) using formal power series. The algebraic identity (1-x)^{-(a+1)} · (1-x)^{-(b+1)} = (1-x)^{-(a+b+2)} is just pow_add; extracting coefficients gives the Vandermonde convolution. Fully verified, 0 axioms.

title: Rising Factorial Identity
description: The simplicial number identity S_k(n) * k! = (n+1)(n+2)...(n+k): binomial coefficients times factorial equal the ascending factorial (Pochhammer symbol). Connects unordered to ordered selections via the rising factorial.

title: Faulhaber's Formula: Power Sums via Bernoulli Numbers
description: Faulhaber's formula expresses the sum of p-th powers ∑_{k=1}^n k^p as a polynomial in n via Bernoulli numbers. Mathlib has the full proof as sum_Ico_pow and sum_range_pow. This file states the formula, derives the classical cases p=1,2,3 by induction, records Bernoulli number values, and proves the Bernoulli polynomial form.

title: The Ballot Problem
description: In an election where candidate A receives p votes and candidate B receives q votes (p > q), the probability that A leads throughout the counting is (p-q)/(p+q).

title: Generalized Ballot Problem: k-Fold Dominance
description: The generalized ballot problem: in an election where candidate A must maintain more than k times the votes of candidate B throughout counting, the probability is (a - kb)/(a + b). Formalized using lattice paths and cyclic rotations.

title: Discrete IVT for the Dvoretzky-Motzkin Cycle Lemma
description: A formal proof of the discrete intermediate value theorem for ballot-type sequences, establishing that prefix sums of {+1, -k}-lists hit every integer value in a range. This is the key analytic lemma used to prove the lower bound in the Dvoretzky-Motzkin Cycle Lemma.

title: Multi-Candidate Ballot Problem: Reduction to Classical Formula
description: Generalizes Bertrand's ballot problem to m ≥ 2 candidates: if candidate 0 leads all opponents combined throughout the count, the probability equals (a-b)/(a+b) — the same classical formula. Proved by projecting multi-candidate sequences to ±1 sequences and showing uniform fiber counts, with one axiom for the measure transfer step.

title: Chung-Feller Theorem via the Cycle Lemma
description: Formalization of the Chung-Feller theorem connecting balanced lattice paths to the Dvoretzky-Motzkin cycle lemma. Proves that prepending +1 to any balanced ±1 path yields a sequence with exactly 1 good cyclic rotation, the structural foundation for showing the uniform distribution of upstep types.

title: Continuous-Time Ballot Problem via Brownian Motion
description: Continuous-time versions of the ballot problem, connecting to Brownian motion and the reflection principle. Formalizes the reflection principle, first passage time distributions, and Lévy's Arcsine Law.

title: Lindström-Gessel-Viennot Lemma via 2D Reflection
description: Higher-dimensional lattice path problems via the 2D reflection principle. Proves the Crossing Lemma (2D version of ballot's reflection argument), the path count formula C(m+n,m), Catalan numbers, ballot formula, and Vandermonde's identity. Develops infrastructure toward the full Lindström-Gessel-Viennot lemma.

title: LGV Lemma 2×2: Lindström-Gessel-Viennot via Involution Bijection
description: Proves the 2×2 case of the Lindström-Gessel-Viennot (LGV) Lemma: the number of non-intersecting pairs of lattice paths equals the determinant of path count matrix. The crossing lemma is proved via column entry order analysis, and the Lindström involution provides a sign-reversing bijection between intersecting pairs. 0 axioms, 0 sorries.

title: General r×r Lindström-Gessel-Viennot Determinant
description: Generalizes the 2×2 LGV lemma to the full r×r case: the number of r-tuples of pairwise non-intersecting lattice paths equals det[e(Aᵢ,Bⱼ)], the determinant of the path count matrix. Formalizes LGVConfig, PathTuple, permutation path tuples, and the Gessel-Viennot sign-reversing involution infrastructure.

title: The Basel Problem: Sum of Reciprocal Squares
description: The sum of reciprocals of squares equals π²/6. Euler's famous 1734 solution to the Basel Problem launched his illustrious career.

title: Is ζ(5) Irrational? (Open Question)
description: Is the value ζ(5) = 1 + 1/2⁵ + 1/3⁵ + ... irrational? This famous open question is the next frontier after Apéry's 1978 proof that ζ(3) is irrational. We formalize what IS known: convergence, bounds (1 ≤ ζ(5) ≤ π⁴/90), and the partial results of Rivoal (infinitely many irrational odd zeta values) and Zudilin (at least one of ζ(5), ζ(7), ζ(9), ζ(11) is irrational).

title: Is ζ(5) Irrational? — Computational Bounds
description: Computational bounds and framework for the open question of ζ(5) irrationality. Proves partial sum lower bounds, tail estimates, defines irrationality measure, and documents the difficulty gap between known results and what's needed.

title: Are All Odd Zeta Values Transcendental?
description: Formalizes the open question: are all odd zeta values ζ(2k+1) transcendental? Proves even zeta transcendence (ζ(2), ζ(4)) from Lindemann axiom, axiomatizes Apéry's theorem (ζ(3) irrational), and establishes structural implications: transcendence conjecture ⟹ irrationality conjecture ⟹ known results.

title: Euler's Proof via Weierstrass Product (OQ-05)
description: Euler's original 1734 proof of the Basel problem via the Weierstrass factorization sin(πx)/(πx) = ∏(1 - x²/n²). Axiomatizes the product formula (not in Mathlib) and outlines the proof structure connecting the product representation to ∑1/n² = π²/6, with partial product convergence properties fully verified.

title: Bertrand's Postulate
description: For every positive integer n, there exists a prime p such that n < p ≤ 2n. Conjectured by Bertrand (1845), first proved by Chebyshev (1852), with an elegant elementary proof by Erdős (1932).

title: What Is the Precise Density of Primes in Short Intervals?
description: Bertrand's Postulate guarantees a prime in every (n, 2n], but how dense are primes in much shorter intervals? This formalization establishes a logarithmic lower bound π(n) ≥ log₂(n) from iterated Bertrand, surveys Baker-Harman-Pintz's x^0.525 record, and formally captures the open Cramér and Legendre conjectures.

title: Bezout's Identity
description: For any integers a, b, there exist x, y such that ax + by = gcd(a,b). Fundamental to number theory.

title: Extended Euclidean Algorithm as Computable Function
description: Formalizes the extended Euclidean algorithm as a fully computable Lean 4 function extGcd : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ × ℤ × ℕ with correctness proof. Proves (1) Bézout correctness: a·x + b·y = g, (2) GCD correctness: g = gcd(a,b), and (3) derived properties (positivity, divisibility). Verified on concrete inputs (12,8), (35,15), (252,198) by native_decide. 10 theorems, 4 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Euclid's Lemma via coprime_iff_linear_combination
description: Euclid's lemma proved formally using coprime_iff_linear_combination: if gcd(a,b)=1 and a|b·c, then a|c. The witness x·c+y·k is constructed directly from Bézout coefficients and the divisibility assumption.

title: Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic from Euclid's Lemma
description: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (unique prime factorization) derived explicitly from euclids_lemma_prime. The proof chain: Bézout → Euclid's Lemma → FTA Uniqueness. The uniqueness half of FTA is proved via induction, with euclids_lemma_prime as the key step showing a prime divides exactly one factor in a prime product.

title: FTA Generalization to Euclidean Domains
description: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic generalizes to all Euclidean domains via Mathlib's UniqueFactorizationMonoid. Every Euclidean domain is a UFD, with irreducible ↔ prime and unique factorization automatic from instance resolution.

title: Euclid's Lemma in Bézout Domains and PIDs
description: Euclid's lemma generalized from ℤ to any commutative ring via IsCoprime, with the IsBezout connection: IsRelPrime ↔ IsCoprime in Bézout rings. A single proof covers ℤ, ℚ[X], ℤ[i], and all Euclidean domains.

title: Constructive Divisibility Algorithm via Bézout Coefficients
description: Given coprime a, b and proof that a ∣ b*c, constructively compute the explicit quotient q with a*q = c by combining the extended Euclidean algorithm with Bézout's identity. The core formula: if u*a + v*b = 1 and b*c = a*k, then q = u*c + v*k.

title: Constructive Divisibility: Removing the Noncomputable Annotation
description: The parent file's constructive_div used classical choice (hdvd.choose) and required the noncomputable annotation. This formalization replaces the choice-based witness with computable integer division (b*c)/a, producing a fully computable constructive_div_computable that can be evaluated with #eval. The key insight: the divisibility proof is only needed at verification time, not at runtime.

title: CRT via Bézout's Identity for Integers
description: A clean formalization of the Chinese Remainder Theorem building directly on bezout_int: the explicit CRT solution x = a·n·v + b·m·u follows immediately from Bézout coefficients.

title: CRT Ring Isomorphism ℤ/mnℤ ≅ ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ
description: Formalizes the Chinese Remainder Theorem as a ring isomorphism: for coprime m, n, the natural map ℤ/mnℤ → ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ is a ring isomorphism. Wraps Mathlib's ZMod.chineseRemainder and proves applications: orthogonal idempotent decomposition, Bézout-based explicit solutions, cardinality preservation, Euler totient multiplicativity, and unit group characterization.

title: k-fold Chinese Remainder Theorem: ℤ/(n₁···nₖ)ℤ ≅ ∏ᵢ ℤ/nᵢℤ
description: The Chinese Remainder Theorem extends from two coprime moduli to any finite list of pairwise coprime moduli. For pairwise coprime n₁, ..., nₖ, the ring ℤ/(n₁···nₖ)ℤ is isomorphic to the product ∏ᵢ ℤ/nᵢℤ. This formalization constructs the k-fold isomorphism by induction using Mathlib's 2-fold ZMod.chineseRemainder, with the key lemma that pairwise coprimality implies coprimality with the product of remaining moduli. Includes explicit 3-fold and 4-fold specializations and k-fold Euler totient multiplicativity.

title: Ideal-theoretic CRT: R/∏Iᵢ ≅ ∏ R/Iᵢ
description: The Chinese Remainder Theorem generalized from ℤ/nℤ to arbitrary commutative rings: for pairwise coprime ideals I₁, ..., Iₖ in a commutative ring R, the quotient R/(⨅ Iᵢ) is isomorphic to the product ∏ R/Iᵢ as rings. This formalization wraps Mathlib's quotientInfRingEquivPiQuotient with explicit coprimality characterizations, proves that coprime ideals have I ∩ J = I · J, and establishes coprimality inheritance (coprime to both J and K implies coprime to J ∩ K).

title: Generalized CRT: Non-Coprime Image Characterization
description: Formalizes the generalized Chinese Remainder Theorem when gcd(m,n) = d > 1. Proves the solvability criterion (x ≡ a mod m ∧ x ≡ b mod n has a solution iff d | (a-b)), uniqueness modulo lcm(m,n), an explicit Bézout-based solution formula, and the image characterization Im = {(a,b) : a ≡ b mod d}. Includes concrete examples (solvable and unsolvable systems). 12 theorems, 1 definition, 0 axioms.

title: Efficient Verified CRT via Direct Bézout
description: Efficient CRT computation using direct Bézout coefficients without modular reduction. Proves correctness and uniqueness. 8 theorems, 0 axioms.

title: GCD Structure: Complete Solution Set of Linear Diophantine Equations
description: The complete parametric structure of all integer solutions to ax + by = c: the solution set forms a 1D arithmetic lattice {(x₀ + (b/d)t, y₀ - (a/d)t) : t ∈ ℤ} where d = gcd(a,b). Includes three-variable Diophantine criterion, GCD minimality, and the ideal characterization of GCD.

title: Linear Diophantine Systems via Smith Normal Form
description: Extends the Bézout solution lattice to matrix systems Ax = b over ℤ: Smith Normal Form decomposes A = UDV into unimodular U, V and diagonal D with invariant factors d₁|d₂|...|dₖ. Solvability reduces to divisibility of transformed RHS by invariant factors. Solution sets are affine translates of the integer null space.

title: Binary GCD (Stein's Algorithm)
description: Formalizes Stein's Binary GCD algorithm (1967) which computes GCD using only subtraction and bit shifts, and proves key GCD lemmas for correctness.

title: Step Count: Binary GCD vs Euclidean Algorithm
description: Formal step count comparison between Binary GCD (Stein's algorithm) and the Euclidean algorithm. Proves Lamé's theorem (Euclidean steps ≤ O(log min(a,b))) and Binary GCD logarithmic bound (steps ≤ O(log a + log b)). All results fully verified, 0 sorries.

title: The Binomial Theorem
description: The Binomial Theorem (Wiedijk #44): $(x+y)^n = \sum_{k=0}^{n} \binom{n}{k} x^k y^{n-k}$, formalized for arbitrary commutative semirings via Mathlib's `add_pow`. Includes coefficient sum ($\sum \binom{n}{k} = 2^n$), alternating sum, Pascal's identity, symmetry, and explicit expansions for $n=2,3$. 176 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Newton's Generalized Binomial Theorem
description: Newton's generalization of the binomial theorem to fractional and negative exponents: for any real α and |x| < 1, (1+x)^α = Σ C(α,k) x^k where C(α,k) = α(α-1)···(α-k+1)/k! are the generalized binomial coefficients.

title: Newton's Generalized Binomial Theorem via Analytic Function Theory
description: The analytic function theory perspective on Newton's generalized binomial series: ODE characterization (1+x)f'=αf uniquely determines (1+x)^α, coefficient recurrence, power series analyticity via Mathlib, functional equation, absorption identity, and explicit half-integer coefficients for the square root series.

title: Multinomial Theorem as a Generalization of the Binomial Theorem
description: Proves the multinomial theorem (∑ f(i))^n = ∑ multinomial(s,k) · ∏ f(i)^k(i) and shows the binomial theorem is the 2-variable special case.

title: Multinomial Distribution and Moment-Generating Function
description: Formalizes the multinomial distribution PMF and shows its moment-generating function follows directly from the multinomial theorem. Proves normalization, MGF formula, and connection to binomial distribution.

title: Vandermonde's Identity via the Binomial Theorem
description: Vandermonde's convolution identity C(m+n,r) = sum C(m,k)*C(n,r-k), proved via coefficient extraction from (1+x)^m*(1+x)^n = (1+x)^{m+n}. Includes symmetry, Pascal's rule as a special case, self-convolution C(2n,n) = sum C(n,k)^2, triple Vandermonde, and the r=2 decomposition.

title: q-Multinomial Coefficients and the q-Multinomial Theorem
description: Formalizes q-multinomial coefficients as iterated q-binomial products, proving they reduce to classical multinomials at q=1, satisfy the product identity qMultinom * ∏qFactorial(kᵢ) = qFactorial(∑kᵢ), and provide the quantum generalization of the multinomial theorem.

title: Binomial Distribution from the Binomial Theorem
description: Can we derive the binomial distribution and its key properties directly from the binomial theorem? YES. The identity (p + (1-p))^n = 1 gives normalization, algebraic manipulation yields mean = np and variance = np(1-p), Vandermonde's identity gives convolution, and the Poisson limit theorem follows from the derivative of log at 1.

title: The Classical Limit (1+x/n)^n → exp(x)
description: The fundamental limit characterization of the exponential function, proved from first principles: log'(1) = 1, so n·log(1+x/n) → x, and continuity of exp gives (1+x/n)^n → exp(x). Includes Euler's number as (1+1/n)^n → e, the reciprocal limit, and the compounding inequality.

title: Vandermonde's Identity: C(m+n,r) = Σ C(m,k)·C(n,r-k)
description: Vandermonde's convolution identity states that C(m+n, r) = Σ_{k=0}^{r} C(m,k)·C(n,r-k). Combinatorially, this counts r-element subsets of an (m+n)-element set by how many come from the first m elements. The classic sum-of-squares corollary C(2n,n) = Σ C(n,k)² follows by setting m=n=r and using symmetry.

title: Vandermonde's Identity: Combinatorial Bijection Proof
description: Proves Vandermonde's convolution identity C(m+n,r) = Σ_k C(m,k)·C(n,r-k) via an explicit bijection rather than algebraic/generating function methods. Constructs the bijection between r-subsets of {0,...,m+n-1} and pairs (k-subsets of {0,...,m-1}) × ((r-k)-subsets of {0,...,n-1}), using a 'split by threshold m' map. Proves forward and inverse maps and bijectivity. 14 theorems, 4 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Vandermonde Identity: Algebraic Proof via Coefficient Comparison
description: Algebraic proof of Vandermonde's identity by comparing coefficients of X^r in (1+X)^(m+n) = (1+X)^m · (1+X)^n, using polynomial Cauchy product.

title: q-Vandermonde Identity: Gaussian Binomial Convolution
description: The q-analog of Vandermonde's identity: ∑ q^{(k-j)(m-j)} · [m,j]_q · [n,k-j]_q = [m+n,k]_q. Generalizes the classical convolution to Gaussian binomial coefficients, counting subspaces of finite vector spaces by intersection dimension.

title: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture
description: One of the seven Millennium Prize Problems ($1,000,000 Clay prize). The weak BSD conjecture states $\text{rank}\,E(\mathbb{Q}) = \text{ord}_{s=1} L(E,s)$, connecting the algebraic rank of an elliptic curve (from Mordell-Weil) with the analytic rank of its L-function. This 7422-line formalization in 70 parts covers the conjecture statement, proven cases (rank 0 via Kolyvagin, rank 1 via Gross-Zagier, CM via Coates-Wiles), Koblitz correspondence (fully proved in both directions), Selmer groups, Iwasawa theory, Tunnell's theorem, the Bloch-Kato generalization, modularity (Wiles-BCDT), arithmetic statistics (Bhargava-Shankar), and BSD verification for curves 37a and 389a.

title: The Birthday Problem
description: The surprising probability that in a group of just 23 people, there's a greater than 50% chance that two share a birthday. A classic example of how probability defies intuition.

title: Birthday Problem: Tight Collision Asymptotics
description: Proves the asymptotic upper bound for the birthday collision probability: ∏(1-i/n) ≤ exp(-k(k-1)/(2n)). Fully proved from Mathlib with 0 axioms and 0 sorries, using the fundamental inequality 1-x ≤ exp(-x) and Gauss's summation formula.

title: Birthday Problem: k-Way Coincidences
description: Generalizes the Birthday Problem from pairwise collisions to k-way coincidences. Proves the generalized pigeonhole bound, classical recovery (k=2 equals non-injectivity), monotonicity, and probability formulas. Fully proved with 0 axioms and 0 sorries.

title: k=3 Birthday Coincidence: Extension Counting Framework
description: Extension-counting framework for the k=3 birthday coincidence threshold. Proves fiber partition, full-days bound, day type decomposition (empty/single/double sum to d), and restriction validity. Enables recursive computation of the exact probability that 3+ people share a birthday.

title: Slot-Based Recurrence for Efficient k=3 Birthday Counting
description: Optimizes the k=3 birthday counting formula by replacing the O(d^n) enumeration over all assignments with an O(n²) slot-based recurrence R(n, e, s). The state (e, s) tracks empty and single-occupied day slots; the recurrence R(n+1, e, s) = e·R(n, e−1, s+1) + s·R(n, e, s−1) computes the count in O(n²) operations. Proves the capacity theorem (R=0 when n > 2e+s), the upper bound R(n,e,s) ≤ (e+s)^n, and verifies the k=3 threshold for d=3,4,5 by decide. The n=88 threshold for d=365 is axiomatized.

title: Asymptotic Scaling of k-Way Birthday Thresholds
description: Proves the asymptotic scaling of k-way birthday thresholds: n_k ~ (k! · d^{k-1})^{1/k} with growth exponent (k-1)/k. Establishes exponent properties (non-negative, strictly increasing, approaches 1), classical recovery (k=2 gives √(2d)), monotonicity, concrete values for d=365, and the limit (k-1)/k → 1.

title: Borsuk-Ulam Theorem
description: For any continuous function from the n-sphere to n-dimensional Euclidean space, there exist antipodal points with the same image. The 'weather theorem' that guarantees antipodal points on Earth with identical temperature and pressure.

title: Equivariant Borsuk-Ulam: Extensions to Other Group Actions (Open Question)
description: The classical Borsuk-Ulam theorem (1933) says every continuous f: Sⁿ → ℝⁿ has an antipodal point where f(x) = f(-x). The antipodal map is a ℤ/2 action. How does this extend to other group actions? For prime p, Yang's theorem (1954) gives an equivariant Borsuk-Ulam for free ℤ/p actions on S^(2n-1). Dold's theorem (1983) gives a cohomological index obstruction for general finite group actions. For general compact Lie groups and non-free actions, optimal dimension bounds remain open.

title: Equivariant Borsuk-Ulam for Non-Prime Groups
description: Abstract framework for equivariant Borsuk-Ulam dimensions of cyclic groups Z/n with non-prime n. Derives lower bounds for Z/4, Z/6, and Z/pq from prime subgroup monotonicity. States the open conjecture that the BU dimension equals the maximum over prime divisors.

title: Fadell-Husseini Index Theory for Equivariant Borsuk-Ulam
description: Formalizes the Fadell-Husseini ideal-valued cohomological index theory for computing equivariant Borsuk-Ulam dimensions. The FH index assigns to each G-space X a homogeneous ideal in H*(BG), enabling algebraic computation of BU dimensions for cyclic groups.

title: Equivariant Borsuk-Ulam for Compact Lie Groups
description: Survey of equivariant Borsuk-Ulam for compact Lie groups (SO(n), U(n)). Formalizes equivariant map definitions, fixed-point subspace properties, and identifies ~2000 lines of infrastructure needed for the full theorem.

title: Dold's Theorem: Cohomological Index for Free G-Spaces
description: Axiomatized formalization of Dold's theorem (1983), which provides a unified cohomological index framework for Borsuk-Ulam type results. The Dold index assigns a numerical invariant to free G-spaces on spheres and shows equivariant maps respect it. From 5 axioms, we derive 11 theorems: classical Borsuk-Ulam (Z/2), Yang-Borsuk (Z/p), composite group bounds, and unification of the buDim framework from OQ02OQ01.

title: Constructive Borsuk-Ulam Theorem and Equivalences
description: Comprehensive formalization of the Borsuk-Ulam theorem (~5000 lines, ~230 declarations, 0 sorries). Includes: constructive 1D BU via IVT, Tucker's 2D lemma, Sperner's lemma, KKM lemma, formal equivalence chains, Lusternik-Schnirelmann covering theorem, no-retraction theorem, Brouwer fixed-point theorem, ray-sphere intersection infrastructure, and a complete axiom reduction chain showing all 4 core axioms reduce to a single independent axiom (borsuk_ulam_general). Applications include Ham Sandwich theorem, Necklace Splitting, Kneser's conjecture, no-odd-map-between-spheres obstruction, equivariant map hierarchy, and isobarycentric point theorem. Degree theory section covers antipodal degree and odd maps.

title: Tucker's 1D Lemma via Discrete IVT, with Interval and Circle Bounds
description: Tucker's 1D lemma proved via a discrete intermediate value theorem, together with Lipschitz and oscillation bounds on the antisymmetric difference, circle Borsuk-Ulam via IVT, and sign-change parity infrastructure toward Tucker 2D. Note: many interval-level BU statements are degenerate because 0 is self-antipodal on [-1,1]; the genuinely nontrivial topology begins on S^1. Tucker 2D and n-D are axiomatized.

title: Tucker 2D Lemma via Graph-Theoretic Path-Following
description: Formalizes the combinatorial infrastructure for Tucker's 2D lemma via graph-theoretic path-following. Defines Tucker labelings, complementary pairs, triangulated complexes, and states the parity principle that drives the proof.

title: Constructive 2D Borsuk-Ulam via Tucker's Lemma
description: The 2D Borsuk-Ulam theorem can be proved combinatorially via Tucker's 2D lemma, avoiding algebraic topology. Tucker's lemma is verified computationally for the 5-vertex triangulated disk (64 labelings) and the 9-vertex grid triangulation (1024 labelings). The logical chain Tucker 2D → approximate BU → exact BU is formalized. BU for linear maps is proved algebraically via rank-nullity.

title: Higher Categorical Analogues of the Covering Space Argument
description: Explores the covering space argument in the Borsuk-Ulam proof through the lens of higher category theory. Formalizes Z/2 involutions, real projective spaces, descent of odd maps, and covering type abstractions for higher categorical generalizations.

title: Bounded Prime Gaps (Zhang/Maynard-Tao/Polymath 8b)
description: A formal development of the bounded prime gaps theorem and its surrounding infrastructure in Lean 4. Formalizes admissible k-tuples, the Polymath 8b bound of 246, Zhang's 70M bound, and consequences including liminf of prime gaps ≤ 246. Deep sieve theory axioms are stated formally with verified consequences derived from them.

title: Bounded Prime Gaps OQ-01: Optimal Admissible Tuples and Gap Bounds
description: Formalizes the connection between admissible k-tuples and prime gap bounds in the Maynard-Tao/Polymath framework. Proves parity constraints on admissible sets, non-admissibility of small tuples via explicit prime witnesses, minimum diameter theorems for k=2,3,5, and the gap bound hierarchy H≤2,12,246. 0 sorries; axiomatized via inherited maynard_tao_sieve.

title: Engelsma's 246 Optimality: The Tightest Admissible 50-Tuple
description: The Polymath 8b bound of 246 on prime gaps comes from a specific admissible 50-tuple {0,4,...,246}. OQ-03 asks whether 246 is optimal — is there any admissible 50-tuple with diameter less than 246? Engelsma (2013) proved by exhaustive computer search that NO admissible 50-tuple with fewer than 50 elements exists with diameter below 246. This formalizes that result: the Engelsma tuple is verified admissible, and 246 is proved to be the exact minimum diameter for admissible 50-tuples.

title: Improving the 246 Bound: k-Tuple Size and Gap Bounds
description: Formalizes the relationship between admissible k-tuple size and prime gap bounds in the Maynard-Tao framework. Proves D(2)=2 and D(3)=6 from scratch (consecutive non-admissibility and parity arguments), proves admissible k-tuples exist for all k via factorial construction, establishes diameter lower bound D(k) >= k-1, axiomatizes D(50)=246 from Engelsma's exhaustive computation, and analyzes the 246 barrier.

title: Bombieri-Vinogradov Theorem: Formalizability Assessment
description: Can the Bombieri-Vinogradov theorem be formalized in Lean/Mathlib? This assesses the key analytic ingredient missing from the Maynard-Tao bounded prime gaps proof chain. BV states that primes are equidistributed in arithmetic progressions for almost all moduli up to √x. We formalize the theorem statement, define Chebyshev ψ functions, establish the level of distribution concept, and map the prerequisite roadmap (~12000 lines across 4 layers).

title: Pólya-Vinogradov Inequality
description: The Pólya-Vinogradov inequality: character sums over intervals are bounded by √q·log(q). Foundation for equidistribution of primes in arithmetic progressions.

title: Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem
description: Every continuous function from a closed ball to itself has at least one fixed point. A cornerstone of topology with profound applications in economics, game theory, and differential equations.

title: Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem: 1D Elementary Proof via IVT
description: Proves the 1D Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem elementarily using only the Intermediate Value Theorem, without algebraic topology. Shows 1D Brouwer is equivalent to IVT and proves Borsuk-Ulam in 1D, the No-Retraction theorem, and Banach contraction as a stronger special case. Explains why n≥2 requires algebraic topology (homology). 16 theorems, 0 axioms.

title: No-Retraction Theorem via Singular Homology
description: Proves the No-Retraction Theorem — there is no continuous retraction r : B^n → S^{n-1} — using the singular homology approach. The pure algebraic argument (id : ℤ →+ ℤ cannot factor through Unit) is fully proved with 0 axioms. The singular homology computations (H_{n-1}(S^{n-1}) ≅ ℤ, H_{n-1}(B^n) = 0, functoriality) are axiomatized with 1 abstract axiom. 11 theorems, 1 axiom.

title: Computational Complexity of Approximate Fixed Points (OQ-02)
description: A comprehensive formalization of the computational complexity landscape for finding approximate fixed points. Covers binary search optimality (O(log 1/epsilon) in 1D), contraction mapping convergence with explicit error bounds, PPAD structure and solution existence via pigeonhole, Sperner's lemma, fixed point stability under perturbation, and Krasnoselskii-Mann averaged iteration.

title: Query Complexity for Specific Function Classes (OQ-02/OQ-02)
description: Formalization of query complexity bounds for finding approximate fixed points across function class hierarchy: contractions (geometric convergence), Lipschitz maps (binary search), and smooth contractions (quadratic/Newton-type convergence). Proves tight bounds, information-theoretic lower bounds, and double-exponential convergence for quadratic iteration.

title: Kakutani Fixed Point Theorem (OQ-04)
description: Kakutani's generalization of Brouwer's fixed point theorem to set-valued (multi-valued) maps, with applications to Nash equilibrium existence.

title: Kakutani Fixed Point Theorem (Infinite-Dimensional)
description: Formalizes Kakutani's fixed point theorem for set-valued maps and its infinite-dimensional generalization (Fan-Glicksberg). Includes application to Nash equilibrium existence and the hierarchy of fixed point theorems.

title: Buffon's Needle Problem
description: If a needle of length l is dropped onto a floor with parallel lines spaced distance d apart, the probability it crosses a line is 2l/(pi*d).

title: Buffon-Barbier for C¹ Curves: Smooth Noodle Theorem (Complete)
description: Proves the Buffon-Barbier theorem for C¹ smooth planar curves: any curve γ : ℝ → ℝ × ℝ of arc length L dropped on a parallel line grid (spacing d) has expected crossings 2L/(πd). This file fills the gap from BuffonsNeedleOQ01OQ01.lean by proving that C¹ smoothness automatically gives the required integrability, requiring no additional hypotheses beyond `ContDiff ℝ 1 γ`.

title: Buffon-Barbier: Angular Average and the Smooth Curve Formula
description: Proves the Buffon-Barbier smooth curve theorem (E[crossings] = 2L/(πd)) from first principles using the angular average identity ∫_0^π |a sin θ + b cos θ| dθ = 2√(a²+b²). This resolves the open question in buffons-needle-oq-01 by replacing the axiomatic smooth case with a concrete verified proof.

title: Buffon's Noodle: Axiom-Free Smooth Case via Concrete Integration
description: Eliminates the two axioms from BuffonsNoodle.lean by showing the smooth Buffon-Barbier theorem (E[crossings] = 2L/(πd)) is provable using the angular-average integration framework. The axiomatic smoothExpectedCrossings is replaced by the concrete double-integral definition concreteSmoothExpectedCrossings, and buffon_noodle_smooth_eq becomes a theorem via buffon_smooth_of_contDiff. All downstream results (shape independence, non-negativity, monotonicity) are re-derived axiom-free.

title: Buffon's Needle: Higher-Dimensional Hyperplane Arrangements
description: Generalizes Buffon's needle to n-dimensional Euclidean space with parallel hyperplane arrangements. Defines the dimensional constant c_n via the Gamma function, proves c₂=2/π (classical), c₃=1 (3D), c₄=4/π (4D), and establishes structural properties: linearity, positivity, monotonicity, and the Cauchy-Crofton mean width connection.

title: 3D Buffon's Noodle: Parallel Planes Formula E = L/(2d)
description: Proves the 3D Buffon formula: a polygonal curve of total length L dropped on a family of parallel planes (spacing d) has expected crossing count E[crossings] = L/(2d). The key is the sphere average E_{S²}[|cos φ|] = 1/2, proved by computing ∫₀^π sin θ |cos θ| dθ = 1 via the substitution |cos θ| = cos θ on [0,π/2] and |cos θ| = -cos θ on [π/2,π]. Compares with the 2D Buffon formula 2L/(πd), proving the 3D crossing factor α₃ = 1/2 is strictly less than the 2D factor α₂ = 2/π.

title: N-Dimensional Buffon Noodle: Crossing Factor Recurrence αₙ₊₂ = (n/(n+1))αₙ
description: Formalizes the general n-dimensional Buffon noodle formula E[crossings] = αₙ · L/d, where the crossing factor αₙ = E_{S^{n-1}}[|u₁|] = Γ(n/2)/(√π·Γ((n+1)/2)) satisfies the recurrence α_{n+2} = (n/(n+1))·αₙ. Verifies α₂ = 2/π, α₃ = 1/2, α₄ = 4/(3π), α₅ = 3/8. Proves the crossing factor strictly decreases with dimension (each 2-step reduces by factor n/(n+1) < 1) and establishes the general noodle theorem (additivity, scaling, monotonicity) in arbitrary dimension.

title: Smooth 3D Buffon Noodle: E[crossings] = L/(2d) for C¹ Curves in ℝ³
description: Extends the 3D Buffon formula from polygonal paths to smooth C¹ curves in ℝ³. Defines 3D arc length via component-wise integration, axiomatizes the smooth expected crossing formula E = L/(2d), and verifies shape independence, monotonicity, approximation convergence, Lipschitz stability, and the dimension comparison 3D < 2D (ratio 4/π).

title: Burnside's Lemma and Necklace Counting
description: Burnside's lemma (orbit-counting theorem): for a finite group G acting on a set X, the number of orbits equals the average number of fixed points. Applied to count binary necklaces of length 4 via cyclic group rotation.

title: Pólya Enumeration Theorem for Cyclic Groups
description: The Pólya enumeration theorem (PET) generalizes Burnside's lemma by identifying the precise fixed-point count for each group element. For cyclic rotation by r on n positions with k colors, the number of fixed colorings is k^gcd(r,n), where gcd(r,n) equals the number of orbits. Combined with Burnside's lemma, this yields the Pólya necklace formula: n·(#distinct k-necklaces) = Σ_{d|n} φ(n/d)·k^d. Concretely verified for binary 4-necklaces: 2^4 + 2^1 + 2^2 + 2^1 = 24, giving 6 distinct necklaces.

title: Cantor's Diagonalization Theorem
description: Cantor's elegant 1891 proof that the real numbers are uncountable, using the famous diagonal argument to show no enumeration can list all infinite binary sequences.

title: The Continuum Hypothesis: Is There a Cardinality Between Countable and Continuum?
description: Cantor's diagonal argument proves aleph_0 < 2^aleph_0, but can it tell us whether any cardinal lies between them? This extension explores the beth number hierarchy, König's constraint, and why CH is independent of the diagonal argument.

title: The Continuum Hypothesis: Independence and Consequences
description: Formalizes the Continuum Hypothesis: whether an intermediate cardinal exists between ℵ₀ and 2^ℵ₀ is independent of ZFC. Proves CH ↔ no intermediate, constructs explicit intermediates under ¬CH, and states König's constraint and Easton's theorem.

title: König's Constraint from Mathlib's Cofinality API
description: Proves König's cofinality constraint (cf(2^ℵ₀) > ℵ₀) directly from Mathlib's Cardinal.lt_cof_power. Shows which alephs are excluded as possible values for the continuum (ℵ_ω, etc.) and which are permitted (all successor alephs).

title: Cardinality of the Set of All Countable Ordinals
description: What is the cardinality of the set of all countable ordinals? A Cantor-style diagonal argument shows this set is uncountable: any countable enumeration of countable ordinals misses a countable ordinal, proving the set has cardinality ℵ₁.

title: ω₁ Properties: Aleph Hierarchy, Regularity, and Cofinality
description: Structural properties of ω₁ = (ℵ₁).ord: aleph hierarchy ℵ_α < ℵ_(α+1), regularity of ℵ₁, uncountable cofinality, and ordinal characterizations.

title: Diagonal Argument Generalized to Regular Cardinals
description: Generalizes the Cantor diagonal argument from countable ordinals (ω₁) to arbitrary regular cardinals κ. For any regular uncountable cardinal κ: (1) any family of ordinals below κ.ord indexed by < κ elements has supremum still below κ.ord (regular_sup_bounded), (2) there exists an ordinal above all elements of any such family (regular_diagonal), (3) no < κ-sized family can surject onto ordinals below κ.ord (regular_no_surjection). 6 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem and Cantor's Theorem
description: The Lawvere fixed-point theorem: if there exists a surjection e : A -> (A -> B), then every endomorphism f : B -> B has a fixed point. Cantor's theorem follows as a corollary by noting that negation (Not) has no fixed point in Prop, so no surjection A -> (A -> Prop) can exist. This unifies Cantor's diagonal argument and Russell's paradox as instances of a single principle, and the Bool variant captures the algebraic pattern underlying the halting problem (though a full formalization of Turing's undecidability result would require additional computational machinery).

title: Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem: Categorical Generalization
description: Generalizes the Lawvere fixed-point theorem from type theory to an abstract evaluation structure, recovering the original categorical generality. Proves the abstract fixed-point theorem, diagonal lemma, type-theoretic recovery, and three concrete instances (Cantor/Prop, Bool, Nat). Includes a categorical framework sketch for the topos-theoretic setting.

title: Completing Categorical Lawvere: Explicit Evaluation Morphism
description: Resolves the 2 sorries in CantorDiagonalizationOQ03OQ01.lean by identifying the root cause (the evaluation morphism e : Pt A → Pt(B^A) was implicit and replaced by a sorry placeholder) and providing the correct formulation. The key fix: make e explicit as a parameter, so C.apply (e a) x is well-typed. The categorical theorem then reduces immediately to lawvere_abstract via an EvalStructure with eval = fun a x => C.apply (e a) x. Also proves categorical Cantor's theorem and shows the categorical version specializes to the type-theoretic version.

title: Lawvere Fixed-Point Theorem: Retraction Version
description: The retraction formulation of Lawvere's fixed-point theorem: if a type Y codes its own endomorphisms via an encode/decode pair with decode . encode = id, then every endomorphism f : Y -> Y has a fixed point. This complements the surjection version (OQ03) by making the section-retraction structure explicit. Derives impossibility results for Nat, Bool, Prop, Cantor's theorem for arbitrary codomains, and extracts the Y combinator constructively.

title: Cantor's Theorem
description: For any set A, there is no surjection from A to its power set P(A). This establishes that |A| < |P(A)| = 2^|A|, proving the hierarchy of infinite cardinalities.

title: The Cardinality of 𝒫(ℝ): What is |P(R)|?
description: The power set of the reals has cardinality 2^𝔠 = 2^(2^ℵ₀) = ℶ₂, the second beth number. This is definitively provable in ZFC via Cantor's theorem and the beth hierarchy. The residual open question — what is the aleph-index of ℶ₂? — is independent of ZFC (Easton's theorem). Under GCH + CH, |𝒫(ℝ)| = ℵ₂; without GCH, König's constraint rules out many values but the exact index remains undetermined.

title: Is |P(R)| = aleph_2? Complete Characterization
description: Shows |P(R)| = aleph_2 is equivalent to CH + GCH at the continuum level. Proves the implication in both directions and establishes unconditional bounds.

title: Lawvere's Fixed-Point Theorem: The Unity of Diagonal Arguments
description: Lawvere's Fixed-Point Theorem (1969) reveals that Cantor's theorem, Russell's paradox, Gödel's incompleteness, and Girard's paradox are all instances of a single categorical diagonal argument: if f : α → (α → β) is surjective, then every g : β → β has a fixed point. Paradoxes arise because certain functions (like ¬ : Prop → Prop) have no fixed points, making surjection impossible.

title: The Diagonal Argument in Cardinal Arithmetic and Beyond
description: A hierarchy of diagonal arguments of increasing generality: Lawvere (uniform fixed-point-free dodge), Coordinate Diagonal (pointwise dodge), and König's Principle (heterogeneous types and dodges at each index). König captures cardinal arithmetic (Σ κᵢ < Π λᵢ), while Cantor and Lawvere are special cases. The diagonal works on Bool, ℕ, ℤ, Prop, and any type with a fixed-point-free endomorphism.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality
description: Fully verified formalization of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in three forms: abstract inner product (via Mathlib), two-variable algebraic (via Lagrange identity), and finite sums (via EuclideanSpace embedding). Includes equality characterization (linear dependence) and applications to the triangle inequality and correlation bound.

title: Bunyakovsky-Schwarz Integral Inequality
description: (integral f*g)^2 <= (integral f^2)*(integral g^2). The integral form of Cauchy-Schwarz via L^2 inner product spaces.

title: Hölder's Inequality as a Generalization of Cauchy-Schwarz
description: Hölder's integral inequality ∫|fg|dμ ≤ (∫|f|^p dμ)^{1/p}·(∫|g|^q dμ)^{1/q} for conjugate exponents, with Cauchy-Schwarz as the p=q=2 special case.

title: Hölder's Inequality in eLpNorm Form
description: Formalizes Hölder's inequality hierarchy using Mathlib 4.26+ eLpNorm API: Young → Hölder (lintegral) → Cauchy-Schwarz (p=q=2) → Minkowski (eLpNorm triangle) → L² inner product CS.

title: Finite-Dimensional Cauchy-Schwarz, AM-GM, Nesbitt, and Titu's Lemma
description: Concrete applications of Cauchy-Schwarz and AM-GM in finite dimensions. Proves CS for ℝ² and ℝ³ via Lagrange identity, Young's inequality (including ε-form), AM-GM via square root, QM-AM, Titu's lemma (Engel form), Nesbitt's inequality, and Schur's inequality. All 13 theorems fully verified from first principles using nlinarith and sum-of-squares decompositions.

title: Power Mean Inequality Chain
description: The complete power mean inequality chain for two positive reals: min ≤ HM ≤ GM ≤ AM ≤ QM ≤ max. Each step proved from first principles using nlinarith and sqrt monotonicity.

title: Riesz Representation for Lp Spaces
description: Can the Riesz representation theorem (Lp)* ≅ Lq be derived from the eLpNorm Hölder inequality? Answer: partially — the embedding direction yes, surjectivity requires Radon-Nikodým.

title: Riesz-Thorin Interpolation from Hölder's Inequality
description: Formalizes the connection between Hölder's inequality and the Riesz-Thorin interpolation theorem, showing Hölder provides endpoint estimates while the full proof requires the three-lines lemma.

title: Minkowski Integral Inequality as Corollary of Cauchy-Schwarz
description: Can Minkowski's inequality ‖f+g‖_p ≤ ‖f‖_p + ‖g‖_p be derived as a corollary of the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality? We prove three explicit paths: (1) For p=2, Minkowski follows directly from inner-product CS via the norm-squared identity. (2) For general p≥1, Minkowski follows from Hölder (generalized CS). (3) The full two-variable Minkowski integral inequality ‖∫F(·,y)dν‖_{Lp} ≤ ∫‖F(·,y)‖_{Lp}dν is proved via Bochner integration in Lp spaces (norm_integral_le_integral_norm).

title: Strict Minkowski Inequality: Equality iff Proportional
description: Equality in the triangle inequality ‖f+g‖ = ‖f‖+‖g‖ holds in a real inner product space if and only if the vectors are non-negatively proportional: ‖f‖•g = ‖g‖•f. The proof reduces to Cauchy-Schwarz equality via squaring, then characterizes proportionality through ‖‖f‖•g - ‖g‖•f‖² = 0.

title: Explicit Lp Minkowski via the Hölder Chain
description: Unwraps the NormedAddCommGroup instance for Lp spaces to expose the full dependency chain: Young's inequality → Hölder's inequality → Minkowski's inequality. Proves each step explicitly with Mathlib primitives.

title: Complex L2 Cauchy-Schwarz via Bridge Theorem
description: Extends the Bunyakovsky-Schwarz integral inequality from real to complex L2 spaces via a bridge theorem connecting the abstract inner product to the integral of pointwise inner products.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz for Complex Inner Product Spaces
description: Extension of Cauchy-Schwarz to complex inner product spaces: ‖⟪u,v⟫_ℂ‖ ≤ ‖u‖·‖v‖. Mathlib's norm_inner_le_norm works uniformly for all RCLike fields, answering yes to the open question.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz Equality for Complex Inner Product Spaces
description: Equality characterization for the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality in complex (and general RCLike) inner product spaces: ‖⟪u,v⟫‖ = ‖u‖·‖v‖ if and only if u and v are linearly dependent.

title: Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization via Cauchy-Schwarz
description: The Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process uses orthogonal projection at each step. The projection coefficient is bounded by Cauchy-Schwarz: the norm of the projection never exceeds the norm of the input. This formalization builds Gram-Schmidt from scratch using the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality as the quantitative backbone.

title: Heisenberg Uncertainty from Complex Cauchy-Schwarz
description: Derives the Heisenberg uncertainty principle σ_x·σ_p ≥ ℏ/2 from the complex Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. Pure algebraic derivation in abstract inner product spaces.

title: Bessel's Inequality for Hilbert Spaces
description: Formalizes Bessel's inequality ∑ᵢ |⟨vᵢ,x⟩|² ≤ ‖x‖² for orthonormal families in Hilbert spaces, and Parseval's identity for Hilbert bases, as consequences of Cauchy-Schwarz and the Pythagorean theorem.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz OQ-02: Hölder, L² Theory, and Minkowski
description: Extends Cauchy-Schwarz to the Hölder-Minkowski family. Proves Hölder's inequality for finite NNReal sums (Cauchy-Schwarz is the p=q=2 case), the L² Pythagorean theorem (orthogonal functions have ‖f+g‖²=‖f‖²+‖g‖²), the parallelogram law in L², the inner product polarization identity, weighted Cauchy-Schwarz for finite sums, and Minkowski's triangle inequality for Lp norms. 18 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Parseval's Identity: Energy Conservation in Fourier Analysis
description: Formalizes Parseval's identity — ∑|ĉₙ(f)|² = ∫|f|²dμ — as a consequence of the L² structure from CauchySchwarzOQ02. Proves: Parseval energy equality (tsum = integral), Bessel-Parseval tightness (Bessel's inequality is equality in total), Fourier orthonormality, Pythagorean theorem for finite Fourier sums, L² convergence of Fourier series, and completeness (zero-kernel). 10 theorems, 0 sorries.

title: Hölder's Inequality as Cauchy-Schwarz Generalization
description: Hölder's inequality ∑f_i·g_i ≤ (∑f_i^p)^(1/p)·(∑g_i^q)^(1/q) for conjugate exponents 1/p+1/q=1, proved via Young's inequality normalization. Cauchy-Schwarz emerges as the p=q=2 special case. Proof chain: Young → Normalized Hölder → General Hölder → Lagrange identity → Cauchy-Schwarz.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz Equality Characterization
description: Formalizes when equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz and Hölder inequalities. CS equality (∑fᵢgᵢ)² = (∑fᵢ²)(∑gᵢ²) iff proportional, proved via Lagrange identity. Extended to general Hölder: equality iff power proportionality fᵢ^p = c·gᵢ^q, proved via Young deficit reduction. Lifted to measure-theoretic integrals.

title: Minkowski's Inequality from Holder's Inequality
description: Minkowski's inequality (sum(f_i+g_i)^p)^(1/p) <= (sum f_i^p)^(1/p) + (sum g_i^p)^(1/p) derived from Holder's inequality. Covers NNReal and real-valued finite sums, p=1 (triangle inequality), p=2 (Euclidean norm), inner product spaces, and Lp integral form. Extends the Young -> Holder -> Cauchy-Schwarz chain with the Lp triangle inequality.

title: Cauchy-Schwarz Equality: Exact Proportionality Constant
description: When |inner u v| = norm u * norm v, the exact proportionality constant is u = (inner u v / norm v^2) * v. Proves the biconditional characterization, projection coefficient properties, geometric interpretation, and finite sum version via the Lagrange identity.

title: Cayley-Hamilton Theorem
description: Every square matrix satisfies its own characteristic polynomial. If A is an n×n matrix with characteristic polynomial p(λ) = det(λI - A), then p(A) = 0.

title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction and Annihilator Theory
description: The minimal polynomial gives an optimal polynomial reduction for matrix evaluation, tighter than the characteristic polynomial. For any polynomial f and matrix M, aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly(M)). The annihilator ideal of M is generated by the minimal polynomial.

title: Jordan Canonical Form and the Minimal Polynomial
description: Characterizes the minimal polynomial of a linear endomorphism via eigenvalues and Jordan block structure. Proves eigenvalues ↔ roots of minpoly, minpoly | charpoly, semisimple ↔ squarefree minpoly, nilpotent ↔ minpoly = X^k. Axiomatizes the JCF product formula: minpoly = Π (X-μ)^{e_μ} where e_μ = size of largest Jordan block for eigenvalue μ. 20 theorems, 0 definitions, 3 axioms.

title: Similar Matrices Have Identical Minimal Polynomials
description: A formal proof that similar matrices B = P⁻¹AP share the same minimal polynomial over any field K. The inner conjugation map A ↦ P⁻¹AP is formalized as a K-algebra endomorphism, and polynomial evaluation is shown to commute with conjugation via aeval_algHom_apply.

title: Minimal Polynomial Generalization to K-Algebras
description: A formal proof that the minimal polynomial is invariant under K-algebra isomorphisms and injective K-algebra homomorphisms. Matrix similarity is shown to be a special case: conjugation by an invertible matrix defines an AlgEquiv, and the abstract result from Mathlib immediately yields minpoly(P⁻¹AP) = minpoly(A).

title: Skolem-Noether Theorem: K-Algebra Automorphisms of Mₙ(K)
description: A fully verified proof of the Skolem-Noether theorem for matrix algebras: every K-algebra automorphism of Mₙ(K) is inner (conjugation by an invertible matrix). Uses an elementary matrix units approach (no Artin-Wedderburn theory needed). Defines inner automorphisms, proves they form a subgroup, and proves the main theorem with all helper lemmas fully verified. Also derives Aut_K(Mₙ(K)) ≅ PGLₙ(K), proves Center(Mₙ(K)) = K·I, and establishes the conjugation kernel theorem. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Counterexample: Same Minpoly and Charpoly, Not Similar
description: A concrete counterexample to the converse of similarity invariance: two 4x4 nilpotent matrices (Jordan types [2,2] and [2,1,1]) share the same minimal polynomial X^2 and characteristic polynomial X^4, yet are not similar. Non-similarity is proved by showing any intertwining matrix has determinant zero.

title: Rational Canonical Form: Similarity Invariance
description: Proves similarity invariance of characteristic and minimal polynomials using Mathlib, defines invariant factor data and companion matrix properties, and provides a detailed gap analysis showing ~1800 lines are needed for full Rational Canonical Form formalization with Smith normal form as the main missing ingredient.

title: Computational Complexity of Finding the Minimal Polynomial
description: Formalizes the Krylov method for computing the minimal polynomial of a matrix: the sequence v, Mv, M²v, ... becomes linearly dependent within deg(μ_M) ≤ n steps, giving an O(n³) algorithm. Proves the Krylov recurrence, annihilation theorem, and dimension bounds.

title: Nonderogatory Matrices and Cyclic Vectors
description: Characterizes nonderogatory matrices (where minimal polynomial = characteristic polynomial) via cyclic vectors. Proves the forward direction: if M has a cyclic vector v (so {v, Mv, ..., M^{n-1}v} is a basis), then M is nonderogatory. Axiomatizes the converse. Proves equivalent characterizations via natDegree and algebraic dimension. 8 theorems, 1 axiom.

title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction in General K-Algebras
description: Formalizes modular reduction via the minimal polynomial in general K-algebras: evaluating f at x equals evaluating f mod minpoly(x). Also proves base change behavior in algebra towers K ⊂ L ⊂ A, showing degree can only decrease when extending the base field.

title: Nonderogatory Matrices Have Cyclic Vectors (Infinite Fields)
description: Over an infinite field K, if M ∈ M_n(K) is nonderogatory (minpoly = charpoly), then M has a cyclic vector. Proved via union avoidance over irreducible factor kernels, with GCD/Bezout annihilation and normalizedFactors from UniqueFactorizationMonoid.

title: Nonderogatory → Cyclic Vector (Finite Field Version)
description: Weakens the infinite field hypothesis to |K| > n: over a field K with |K| > n, every nonderogatory matrix has a cyclic vector. Uses a finite version of the union avoidance lemma.

title: Cyclic Vectors Have Full Lebesgue Measure
description: For a nonderogatory matrix M over the reals, the set of non-cyclic vectors has Lebesgue measure zero. The non-cyclic vectors lie in a finite union of proper subspaces (cofactor kernels), each of which is null by Mathlib's addHaar_submodule. Thus almost every vector is cyclic.

title: Nonderogatory Operators via Module Theory (Infinite-Dimensional Extension)
description: Extends the nonderogatory/cyclic vector theory from finite-dimensional matrices to arbitrary K-modules. A linear endomorphism T on V makes V into a K[X]-module; T is nonderogatory exactly when V is cyclic as K[X]-module. Includes a complete infinite-dimensional example: multiplication by X on K[X].

title: Nonderogatory → Cyclic Vector: The General Case (All Fields)
description: The nonderogatory → cyclic vector theorem holds for ALL fields, including finite fields F_q with q ≤ n where union avoidance fails. Demonstrates F_2 counterexample to union avoidance and develops the module-theoretic approach via annihilator polynomials and GCD Bezout.

title: Minimal Polynomial Degree and Field Extension Degree
description: Formalizes the relationship between [L:K] and the minimal polynomial degree: deg(minpoly K x) = finrank K K(x), deg(minpoly K x) | [L:K], tower decomposition, degree drop bounds, and characterization of when the degree is preserved.

title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction and Annihilator Theory
description: Proves that any polynomial function of a matrix can be reduced modulo the minimal polynomial: aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly K M). Shows the minimal polynomial generates the annihilator ideal and gives the sharpest degree bound. Compares minpoly vs charpoly reduction: minpoly is at least as tight. Proves the nonderogatory characterization: minpoly = charpoly iff charpoly generates the annihilator ideal. 30 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Computing Matrix Functions via Cayley-Hamilton Reduction
description: Proves that any polynomial function of a matrix reduces modulo the characteristic polynomial: aeval A p = aeval A (p mod charpoly(A)). The reduced polynomial has degree < n, enabling efficient matrix function computation. Proves power reduction (A^k as linear combination of I,...,A^{n-1}), polynomial congruence (same remainder → same matrix value), and partial sum reduction. Foundation for computing matrix exponentials e^{tA}. 20 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Matrix Function Reduction via Cayley-Hamilton
description: Any polynomial function of an n×n matrix A reduces to a polynomial of degree at most n-1: aeval A p = aeval A (p mod charpoly(A)). This enables efficient computation of matrix powers, exponentials, and other matrix functions.

title: Efficient Cayley-Hamilton Reduction for Sparse Matrices
description: The Cayley-Hamilton reduction is computationally efficient for structured sparse matrices: upper triangular matrices have charpoly = ∏(X - diagonal), block triangular matrices decompose into independent reductions, and nilpotent matrices have bounded polynomial basis.

title: Minimal Polynomial vs Characteristic Polynomial Reduction
description: Formalizes the relationship between reducing polynomials mod the minimal vs characteristic polynomial of a matrix, proving minpoly divides charpoly, degree comparisons, and introducing non-derogatory matrices.

title: Rational Canonical Form: Companion Matrix
description: Companion matrix definition and properties — the building block of rational canonical form (Frobenius normal form).

title: Central Limit Theorem
description: The sum of a large number of independent random variables converges to a normal distribution. This proof combines the classical characteristic function approach with an algebraic topological interpretation of the Gaussian as an attractor.

title: What Happens When Variance is Infinite?
description: When a distribution has infinite variance, the classical Central Limit Theorem fails—but a generalized version holds. This proof formalizes α-stable characteristic functions and proves the key stability property: exp(-|t|^α) satisfies [φ(t/n^(1/α))]^n = φ(t), showing that Cauchy (α=1), Lévy (α=1/2), and all α-stable distributions remain stable under the correct normalization.

title: The Gnedenko-Kolmogorov Domain of Attraction Theorem
description: When does the Central Limit Theorem generalize beyond finite variance? The Gnedenko-Kolmogorov theorem gives a complete characterization: a distribution lies in the domain of attraction of an α-stable law if and only if its tails are regularly varying with index -α. This file formalizes slowly varying functions, regular variation, the tail balance condition, and states the full forward, converse, and Gaussian cases of the theorem.

title: Lévy-Khintchine Representation: Triplets, Decomposition, and Classification
description: Formalizes the Lévy-Khintchine representation framework for infinitely divisible distributions. Defines Lévy triplets (γ, σ², ν), proves Gaussian and Poisson distributions are infinitely divisible with explicit triplets, establishes componentwise addition of triplets under independent sums, defines the Lévy-Itô decomposition, and proves classification theorems (no jumps → Gaussian, no Gaussian → compound Poisson). Connects to α-stable characteristic functions from OQ01.

title: Free Probability and Stable Distributions
description: Formalizes the algebraic framework for free probability theory: NCProbSpace structure, variance, free independence (simplified), and stability index classification. Documents the Bercovici-Pata bijection between classical and free stable distributions and provides a rigorous gap analysis showing ~3900 lines of new Mathlib infrastructure (R-transform, free convolution, free cumulants) are needed for the full theory.
