description: How many distinct common differences can occur in three-term APs within an n-element set? Conjectured O(n^{3/2}). Best bounds: n^{1.778} (Lemm) to n^{11/6} (Katz–Tao). Equivalent to Bourgain's sums-differences problem.

title: Common Differences in k-Term Arithmetic Progressions
description: Generalizes Erdős #1097 from 3-term to k-term APs. Defines D_k(A) and proves anti-monotonicity in k, containment D_k ⊆ D_3 for k ≥ 3, symmetry, and the O(n²) upper bound. Asks for the growth exponent α(k).

title: Non-Commuting Graphs of Groups
description: If the non-commuting graph Γ(G) has no infinite clique, is there a finite bound on clique sizes? YES (Neumann 1976). Equivalent to Z(G) having finite index.

title: Groups with Small Clique Number in the Non-Commuting Graph
description: Characterizes groups with small clique number ω in the non-commuting graph Γ(G). Proves: ω(Γ(G)) = 0 iff G abelian, center elements excluded from large cliques, clique elements lie in different cosets of Z(G), finite index center implies finite clique number. All theorems fully proved (0 sorries, 0 axioms).

title: Erdős #1098 OQ-01-OQ-01: Groups with Non-Commuting Graph Clique Number 3
description: Characterizes groups with clique number ω(Γ(G)) = 3 in the non-commuting graph. Proves necessary conditions: any 3-clique forces [G:Z(G)] ≥ 4 and G non-abelian. Shows S₃ achieves ω = 3 (the 3 transpositions pairwise non-commute). The proof that clique elements lie in distinct Z(G)-cosets is fully proved; the index lower bound and S₃ witness are axiomatized.

title: Commutativity Degree and the Non-Commuting Graph
description: Formalizes the commutativity degree (commuting probability) of finite groups and its relationship to the non-commuting graph. Proves commProb G ≤ 1 with equality iff G is abelian, and states Gustafson's 5/8 theorem as a formalization goal.

title: Erdős Problem #1099: Divisor Ratio Sum Boundedness
description: For α > 1, is liminf h_α(n) bounded, where h_α(n) = Σ((d_{i+1}/dᵢ) - 1)^α over consecutive divisors? YES, proved by Vose (1984).

title: Erdős Problem #11: Squarefree + Power of 2
description: Is every odd n > 1 the sum of a squarefree number and a power of 2? OPEN problem with deep connections to Wieferich primes. Verified up to 2^50.

title: Erdős Problem #110: Chromatic Number Growth in Uncountable Graphs
description: Is there F(n) such that every ℵ₁-chromatic graph has an n-chromatic subgraph on ≤F(n) vertices? DISPROVED by Lambie-Hanson (2020) in ZFC. Earlier, Shelah showed consistency of a negative answer.

title: EHS Conjecture at Higher Cardinals: Failure at All Successor Alephs
description: Generalizes the Erdős-Hajnal-Szemerédi conjecture to arbitrary uncountable cardinals and proves it fails at every successor aleph ℵ_{α+1}. The limit cardinal case remains open. Extends the Lambie-Hanson (2020) disproof of Erdős Problem #110 via Todorcevic's walks on ordinals framework.

title: Erdős Problem #1100: Coprime Consecutive Divisors
description: Let 1 = d₁ < d₂ < ... < d_τ(n) = n be the divisors of n. Define τ⊥(n) as the count of indices i where gcd(dᵢ, dᵢ₊₁) = 1. Three questions: (1) Does τ⊥(n)/ω(n) → ∞ for almost all n? (2) Is τ⊥(n) < exp((log n)^o(1)) for all n? (3) For squarefree n with ω(n) = k, what is g(k) = max τ⊥(n)?

title: Erdős Problem #1101: Good Sequences and Gaps in Sieved Integers
description: Given a pairwise coprime sequence u with convergent reciprocal series, when do the integers not divisible by any uᵢ have gaps bounded by the product formula?

title: Erdős Problem #1102: Squarefree Properties P and Q
description: How fast must sequences with squarefree properties P or Q grow? van Doorn-Tao (2025) resolved this: P-sequences have density 0, Q-sequences have upper density at most 6/π².

title: Squarefree Sumsets
description: For an infinite A ⊆ ℕ with every a+b squarefree, how fast must A grow? Erdős conjectured exponential growth is necessary. van Doorn–Tao (2025) proved bounds: a_j > 0.24·j^{4/3} and a_j < exp(5j/log j).

title: Erdős Problem #1104: Maximum Chromatic Number of Triangle-Free Graphs
description: Let f(n) = max χ(G) over triangle-free graphs on n vertices. Estimate f(n). Known: f(n) = Θ(√(n/log n)). Exact constant open. Lower: Hefty–Horn–King–Pfender (2025). Upper: Davies–Illingworth (2022).

title: Erdős Problem #1105: Anti-Ramsey Numbers for Cycles and Paths
description: Determine exact formulas for the anti-Ramsey numbers AR(n, C_k) and AR(n, P_k), where AR(n,G) is the maximum number of colors in a rainbow-G-free edge-coloring of K_n.

title: Erdős #1106: Prime Factors of Partition Products
description: Let F(n) count distinct prime factors of ∏_{k=1}^n p(k) where p(k) is the partition function. Does F(n) → ∞? Is F(n) > n eventually? The first is proved; the second remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #1107: Sums of r-Powerful Numbers
description: Is every sufficiently large integer expressible as the sum of at most r+1 many r-powerful numbers?

title: Erdős Problem #1108: Factorial Sums and Perfect Powers
description: Does the set of finite sums of distinct factorials contain only finitely many k-th powers (for k >= 2)? Does it contain only finitely many powerful numbers?

title: Erdős Problem #1109: Squarefree Sumsets
description: Let f(N) be the max size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with A+A squarefree. Is f(N) ≤ N^{o(1)} or (log N)^{O(1)}? Current bounds: (log log N)(log N)² ≪ f(N) ≪ N^{11/15+o(1)}. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #111: Edge Deletion to Bipartiteness for Large Chromatic Graphs
description: For graphs with chromatic number ℵ₁, does the ratio h_G(n)/n tend to infinity, where h_G(n) measures edges needed to make n-vertex subgraphs bipartite?

title: Erdős Problem #1110: Representability by Sums of p^k q^l
description: For coprime p > q ≥ 2, when can integers be represented as sums of p^k q^l where no term divides another? The {2,3} case has all positive integers representable; other cases have infinitely many exceptions.

title: Erdős Problem #1111: Anticomplete High-Chromatic Subgraphs
description: For t, c ≥ 1, find d(t, c): minimal d such that any graph with χ(G) ≥ d and ω(G) < t has anticomplete sets A, B with χ(A) ≥ χ(B) ≥ c. Known: d(2,2)=2, d(3,2)=4, d(4,2)=5. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #1112: k-fold Sumsets Avoiding Lacunary Sequences
description: For k ≥ 3 and gap bounds d₁ < d₂, does there exist r such that for any r-lacunary sequence B, there exists A with bounded gaps where the k-fold sumset kA avoids B?

title: Erdos Problem #1113: Sierpinski Numbers Without Covering Sets
description: Are there Sierpinski numbers with no finite covering set? OPEN. Izotov's candidate m = 734110615000775^4 is conjectured uncovered. If NO, infinitely many Fermat primes would exist.

title: Erdős Problem #1114: Monotonicity of Critical Point Gaps
description: For a polynomial with all real roots in arithmetic progression, the gaps between consecutive critical points of its derivative increase monotonically from the midpoint outward.

title: Erdős Problem #1115: Path Length for Entire Functions
description: For finite-order entire functions f(z), can we find a path Γ to infinity with ℓ(r) ≪ r? DISPROVED by Gol'dberg-Eremenko (1979). Hayman showed YES if log M(r) ≪ (log r)², but counterexamples exist for any faster growth.

title: Erdős Problem #1116: Extreme Value Distribution of Entire Functions
description: Does there exist an entire function f such that for every a ≠ b, lim sup n(r,a)/n(r,b) = ∞? YES - proved by Gol'dberg (1978) and Toppila (1976) who constructed such functions.

title: Erdős Problem #1117: Maximum Modulus Points on Circles
description: For a non-monomial entire f, let ν(r) count maximum modulus points on |z|=r. Can lim sup ν(r) = ∞? YES (Herzog–Piranian 1968). Can lim inf ν(r) = ∞? OPEN. Approximate answer by Glücksam–Pardo-Simón (2024).

title: Erdős Problem #1118: Entire Functions with Finite Measure Superlevel Sets
description: For entire f with |{z:|f(z)|>c}| finite: (1) What is minimum growth? (2) Must smaller c' work? SOLVED: Camera-Gol'dberg 1977-79.

title: Superlevel Sets in Several Complex Variables
description: Higher-dimensional analogue of Erdős 1118: superlevel sets of holomorphic maps ℂⁿ → ℂ. Plurisubharmonicity, Oka theory, Hartogs extension.

title: Erdős Problem #1119: Families of Entire Functions with Cardinal Constraints
description: If a family of entire functions has at most 𝔪 distinct values at each point, must the family have cardinality ≤ 𝔪? Answer: YES if 𝔪⁺ < 𝔠, INDEPENDENT of ZFC if 𝔪⁺ = 𝔠.

title: Erdős Problem #112: Directed Ramsey — Independent Sets vs Transitive Tournaments
description: Determine k(n,m): the minimum vertices guaranteeing an independent set of size n or a transitive tournament of size m in any directed graph. Known: R(n,m) ≤ k(n,m) ≤ R(n,m,m). Open.

title: Erdős Problem #1120: Shortest Path in Polynomial Sublevel Sets
description: For monic f of degree n with roots in the unit disk, what is the shortest path in {|f(z)| ≤ 1} from 0 to |z| = 1? Conjectured to grow to infinity with n.

title: Erdős Problem #1121: Circle Covering Theorem
description: If circles C₁,...,Cₙ with radii r₁,...,rₙ have no separating line, they can be covered by a circle of radius Σrᵢ. Proved by Goodman-Goodman (1945), generalizes to higher dimensions.

title: Erdős Problem #1122: Additive Functions and Monotonicity Defects
description: Let f: ℕ → ℝ be additive. If the set A = {n : f(n+1) < f(n)} has |A ∩ [1,X]| = o(X), must f(n) = c·log(n)?

title: Erdős Problem #1123: Boolean Algebras Modulo Density Zero Sets
description: Are B₁ = P(ℕ)/I₁ and B₂ = P(ℕ)/I₂ isomorphic, where I₁, I₂ are the density-zero and log-density-zero ideals? Set-theoretically dependent: YES under CH (Just-Krawczyk 1984).

title: Erdős Problem #1124: Tarski's Circle-Squaring Problem
description: Can a circle and square of equal area be decomposed into finitely many congruent pieces? SOLVED by Laczkovich (1990): YES, using translations only with approximately 10^50 pieces.

title: How Few Pieces to Square a Circle?
description: Laczkovich proved that a circle and square of equal area can be decomposed into ~10^50 translation-congruent pieces. But how few pieces actually suffice? This file formalizes the minimum piece count problem, proves 0-piece and 1-piece impossibility (the latter via a diagonal argument and π > 3), proves transitivity of translation congruence, and states the known bounds: at least 3 (topological obstruction) and at most 10^50 (Laczkovich) or 10^5 (Marks-Unger, with Borel pieces).

title: Erdős Problem #1125: Kemperman's Inequality and Monotonicity
description: If f : ℝ → ℝ satisfies 2f(x) ≤ f(x+h) + f(x+2h) for all x and h > 0, must f be monotonic? Laczkovich (1984) proved YES unconditionally.

title: Erdős Problem #1126: Almost Additive Functions
description: If f(x+y) = f(x) + f(y) for almost all x,y ∈ ℝ, then there exists g with g(x+y) = g(x) + g(y) for ALL x,y and f = g a.e. Proved by de Bruijn (1966) and Jurkat (1965).

title: Extending de Bruijn-Jurkat to Other Functional Equations
description: Can the de Bruijn-Jurkat theorem (almost additive → additive a.e.) be extended to multiplicative, Jensen, and derivation functional equations? We formalize the extensions and prove key structural connections.

title: Decomposing ℝⁿ into Sets with Distinct Distances
description: Can ℝⁿ be decomposed into countably many sets where all pairwise distances within each set are distinct? YES assuming the Continuum Hypothesis (Erdős-Kakutani 1943 for n=1, Davies 1972 for n=2, Kunen 1987 for all n). CH is necessary.

title: Erdős Problem #1128: Monochromatic Cubes in Cardinal Products
description: Must every 2-coloring of ℵ₁ × ℵ₁ × ℵ₁ contain a countably infinite monochromatic cube? NO — disproved by Prikry-Mills (1978).

title: Erdős Problem #1129: Optimal Lagrange Interpolation Nodes
description: Which choice of interpolation nodes x₁,...,xₙ in [-1,1] minimizes the Lebesgue constant Λ = max Σ|l_k(x)|? SOLVED: Optimal nodes exist, are characterized by equal subinterval maxima, and achieve Λ ~ (2/π) log n.

title: Erdős Problem #113: Extremal Numbers and Degeneracy of Bipartite Graphs
description: The Erdős-Simonovits Conjecture (1984) claimed: for bipartite G, ex(n;G) ≪ n^{3/2} if and only if G is 2-degenerate. DISPROVED by Janzer (2023) who constructed 3-regular bipartite H with ex(n;H) ≪ n^{4/3+ε}.

title: Erdős Problem #1130: Lagrange Basis Function Sums
description: For nodes in [-1,1], is the minimum over subintervals of the max Lebesgue function at most O(log n)? PROVED: Υ ≤ (2/π) log n + O(1). De Boor–Pinkus characterized the optimal nodes.

title: Minimizing Lagrange Interpolation Basis Polynomial Integrals
description: For points x₁,...,xₙ ∈ [-1,1], what is the minimum of ∫ Σ |l_k(x)|² dx over all Lagrange basis configurations? Conjecture: min I = 2 - (1+o(1))/n. OPEN problem.

title: Lagrange Basis Variance Decomposition and Strict Lower Bound
description: Proves that the Cauchy-Schwarz bound I ≥ 2/n for Lagrange basis integrals is NEVER tight: I > 2/n strictly for n ≥ 2. Uses a variance decomposition I = 2/n + ∫variance, where the integrated variance is strictly positive by continuity and positivity at nodes.

title: Erdős Problem #1132: Lagrange Interpolation and Lebesgue Functions
description: Two open questions about Lebesgue functions Lₙ(x) for infinite node sequences: must there exist x with large Lₙ(x) infinitely often, and is the growth property satisfied almost everywhere?

title: Erdős Problem #1133: Large Polynomial Interpolation Bound
description: For any C > 0, can one always choose target values y_i in [-1,1] for sample points x_i such that any low-degree polynomial approximating most points must exceed C somewhere in [-1,1]? OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #1134: Density of Sets Closed Under Affine Maps
description: Let A ⊆ ℕ be the smallest set containing 1 and closed under x ↦ 2x+1, x ↦ 3x+1, and x ↦ 6x+1. Does A have positive lower density? Answer: NO.

title: Erdős Problem #1135: The Collatz Conjecture
description: Does every positive integer eventually reach 1 under f(n) = n/2 (even) or (3n+1)/2 (odd)? Verified up to 2^68. Tao: almost all orbits attain small values. Open. $500.

title: Erdos Problem #1136: Sum-Free Sets Avoiding Powers of Two
description: Does there exist a subset of natural numbers with density > 1/3 where no two elements sum to a power of 2? Muller proved the answer is yes with optimal density 1/2.

title: Erdős Problem #1137: Consecutive Prime Gap Products
description: Let d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n. Is it true that max_{n<x} d_n·d_{n-1} / (max_{n<x} d_n)² → 0 as x → ∞? This asks whether record-breaking prime gaps are isolated rather than consecutive.

title: Erdős Problem #1138: Primes in Short Intervals and Maximal Gaps
description: For x/2 < y < x and C > 1, if d is the maximal prime gap below x, is π(y + Cd) - π(y) ~ Cd / log y?

title: Prime Gap Bounds: Bertrand, Cramer Sublinearity, and BddAbove
description: Extends the Erdos 1138 prime gap formalization with proved bounds: prime gaps are bounded above (BddAbove via gap <= x), Bertrand's postulate gives gap <= prev_prime, maxPrimeGap <= x/2 for x >= 25, Cramer's C*(log x)^2 = o(x) sublinearity, and monotonicity. All former axioms and sorries resolved. Baker-Harman-Pintz x^0.525 bound axiomized.

title: Erdős Problem #1139: Gaps in the Almost-Prime Sequence
description: For the sequence of integers with at most 2 prime factors (primes and semiprimes), do the gaps grow faster than log k? Formalization with 16 proved theorems including enumeration via Nat.nth, gap function, structural properties, and counting bounds.

title: Erdős Problem #114: Lemniscate Length Maximization
description: For monic degree-n polynomials p(z), is the arc length of {|p(z)|=1} maximized by z^n-1? Tao (2025) proved this for large n. Solved for n=2 (Eremenko-Hayman 1999). $250 bounty. Status: OPEN (all n).

title: Explicit Bounds on Tao's Lemniscate Threshold
description: Can Tao's threshold N₀, above which zⁿ-1 uniquely maximizes lemniscate length, be made explicit? This formalization defines the threshold via Nat.find, proves finite reduction (the full conjecture reduces to checking finitely many cases in [3, N₀)), and establishes structural bounds using known results of Dolzhenko, Danchenko, Fryntov-Nazarov, and Eremenko-Hayman.

title: Verifying Lemniscate Axioms via Mathlib Complex Analysis
description: Assesses which axioms from Erdős #114 can be eliminated using Mathlib. Defines lemniscate sets properly using Polynomial.eval and complex norm (‖·‖), proves basic set-theoretic properties, and classifies axiom eliminability.

title: Erdős Problem #1140: Primes of the Form n - 2x²
description: Do infinitely many n exist such that n - 2x² is prime for all x with 2x² < n? Disproved by Epure-Gica: only finitely many n exist.

title: Erdős Problem #1141: Coprime-Square Subtraction Primes
description: Are there infinitely many n such that n - k² is prime for all k with gcd(n, k) = 1 and k² < n?

title: Erdős Problem #1142: Primes of the form n − 2^k
description: Are there infinitely many n (or any n > 105) such that n − 2^k is prime for all 1 < 2^k < n?

title: Erdős Problem #1143: Covering Intervals with Multiples of Primes
description: Estimate F_k(p₁,...,pᵤ), the minimum number of integers in any interval of k consecutive integers divisible by at least one of the primes p₁,...,pᵤ.

title: Erdős Problem #1144: Partial Sums of Random Multiplicative Functions
description: Let f be a random completely multiplicative function with f(p) ∈ {-1, 1} chosen independently for each prime p. The conjecture states that limsup |∑_{m ≤ N} f(m)| / √N = ∞ almost surely.

title: Erdős Problem #1145: The Erdős–Sárközy Conjecture on Two-Set Bases
description: If A, B ⊆ ℕ are infinite with aₙ/bₙ → 1 and A + B covers all large integers, must the two-set representation function r_{A,B}(n) be unbounded? Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #1146: Is {2^m · 3^n} an Essential Component?
description: Is the set B = {2^m · 3^n : m, n ≥ 0} an essential component? A set is essential if it strictly increases Schnirelmann density when added to any set with positive density. The 3-smooth numbers have counting function ~ C · (log N)², exactly at Ruzsa's threshold.

title: Erdős Problem #1147: Additive Basis from Diophantine Approximation
description: Is the set {n ≥ 1 : ‖αn²‖ < 1/log(n)} an additive basis of order 2 for every irrational α > 0? NO (Konieczny [Ko16b]). For almost every α, the set fails to be a basis. The result extends to any threshold ε(n) → 0.

title: Erdős Problem #1148: Representation as x² + y² - z²
description: Can every sufficiently large integer n be written as n = x² + y² - z² where max(x², y², z²) ≤ n?

title: Erdős Problem #1149: Coprimality of n and ⌊n^α⌋
description: The density of integers n where gcd(n, ⌊n^α⌋) = 1 is 6/π² for non-integer α > 0. This shows n and ⌊n^α⌋ behave as 'independent random integers' for coprimality.

title: Erdős Problem #115: Polynomial Derivatives on Connected Lemniscates
description: For a degree-n polynomial with connected lemniscate, max|p'(z)| ≤ (1/2 + o(1))n². Proved by Eremenko and Lempert; Chebyshev polynomials are extremal.

title: Rate of o(1) Correction in Lemniscate Derivatives
description: What is the exact rate of the o(1) correction in max|p'| ≤ (1/2 + o(1))n² on connected lemniscates? Formalizes the correction term, defines possible rates (O(1/n), O(1/log n), O(1/√n), O(n^{-α})), and states the open question about which rate is correct.

title: Erdős Problem #1150: Supremum of Littlewood Polynomials
description: Does there exist c > 0 such that for all large n and all ±1 coefficient polynomials of degree n, max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| > (1+c)√n? Equivalently, do ultraflat Littlewood polynomials NOT exist?

title: Erdős Problem #1151: Limit Points of Lagrange Interpolation at Chebyshev Nodes
description: For Lagrange interpolation at Chebyshev nodes, prove that for any closed set A in [-1,1], there exists a continuous function f such that A is the set of limit points of the interpolation values.

title: Erdős Problem #1153: Lebesgue Constants of Lagrange Interpolation
description: For any subinterval [a,b] of [-1,1], the maximum of the Lebesgue function λ(x) = Σ|lₖ(x)| over any n interpolation nodes exceeds (2/π - o(1))log n. Proved by Bernstein (1931) for the full interval; sharp constant 2/π established by Erdős (1961).

title: Erdős Problem #1155: Triangle Removal Process
description: Is it true that E[f(n)] ≍ n^{3/2} and f(n) ≪ n^{3/2} almost surely?

title: Triangle Removal Process: Exact Asymptotics
description: Formalizes the gap between the Bohman-Frieze-Lubetzky $n^{3/2+o(1)}$ result and Erdős's conjectured $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ for the triangle removal process on $K_n$. The triangle removal process repeatedly deletes edges of a uniformly random triangle from $K_n$ until no triangles remain; $f(n)$ counts the surviving edges. This 489-line formalization proves 20 theorems from 5 axioms (0 sorries): structural decomposition of the conjecture into independent $O$ and $\Omega$ bounds, characterization of $3/2$ as the exact critical exponent, the strict hierarchy Conjecture $\Rightarrow$ BFL $\Rightarrow$ Grable, and sufficient conditions (ratio convergence) for the full conjecture.

title: Triangle Removal: Convergence of f(n)/n^{3/2}
description: Formalizes the open question of whether the ratio $f(n)/n^{3/2}$ converges to a specific positive constant $L$ in the triangle removal process. The triangle removal process repeatedly deletes edges of a uniformly random triangle from $K_n$ until no triangles remain; $f(n)$ counts the surviving edges. BFL (2015) established $f(n) = n^{3/2+o(1)}$ a.s., and the Erdős conjecture (parent OQ-01) asks for $\Theta(n^{3/2})$ with bounded ratio. This formalization addresses the strictly stronger convergence question: does $f(n)/n^{3/2} \to L$ for some $L > 0$? Thirteen theorems establish the hierarchy (convergence $\Rightarrow$ Erdős $\Rightarrow$ BFL), limit uniqueness, sharp asymptotics $f(n) \sim L \cdot n^{3/2}$ under convergence, ε-neighborhood and limsup/liminf characterizations, and a metric Cauchy criterion for the convergence conjecture. The limit $L$ (if it exists) would be determined by the differential equations governing the BFL analysis.

title: K_r-Clique Removal Process Generalization
description: Generalizes the triangle removal process (Erdős #1155) from K_3 to K_r for arbitrary r ≥ 3. The K_r-removal process starts with K_n, repeatedly removes all edges of a uniformly random r-clique, and terminates when the graph is K_r-free. This formalization defines the generalized process, proves structural properties (exponent monotonicity, Turán bound comparisons, convergence of exponents to 2 as r → ∞), and states the natural conjecture f_r(n) ≍ n^{2-2/(r+1)} with equivalence characterizations paralleling the triangle case.

title: Erdős Problem #1157: General Extremal Numbers for r-Uniform Hypergraphs
description: Determine the extremal number f^(r)(n; k, s) for r-uniform hypergraphs. The Brown-Erdős-Sós conjecture asserts f^(t)(n; k, s) = o(n^t) when k >= (r-t)s + t + 1. Resolved for 3-uniform (Delcourt-Postle 2024). Open for r >= 4.

title: Erdős Problem #1158: Hypergraph Turán Lower Bound for K_t(r)
description: Is ex_t(n, K_t(r)) ≥ n^{t - r^{1-t} - o(1)}? The hypergraph generalization of the Zarankiewicz problem. Only known for t=2 with r=2,3.

title: Erdos Problem #1159: Bounded Blocking Sets in Projective Planes
description: Does there exist an absolute constant C such that every finite projective plane has a blocking set meeting every line in at most C points?

title: Erdős Problem #116: Measure of Polynomial Sublevel Sets
description: For a monic polynomial p with all roots in the unit disk, is |{|p(z)|<1}| ≥ n^{-O(1)}? PROVED: Krishnapur-Lundberg-Ramachandran showed |{|p(z)|<1}| ≥ c/log n, and this is tight up to log log factors.

title: Erdős Problem #1160: Group Counting Function Maximized at Powers of 2
description: Let g(n) denote the number of non-isomorphic groups of order n. Conjecture: if n ≤ 2^m then g(n) ≤ g(2^m). Powers of 2 maximize the group-counting function.

title: Erdős Problem #1161: Maximizing Permutation Count by Order
description: For permutations of [n], which cyclic orders k maximize the count of permutations having order k? SOLVED by Beker: max_k f_k(n) ~ (n-1)! and the maximizer is characterized by lcm divisibility.

title: Erdős Problem #1162: Number of Subgroups of S_n
description: Give an asymptotic formula for the number of subgroups of S_n. Pyber (1993) proved log f(n) ≍ n². Roney-Dougal-Tracey (2025) proved log f(n) = (1/16 + o(1))n². The constant 1/16 arises from elementary abelian 2-subgroups.

title: Erdős Problem #1165: Favourite Sites of Random Walks in ℤ²
description: How many sites share the maximum visit count of a 2D random walk infinitely often? Tóth (2001): at most 3. Hao-Li-Okada-Zheng (2024): exactly 3 almost surely. SOLVED.

title: Erdős Problem #1166: Most-Visited Points in Planar Random Walk
description: Is the union of most-visited sites in a planar random walk bounded by a polylogarithmic function almost surely?

title: Erdős Problem #1167: Stepping-Down Partition Relations
description: For finite r ≥ 2, infinite cardinal λ, and cardinals κ_α (for all α < γ), does 2^λ → (κ_α + 1)^{r+1}_{α < γ} imply λ → (κ_α)^r_{α < γ}? A fundamental open question in infinitary combinatorics about transferring partition properties from higher to lower exponents.

title: Erdős Problem #1168: Negative Partition Relation for ℵ_{ω+1}
description: Prove ℵ_{ω+1} ↛ (ℵ_{ω+1}, 3, …, 3)_{ℵ₀}² without GCH. Open problem in set-theoretic combinatorics at the intersection of partition calculus and pcf theory.

title: Erdős Problem #1169: Partition Relations for ω₁²
description: Does ω₁² → (ω₁², 3)² hold (in ZFC)?

title: Erdős Problem #117: Covering Groups by Abelian Subgroups
description: Estimate h(n): minimum Abelian subgroups to cover a group where every (n+1)-element subset has a commuting pair. Pyber: c₁^n < h(n) < c₂^n. Open.

title: Exponential Growth Rate of the Abelian Covering Number
description: Pyber (1987) proved c₁ⁿ ≤ h(n) ≤ c₂ⁿ for the abelian covering number. Does lim log(h(n))/n exist? If so, h(n) = Θ(cⁿ) for a single constant c. Formalizes the growth rate sequence, proves it is bounded (from Pyber), defines liminf/limsup, and states the convergence question. Connection to Fekete's lemma via submultiplicativity.

title: Erdős Problem #1170: Partition Properties of ω₂
description: Is it consistent that ω₂ → (α)²₂ for every α < ω₂? That is, can every 2-coloring of pairs from ω₂ always yield a homogeneous subset of any prescribed order type below ω₂?

title: Erdős Problem #1171: Multicolor Partition Relations for ω₁²
description: Is it true that, for all finite k < ω, ω₁² → (ω₁·ω, 3, ..., 3)²_{k+1}? That is, for any (k+1)-coloring of pairs from ω₁², must there exist either a monochromatic-0 subset of order type ω₁·ω, or a monochromatic triangle in some other color?

title: Erdős Problem #1172: Partition Relations under GCH and CH
description: Do the partition relations ω₃ → (ω₂, ω₁ + 2)² and related ordinal relations hold under GCH?

title: Erdős Problem #1173: Free Sets for Set Mappings under GCH
description: Does there exist a free set of cardinality ℵ_{ω+1}?

title: Erdős Problem #1174: Monochromatic Cliques from Edge Colorings
description: Does there exist a K₄-free graph such that every countable edge coloring contains a monochromatic triangle, and does the analogous infinite generalization hold?

title: Erdős Problem #1175: Triangle-Free Subgraphs with Large Chromatic Number
description: For each uncountable cardinal κ, does there exist λ such that every graph with χ(G) ≥ λ contains a triangle-free subgraph with χ ≥ κ? Shelah showed a negative answer is consistent with ZFC for κ = λ = ℵ₁. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #1176: Edge Coloring and Vertex Color Classes
description: For a graph G with chromatic number ℵ₁, can we edge-color with ℵ₁ colors so that in every proper countable vertex coloring, some vertex class sees all edge colors?

title: Erdos Problem #1177: Chromatic Numbers of Hypergraph Families with Forbidden Subgraphs
description: Three conjectures about F_G(kappa) = {3-uniform hypergraphs with chi = kappa avoiding G}: bounded witness size, intersection of families, and cardinal transfer of nonemptiness. All open.

title: Erdős Problem #1178: Brown-Erdős-Sós Conjecture (General Form)
description: For r ≥ 3, let d_r(e) be the minimal d such that ex_r(n, F) = o(n²), where F is the family of r-uniform hypergraphs on d vertices with e edges. Conjecture: d_r(e) = (r-2)e + 3 for all r, e ≥ 3. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #1179: Uniform Subset Sum Representations in Abelian Groups
description: Question: Estimate g_ε(N). In particular, is g_ε(N) = (1 + o_ε(1)) log₂ N?

title: Second-Order Term in Uniform Subset Sum Representations
description: What is the precise second-order term in g_ε(N)? Formalizes the correction term hierarchy (O(1) vs Θ(log log N) vs o(log N)) and proves foundational properties of representation counts in ℤ/Nℤ, including the partition identity ∑_g F_A(g) = 2^|A|, monotonicity under set growth, and coverage monotonicity. Proves erdos_renyi_decay (exponential decay of Fourier error) from the corrected fourier_error_bound axiom via geometric series arguments.

title: Erdős Problem #118: Partition Ordinals and Higher Cliques
description: Does α → (α,3)² imply α → (α,n)² for all n ≥ 3? DISPROVED by Schipperus (1999/2010) and Darby (1999). Larson's counterexample: ω^(ω²) → (ω^(ω²),3)² but ω^(ω²) ↛ (ω^(ω²),5)².

title: Erdős Problem #1181: Upper Bound on q(n, log n)
description: Let q(n,k) be the least prime not dividing ∏_{1≤i≤k}(n+i). Is there c > 0 such that q(n, ⌊log n⌋) < (1-c)(log n)² for all large n? The trivial bound gives (1+o(1))(log n)² via the primorial argument. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #1183: Monochromatic Lattice Families
description: In any 2-coloring of the subsets of {1,...,n}, there exists a monochromatic family closed under unions and intersections. How large must it be? The trivial chain bound gives ⌈(n+1)/2⌉. Erdős and Ulam had 'no plausible conjecture' for the true order of magnitude.

title: Maximum Modulus of Polynomials on the Unit Circle
description: For points z_i on the unit circle, define M_n = max_{|z|=1} |∏(z - z_i)|. Parts 1-2 (limsup M_n = ∞, M_n > n^c i.o.) are solved. Part 3 (∑M_k > n^{1+c}) remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #12: Divisibility-Free Sets
description: How large can a set A be if no element a divides the sum b+c of two larger elements? Three OPEN questions about density, sparseness, and reciprocal sums.

title: Erdős Problem #120: The Similarity Problem
description: For every infinite A ⊆ ℝ, must there exist a set E of positive Lebesgue measure containing no similar copy aA + b (a ≠ 0)?

title: Erdős Problem #121: Square-Free Products
description: Let F_k(N) be the max size of A ⊆ {1,…,N} with no k-element product a perfect square. Conjecture F_{2k+1}(N) = (1-o(1))N. DISPROVED by Tao (2024): F_k(N) ≤ (1-c_k)N for k ≥ 4.

title: Erdős Problem #122: Distribution of n + f(n) in Short Intervals
description: For which f is it true that n + f(n) concentrates in short intervals? Proved for d(n) and ω(n) by Erdős–Pomerance–Sárközy. Conjectured false for φ(n) and σ(n). OPEN.

title: Erdős #123: d-Complete Sequences
description: Is the set {a^i·b^j·c^k : i,j,k ≥ 0} d-complete for pairwise coprime a,b,c? OPEN in general; {2^k·3^l} case is SOLVED.

title: Erdős Problem #124: Complete Sequences from Digit-Restricted Sums
description: For bases 3 ≤ d₁ < ... < dᵣ with Σ1/(dᵢ-1) ≥ 1, can all large integers be written as Σcᵢaᵢ with cᵢ ∈ {0,1} and aᵢ having only digits {0,1} in base dᵢ? Q1 PROVED. Q2 open (proved for {3,4,7}).

title: Erdos Problem #124: Complete Sequences
description: The first open mathematical conjecture solved autonomously by AI: every natural number is representable using 0/1 digits across multiple bases when the reciprocal condition is met.

title: Erdős Problem #125: Positive Density of Digit-Restricted Sumsets
description: Let A = {digits 0,1 in base 3}, B = {digits 0,1 in base 4}. Does A + B have positive density? Known: |A+B ∩ [1,x]| ≫ x^{0.9777}, upper density ≤ 0.696. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #126: Distinct Prime Factors of Pairwise Sums
description: Is it true that f(n)/log(n) → ∞, where f(n) is the maximum number of distinct prime factors guaranteed in the product of all pairwise sums of an n-element set? OPEN ($250 prize).

title: Erdős Problem #127: Large Bipartite Subgraphs Beyond Edwards' Bound
description: Let f(m) be the excess beyond Edwards' bound for bipartite subgraphs of m-edge graphs. Is there a sequence mᵢ with f(mᵢ) → ∞? SOLVED: YES (Alon 1996).

title: Erdős Problem #128: Triangle-Free Graphs with Dense Subgraphs
description: If every induced subgraph on ≥ ⌊n/2⌋ vertices has > n²/50 edges, must G contain a triangle? 1/50 is best possible (C₅ blow-up). Partial: EFRS (1/16), Krivelevich (3n/5, 1/25), Razborov (27/1024). Open ($250).

title: Ramsey Numbers Avoiding Monochromatic Cliques
description: R(n;k,r) is the smallest N such that every r-coloring of K_N has n vertices with no monochromatic K_k. Erdős–Gyárfás conjecture: C₁^{n^{1/(k-1)}} < R(n;k,r) < C₂^{n^{1/(k-1)}}.

title: Erdős Problem #13: Divisibility-Free Sets
description: For A ⊆ {1,...,N} with no a,b,c where a|(b+c) and a < min(b,c), is |A| ≤ N/3 + O(1)? SOLVED by Bedert (2023). The upper third (2N/3, N] is optimal.

title: Erdős Problem #130: Integer Distance Graphs in General Position
description: Given an infinite set A ⊆ ℝ² with no 3 collinear and no 4 cocircular points, form the integer distance graph G(A). Can χ(G(A)) be infinite? Anning–Erdős shows the clique number must be finite. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #131: Non-Dividing Sets
description: Maximum size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} where no a ∈ A divides the sum of other elements. Original question (F(N) > N^{1/2-o(1)}?) resolved NO by Pham-Zakharov (2024). Exact growth rate remains open.

title: Erdős #131: Non-Dividing Sets Growth Rate
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #131: estimate F(N) = max size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} where no element divides the sum of other distinct elements. Defines IsNonDividing predicate, proves the two formulations are not equivalent (counterexample {2,4}), monotonicity of F, and derives the negative resolution: Pham-Zakharov (2024) shows F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}, answering Erdős's question negatively. 20 theorems, 6 definitions, 2 axioms.

title: Erdős Problem #132: Distance Multiplicities in Planar Point Sets
description: Given n points in ℝ², must there exist two distances that each occur at most n times? True for n=5,6 (Erdős-Fishburn 1995) and convex position (CDL 2025), but OPEN for general n≥7.

title: Erdős Problem #133: Maximum Degree in Triangle-Free Diameter-2 Graphs
description: Let f(n) be minimal such that every triangle-free graph G with n vertices and diameter 2 contains a vertex with degree ≥ f(n). Does f(n)/√n → ∞? Answer: NO, f(n) = Θ(√n).

title: Erdős Problem #134: Triangle-Free Graphs with Diameter 2
description: Can a triangle-free graph G on n vertices with max degree < n^{1/2-ε} be extended to a triangle-free diameter-2 graph by adding at most δn² edges? SOLVED: YES (Alon proved O(n^{2-ε}) edges suffice).

title: Erdős Problem #135: Four Points, Five Distances
description: If any 4 points from A ⊂ ℝ² determine at least 5 distinct distances, must A determine ≫ n² distances? DISPROVED by Tao (2024).

title: Erdős Problem #136: The Erdős-Gyárfás Function f(n,4,5)
description: Minimum colors to edge-color Kₙ so every K₄ has ≥5 colors among its 6 edges. Answer: f(n) ~ (5/6)n. Erdős-Gyárfás bounds: (5/6)(n-1) < f(n) < n. Resolved by Bennett et al. (2022).

title: Erdős Problem #137: Powerful Products of Consecutive Integers
description: For k ≥ 3, can the product of k consecutive integers ever be powerful? Conjectured: NO.

title: Van der Waerden Numbers Growth Rate
description: Erdős Problem #138 asks whether W(k)^{1/k} → ∞, where W(k) is the van der Waerden number - the minimum N such that any 2-coloring of {1,...,N} contains a monochromatic k-term arithmetic progression. This remains OPEN with a $500 prize.

title: Erdős #139: Szemerédi's Theorem
description: Szemerédi's theorem states that any subset of natural numbers with positive upper density contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. This formalization covers the equivalent density formulation: r_k(N) = o(N), where r_k(N) is the maximum size of a k-AP-free subset of {1,...,N}.

title: Unique Sums and Non-Unique Representation
description: For A ⊆ ℕ, let B be integers with exactly one representation as a+b (a≤b, a,b∈A). (a) Is |{1,...,N}\B| ≫ N^{1/2−ε}? (b) Can |{1,...,N}\B| = o(√N)? ESS: ≪ N^{1/2+ε} achievable, ≫ N^{1/3−ε} infinitely often.

title: Erdős #14: Unique Representation Sums
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #14: estimate the count U(N) of integers not uniquely representable as a sum of two elements from A ⊆ ℕ. Introduces repCount, uniqueSums, nonUniqueCount predicates. Axiomatizes Erdős's construction (U(N) << N^{1/2+ε}), Erdős-Freud finite bound, and the lower bound holding infinitely often. Proves Sidon sets have all sums unique and are sparse. 6 theorems, 13 definitions, 3 axioms.

title: Erdős Problem #140: Density of 3-AP-Free Sets
description: Let r₃(N) be the size of the largest subset of {1,...,N} with no 3-term arithmetic progression. Prove r₃(N) ≪ N/(log N)^C for every C > 0. SOLVED by Kelley-Meka (2023).

title: Erdős Problem #141: Consecutive Primes in Arithmetic Progression
description: Are there k consecutive primes in arithmetic progression for every k >= 3?

title: Erdős Problem #142: Asymptotic Formula for r_k(N)
description: Prove an asymptotic formula for r_k(N), the maximum size of a subset of {1,...,N} with no non-trivial k-term AP. The gap between Behrend's lower bound and Kelley–Meka's upper bound remains enormous even for k=3. Open ($10,000).

title: Erdős Problem #143: Sparseness of Dilation-Avoiding Sets
description: If A ⊂ (1,∞) satisfies |kx - y| ≥ 1 for all distinct x,y ∈ A and k ≥ 1, must A be sparse?

title: Erdős Problem #144: Propinquity of Divisors
description: The density of integers with two divisors d₁ < d₂ < 2d₁ equals 1. SOLVED by Maier-Tenenbaum (1984). The threshold β* = log 3 - 1 separates density 1 from density 0.

title: Erdős Problem #145: Moments of Squarefree Gaps
description: Let s₁ < s₂ < ... be the sequence of squarefree numbers. Does the limit of (1/x) ∑_{sₙ≤x} (s_{n+1} - sₙ)^α exist for all α ≥ 0?

title: Erdős Problem #146: Turán Numbers for Bipartite r-Degenerate Graphs
description: If H is bipartite and r-degenerate, is ex(n;H) ≪ n^{2-1/r}? OPEN even for r=2. Best known: n^{2-1/4r} (AKS 2003). Prize: $500.

title: Erdős Problem #147: Turán Numbers for Bipartite Graphs
description: If H is bipartite with minimum degree r, is ex(n;H) ≫ n^{2-1/(r-1)+ε}? NO, disproved by Janzer (2023) who showed ex(n;H) ≪ n^{2-2/r+ε}.

title: Erdos Problem #148: Unit Fraction Decompositions
description: Find good estimates for F(k), the count of ways to write 1 as a sum of k distinct unit fractions. Known bounds: 2^{c*k/log k} <= F(k) <= c_0^{(1/5+o(1))*2^k}.

title: Erdős Problem #149: Strong Chromatic Index Conjecture
description: Is χ'_s(G) ≤ (5/4)Δ² for all graphs G with maximum degree Δ? This asks if every graph can be strongly edge-colored using at most (5/4)Δ² colors. OPEN - best bound is 1.772Δ² (Hurley-de Joannis de Verclos-Kang 2022).

title: Erdős Problem #15: Alternating Prime Series
description: Does the alternating series Σ(-1)^n · n/p_n converge? OPEN problem, conditionally proved by Tao (2023) assuming Hardy-Littlewood.

title: Erdos Problem #150: Minimal Cuts in Graphs
description: Does the maximum number of minimal vertex cuts in an n-vertex graph satisfy c(n)^{1/n} converging to some alpha < 2? YES, proved by Bradac (2024).

title: Erdős Problem #151: Clique Transversal and Triangle-Free Independence
description: Is τ(G) ≤ n − H(n) for every n-vertex graph G, where τ is the clique transversal number and H(n) is the triangle-free independence number?

title: Erdős Problem #152: Isolated Elements in Sidon Sumsets
description: For large finite Sidon sets A, are there arbitrarily many isolated elements a ∈ A+A with a±1 ∉ A+A? Conjectured ≫ |A|² such elements. OPEN.

title: Two Isolated Elements in Sidon Sumsets
description: For a Sidon set A with |A| >= 7 and min(A) >= 1, the sumset A+A contains at least 2 isolated elements. Strengthens the pigeonhole bound of >= 1 isolated element.

title: Erdős Problem #153: Gap Variance in Sidon Sumsets
description: Let A be a finite Sidon set and A+A = {s₁ < ... < sₜ}. Is it true that (1/t) · Σ (s_{i+1} - s_i)² → ∞ as |A| → ∞? The mean squared gap in sumsets of Sidon sets should diverge. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #154: Distribution of Sidon Sumsets over Moduli
description: For Sidon sets A ⊂ {1,...,N} with |A| ~ √N, must A+A be well-distributed over all small moduli? SOLVED: YES (Lindström 1998, Kolountzakis 1999).

title: Erdős Problem #155: Slow Growth of Maximum Sidon Subsets
description: Let F(N) be the largest Sidon subset of {1,...,N}. Is F(N+k) ≤ F(N)+1 for all sufficiently large N, for every fixed k? Possibly even for k ≈ ε√N. F(N) ~ √N. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #156: Minimum Size of Maximal Sidon Sets
description: Does there exist a maximal Sidon set A ⊂ {1,...,N} of size O(N^{1/3})?

title: Erdős Problem #157: Infinite Sidon Set as Asymptotic Basis
description: Does there exist an infinite Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 3? YES (Pilatte 2023). Two theorems verified: sidon_iff_sidon_alt and powers_of_two_sidon.

title: Erdős Problem #158: B₂[g] Sets and Counting Function Growth
description: For an infinite B₂[2] set A (at most 2 representations per sum), must liminf |A ∩ {1,...,N}|/√N = 0?

title: Erdős Problem #159: Ramsey Numbers for C₄ and Complete Graphs
description: Does there exist c > 0 such that R(C₄, Kₙ) ≪ n^{2-c}? Known bounds: n^{3/2}/(log n)^{3/2} ≪ R(C₄, Kₙ) ≪ n²/(log n)².

title: Erdős Problem #16: Odd Integers Not of Form 2^k + p
description: Is the set of odd integers not of the form 2^k + p the union of an arithmetic progression and a density-0 set? DISPROVED by Chen (2023).

title: Erdős Problem #160: Rainbow-Free Colorings of Arithmetic Progressions
description: Let h(N) be the minimum colors so that every 4-AP in {1,...,N} uses ≥ 3 colors. Known: exp(c(log N)^{1/9}) ≤ h(N) ≤ N^{log3/log22+o(1)}. Close the gap. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #161: Almost Monochromatic Subsets in Hypergraph Colorings
description: Does F^(t)(n,α) have jumps as α varies from 0 to 1/2? SOLVED for t=3 by Conlon-Fox-Sudakov (2011): exactly one jump at α=0. F^(t)(n,α) measures the largest m ensuring every large subset has balanced colors.

title: Discrepancy in 2-Coloured Complete Graphs
description: For 0 < α ≤ 1/2, is F(n, α) ~ c_α log n, where F(n, α) is the largest k such that some 2-colouring of K_n has every k-vertex subgraph α-balanced?

title: Erdős Problem #163: The Burr-Erdős Conjecture
description: For d-degenerate graph H on n vertices, is R(H) = O(n)? SOLVED: YES, R(H) ≤ 2^{2^{O(d)}} · n (Lee, 2017).

title: Erdős Problem #164: Maximum Sum for Primitive Sets
description: Is the sum Σ 1/(n log n) over a primitive set A ⊆ ℕ maximized when A is the set of primes? YES — proved by Lichtman (2023).

title: Erdős Problem #165: Asymptotic Formula for R(3,k)
description: Determine the asymptotic formula for R(3,k), the Ramsey number for triangles vs independent sets. The answer is R(3,k) = Θ(k²/log k), with current best bounds (1/2 - o(1))k²/log k ≤ R(3,k) ≤ (1 + o(1))k²/log k.

title: Erdős Problem #166: Ramsey Number R(4,k) Lower Bound
description: Prove that R(4,k) >> k³/(log k)^O(1). SOLVED by Mattheus-Verstraete (2023): R(4,k) >> k³/(log k)⁴, earning the $250 Erdős prize.

title: Erdős Problem #167: Tuza's Conjecture
description: If G is a graph with at most k edge-disjoint triangles, can G be made triangle-free by removing at most 2k edges? Tuza's Conjecture (1981) remains open in general.

title: Erdős Problem #168: {n, 2n, 3n}-Free Sets
description: Let F(N) be the maximum size of a subset of {1,...,N} avoiding {n, 2n, 3n} triples. What is lim F(N)/N? Is it irrational?

title: Erdős Problem #169: Harmonic Sum of AP-Free Sets
description: For k ≥ 3, estimate f(k), the supremum of ∑ 1/n over sets lacking k-term arithmetic progressions. Is lim f(k)/log W(k) = ∞?

title: Erdős Problem #17: Cluster Primes
description: Are there infinitely many cluster primes? A prime p is a cluster prime if every even n ≤ p-3 can be expressed as a difference of primes ≤ p. First non-cluster prime: 97.

title: Erdős Problem #170: Sparse Rulers (Perfect Difference Bases)
description: Let F(N) be the minimum size of A ⊆ {0,...,N} such that every k ∈ {1,...,N} is a difference of elements in A. Find lim F(N)/√N.

title: Erdős Problem #171: Unit Distance Chromatic Number
description: What is the chromatic number χ(ℝ²) of the unit distance graph? The Hadwiger-Nelson problem. Nelson (1950): χ ≥ 4. Isbell (1950): χ ≤ 7. de Grey (2018): χ ≥ 5. Current knowledge: 5 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7.

title: Erdős Problem #172: Monochromatic Sums and Products
description: In any finite coloring of ℕ, do there exist arbitrarily large sets A with all sums and products of elements monochromatic?

title: Erdős Problem #173: Monochromatic Triangles in Plane Colorings
description: In any 2-coloring of R^2, all but at most one triangle T has a monochromatic congruent copy. Shader proved this for all right triangles. The equilateral triangle is the candidate exception.

title: Erdős Problem #174: Euclidean Ramsey Sets
description: Characterize which finite sets in ℝⁿ are Ramsey: guaranteed to contain monochromatic copies under any k-coloring of high-dimensional space. Known: Ramsey implies spherical. OPEN: Is every spherical set Ramsey?

title: Erdős Problem #175: Central Binomial Coefficient Not Squarefree
description: Show that for n ≥ 5, C(2n,n) is not squarefree. Proved by Granville-Ramaré (1996). The function f(n) = max prime power exponent satisfies (log n)^{1/4} ≪ f(n) ≪ log n.

title: Erdős Problem #176: Discrepancy of Arithmetic Progressions
description: Find bounds for N(k,ℓ), the minimal N such that any ±1 coloring of {1,...,N} has a k-AP with discrepancy ≥ ℓ. Known: N(k,1) exactly; Open: N(k,2) ≤ C^k?

title: Erdős Problem #177: Discrepancy of Arithmetic Progressions
description: Find the smallest h(d) such that there exists f: ℕ → {-1,1} with max discrepancy ≤ h(d) over all APs with difference d. Known: d^{1/2} ≤ h(d) ≤ d^{8+ε}. Status: OPEN.

title: Optimal Colorings for AP Discrepancy (Erdős #177 OQ4)
description: Formalizes coloring constructions for Erdős Problem #177 on arithmetic progression discrepancy. Proves the alternating coloring is valid and optimal for d=1 (achieving h(1)=1 exactly), the alternating coloring fails badly for d=2, and the trivial upper bound disc ≤ k for any valid coloring. States the Roth lower bound h(d) ≥ c√d, Beck's improved upper bound, and the Rudin-Shapiro simultaneous bound as axioms. 12 theorems, 8 definitions, 3 axioms.

title: Erdős Problem #178: Balancing Infinite Collections of Integer Sequences
description: Does there exist f : ℕ → {-1,1} such that the discrepancy over any d sequences is bounded independently of m? SOLVED (Beck 1981): YES, with bound O(d^(4+ε)) (Beck 2017).

title: Erdős Problem #179: Arithmetic Progression Supersaturation
description: For integers 1 ≤ k < ℓ, define F_k(N, ℓ) as the minimum number such that every set A ⊆ ℕ of size N containing at least F_k(N, ℓ) many k-term APs must contain an ℓ-term AP. Questions: Is F₃(N, 4) = o(N²)? Is lim log F₃(N, ℓ) / log N = 2 for all ℓ > 3? Answer: YES to both.

title: Erdős Problem #18: Practical Numbers
description: Is h(n!) < n^o(1), where h(m) is the minimum number of divisors of m needed to represent all integers k < m? A number m is practical if every k < m is a sum of distinct divisors of m. Prize: $250.

title: Erdős Problem #180: Turán Numbers for Graph Families
description: For a finite family F of graphs, does there exist G in F such that ex(n;G) = O(ex(n;F))? Yes for non-bipartite families by Erdős-Stone. Folklore counterexample for infinite families. OPEN.

title: Ramsey Number of the Hypercube
description: Prove R(Q_n) ≪ 2^n (Burr-Erdős). Best known: R(Q_n) ≪ 2^{(2-c)n} (Tikhomirov 2022). The conjecture says the Ramsey number is linear in the vertex count. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #182: Maximum Edges Avoiding k-Regular Subgraphs
description: For k >= 3, what is the maximum number of edges a graph on n vertices can have if it contains no k-regular subgraph? Resolved by Janzer-Sudakov (2023): the answer is Θ(n log log n).

title: Erdős Problem #183: Multicolor Triangle Ramsey Numbers
description: Determine the limit of R(3;k)^{1/k} as k approaches infinity, where R(3;k) is the minimum n such that any k-coloring of the edges of K_n contains a monochromatic triangle.

title: Graph Decomposition into Cycles and Edges
description: The Erdős-Gallai Conjecture: Any graph on n vertices can be decomposed into O(n) edge-disjoint cycles and edges. OPEN. Best known: O(n log* n) by Bucić-Montgomery (2022). Lower bound: (1+c)n from K_{3,n-3}.

title: Erdős Problem #185: Cap Sets in {0,1,2}^n
description: Is f₃(n) = o(3^n) where f₃(n) is the max cap set in {0,1,2}^n? YES - Proved via density Hales-Jewett (Furstenberg-Katznelson 1991).

title: Erdős Problem #186: Non-Averaging Sets
description: What is the maximum size of a non-averaging subset of {1,...,N}? Answer: N^(1/4+o(1)), essentially resolved by Bosznay (1989) and Pham-Zakharov (2024).

title: Erdős Problem #187: Arithmetic Progressions in 2-Colorings
description: Find optimal f(d) such that any 2-coloring of ℤ has a monochromatic AP of length f(d) with difference d for infinitely many d. Known: f(d) → ∞ (van der Waerden), f(d) ≤ (1+o(1))log₂ d (Beck). Open.

title: Erdos Problem #188: Unit Distance Colorings and Arithmetic Progressions
description: Find the smallest k such that R^2 can be red/blue colored with no red unit distances and no k-term blue AP with distance 1.

title: Erdős Problem #189: Rectangles of Every Area in Colored Planes
description: If the plane is finitely colored, must some color class contain rectangle vertices of every area? Disproved by Kovač (2023) with a 25-coloring.

title: Erdős Problem #19: Erdős-Faber-Lovász Conjecture
description: If G is an edge-disjoint union of n copies of K_n, then χ(G) = n.

title: Explicit Bounds on the EFL Threshold
description: What is the explicit threshold N₀ such that the Kang-Kelly-Kühn-Methuku-Osthus asymptotic proof of the Erdős-Faber-Lovász conjecture takes over? This formalization defines the threshold, proves the finite reduction theorem (EFL reduces to checking finitely many cases in [10, N₀)), and establishes structural bounds.

title: Erdős Problem #190: Canonical Ramsey Number for Arithmetic Progressions
description: Estimate H(k), the smallest N guaranteeing either a monochromatic or rainbow k-term arithmetic progression in every coloring of {1,...,N}.

title: Erdős Problem #191: Monochromatic Sets with Large 1/log Sum
description: For any C > 0, if n is large enough, any 2-coloring of edges of K({2,...,n}) contains monochromatic X with Σ(1/log x) ≥ C. SOLVED by Rödl (2003). Tight bound: Θ(log log log n) by Conlon-Fox-Sudakov.

title: Erdős Problem #192: Unit Vector Sequences and Abelian Squares
description: For which d must an infinite unit vector sequence in ℝᵈ contain a 3-term AP? Answer: d ≤ 3 yes, d ≥ 4 no (Keränen 1992).

title: Erdős Problem #193: Collinear Points in Lattice Walks
description: Let S ⊆ ℤ³ be a finite step set and A an infinite S-walk in ℤ³. Must A contain three collinear points? Proved for ℤ² by Gerver–Ramsey; the ℤ³ case remains open.

title: Erdos Problem #194: Chaotic Orderings and Monotone Arithmetic Progressions
description: Must any ordering of R contain a monotone k-term arithmetic progression? NO - Chaotic orderings exist that avoid all such progressions, even for k=3.

title: Erdős Problem #195: Monotone Arithmetic Progressions in Permutations
description: What is the largest k such that every permutation of ℤ must contain a monotone k-term arithmetic progression? Known: 3 ≤ k ≤ 4. The exact value is OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #196: Monotone 4-Term APs in Permutations
description: Must every permutation of ℕ contain a monotone 4-term arithmetic progression? k=3: YES (DEGS 1977). k=4: OPEN. k=5: NO (DEGS 1977). LeSaulnier–Vijay (2011) showed odd-CD 4-APs are avoidable.

title: Erdős Problem #197: Partition of ℕ Avoiding Monotone 3-AP Permutations
description: Can ℕ be partitioned into two sets, each of which can be permuted to avoid monotone 3-term arithmetic progressions? This problem remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #198: Sidon Sets and Arithmetic Progressions
description: If A ⊆ ℕ is a Sidon set, must the complement of A contain an infinite arithmetic progression? Answer: NO.

title: Erdős Problem #199: Arithmetic Progressions in Set Complements
description: If A ⊂ ℝ contains no 3-term arithmetic progression, must ℝ \ A contain an infinite arithmetic progression? NO - disproved by Baumgartner (1975) using the axiom of choice.

title: Erdős Problem #2: Covering Systems
description: Can the smallest modulus of a covering system be arbitrarily large? SOLVED: NO (Hough 2015, Balister et al. 2022).

title: Exact Maximum Minimum Modulus for Covering Systems
description: Structural theorems about the exact maximum minimum modulus M for covering systems. Proves existence, uniqueness, and the gap 42 ≤ M ≤ 616,000 from Owens' construction and Balister et al.'s bound. Characterizes the achievable set as an initial segment [0, M].

title: Erdős Problem #20: The Sunflower Conjecture
description: Is f(n,k) < c_k^n where f(n,k) is the minimum family size guaranteeing a k-sunflower? OPEN with $1,000 prize. Major progress by ALWZ (2020) and Rao (2020).

title: Erdős Problem #200: Longest Arithmetic Progression of Primes
description: Does the longest arithmetic progression of primes in {1,...,N} have length o(log N)? PNT gives an upper bound of (1+o(1))·log N. Green-Tao proved primes contain arbitrarily long APs. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #201: Arithmetic Progressions in Integer Sets
description: Let G_k(N) be the minimum AP-free subset size guaranteed in any N-element integer set, and R_k(N) the maximum AP-free subset of {1,…,N}. Is lim R_3(N)/G_3(N) = 1?

title: Erdős #202: Disjoint Covering Systems
description: How many disjoint congruence classes can have moduli bounded by N? Bounds involve L(N) = exp(√(log N · log log N)).

title: Erdos Problem #203: Covering Systems and Prime Avoidance
description: Is there an integer m >= 1 with (m, 6) = 1 such that none of 2^k * 3^l * m + 1 are prime, for any k, l >= 0?

title: Erdős Problem #204: Disjoint Covering Systems by Divisors
description: Are there n with a covering system using divisors of n that is 'as disjoint as possible'? NO - Adenwalla (2025) proved no such n exists, confirming the Erdős-Graham conjecture.

title: Erdős Problem #205: 2^k + m with Few Prime Factors
description: Can all large n be written as 2^k + m where Ω(m) < log log m? DISPROVED by Barreto-Leeham (2026). Formalization includes Ω function properties, covering systems, and de Polignac numbers.

title: Erdős Problem #206: Eventually Greedy Egyptian Fractions
description: Are the best underapproximations by Egyptian fractions eventually constructed greedily for almost all x? Disproved by Kovač (2024): the set of eventually greedy numbers has Lebesgue measure zero.

title: Erdős Problem #207: High-Girth Steiner Triple Systems
description: For g≥2 and large admissible n, do STS(n) with girth ≥g exist? YES (Kwan-Sah-Sawhney-Simkin 2022).

title: Erdős Problem #208: Gaps Between Squarefree Numbers
description: Let s₁ < s₂ < ... be the squarefree numbers. Is it true that for any ε > 0, the gap s_{n+1} - sₙ ≪ sₙ^ε?

title: Erdős Problem #209: Gallai Triangles in Line Arrangements
description: Must every line arrangement (d ≥ 4 lines, no parallels, no 4-concurrent) have a Gallai triangle? NO, disproved by Füredi-Palásti (1984) and Escudero (2016).

title: Erdős Problem #21: Covering Intersecting Families
description: Let f(n) be the minimum size of an intersecting family of n-sets that covers all (n-1)-sets. Is f(n) = O(n)? SOLVED by Kahn (1994): YES.

title: Erdős Problem #210: Ordinary Lines
description: Let f(n) be the minimum number of ordinary lines (lines through exactly 2 points) for any n points not all collinear. Does f(n) → ∞? SOLVED: f(n) ≥ n/2 for large even n (Green-Tao, 2013) - TIGHT.

title: Erdős Problem #211: Lines Formed by Points in the Plane
description: For n points with at most n-k collinear (1≤k<n), there are Ω(kn) lines through ≥2 points. SOLVED by Beck and Szemerédi-Trotter (1983).

title: Erdős Problem #212: Rational Distance Sets in the Plane
description: Is there a dense subset of ℝ² such that all pairwise distances are rational? Conjectured NO by Ulam.

title: Erdős Problem #213: Integer Distance Sets in General Position
description: For n ≥ 4, are there n points in ℝ², no three on a line and no four on a circle, with all pairwise distances integers?

title: Erdős Problem #214: Unit Distance Free Sets and Unit Squares
description: If S ⊂ ℝ² has no two points at distance 1 apart, must the complement contain four points forming a unit square? YES (Juhász, 1979). More generally, the complement contains a congruent copy of any 4-point set.

title: Erdős #215: The Steinhaus Lattice Point Problem
description: Does there exist S ⊆ ℝ² such that every congruent copy of S contains exactly one integer lattice point? Surprisingly YES, proved by Jackson-Mauldin (2002) using the Axiom of Choice.

title: Erdős Problem #216: Empty Convex Polygons
description: Let g(k) be the smallest integer such that any g(k) points in ℝ² contains an empty convex k-gon. Does g(k) exist? PARTIALLY SOLVED: g(k) exists iff k ≤ 6, with g(3)=3, g(4)=5, g(5)=10, g(6)=30 (Heule-Scheucher 2024). For k ≥ 7, Horton sets prove g(k) does not exist.

title: Erdős Problem #217: Point Configurations with Distance Multiplicities
description: For which n are there n points in R² in general position with n-1 distinct distances where the i-th distance appears exactly i times? OPEN. Known for n ≤ 8 (Pomerance, Palásti), conjectured impossible for large n.

title: Erdős Problem #218: Prime Gap Densities
description: Let d_n = p_{n+1} - p_n be the prime gap. Erdős conjectured that the sets where d_{n+1} ≥ d_n and d_{n+1} ≤ d_n each have density 1/2, and that infinitely many equal gaps d_n = d_{n+1} exist. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #219: Arbitrarily Long Arithmetic Progressions of Primes
description: Are there arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions of primes? Answer: YES (Green-Tao 2008).

title: Erdős Problem #22: Ramsey-Turán Numbers for K₄
description: Is rt(n; 4, εn) ≥ n²/8? Can K₄-free graphs have n²/8 edges with sublinear independence number? YES, proved by Fox-Loh-Zhao (2015).

title: Erdős Problem #220: Squared Gaps Between Reduced Residues
description: For reduced residues a₁ < ⋯ < a_{φ(n)} mod n, is ∑(a_{k+1}-a_k)² ≪ n²/φ(n)? Montgomery-Vaughan (1986) proved YES, with general bound for any power γ ≥ 1.

title: Erdős Problem #221: Additive Complements with Powers of 2
description: Is there a set A ⊆ ℕ with |A ∩ {1,...,N}| ≪ N/log N such that every large integer can be written as 2^k + a for some k ≥ 0 and a ∈ A? SOLVED: YES, by Ruzsa (1972) using an ingenious construction based on powers of 5.

title: Erdős Problem #222: Gaps Between Sums of Two Squares
description: Let n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ be the integers that are sums of two squares. What are the best bounds on consecutive gaps n_{k+1} - n_k? Erdős (1951) showed gaps can be Ω(log n / √(log log n)). Bambah-Chowla (1947) proved gaps are O(n^(1/4)).

title: Erdős Problem #223: Maximum Diameter Pairs (Vázsonyi's Conjecture)
description: How many pairs of points can realize the diameter in an n-point configuration? f₂(n)=n, f₃(n)=2n-2, and f_d(n)~cn² for d≥4. Fully solved by Hopf-Pannwitz (1934), Grünbaum/Heppes/Strasziewicz (1956-57), Erdős (1960), and Swanepoel (2009).

title: Erdős Problem #224: Obtuse Angles in Point Sets
description: Any 2^d + 1 points in ℝ^d contain three points forming an obtuse angle. SOLVED by Danzer-Grünbaum (1962). Hypercube is extremal.

title: L¹ Norm of Trigonometric Polynomials with Real Roots
description: If a trigonometric polynomial has all roots on the unit circle and supremum norm 1, then its L¹ norm is at most 4.

title: Erdős Problem #226: Entire Functions Preserving Rationality
description: Is there an entire non-linear function f such that x ∈ ℚ ↔ f(x) ∈ ℚ for all real x? SOLVED: YES by Barth-Schneider (1970). For any two countable dense sets A, B ⊂ ℝ, a transcendental entire function mapping A to B exists.

title: Erdős Problem #227: Maximum Term vs Maximum Modulus
description: For an entire function f = Σaₙzⁿ, if lim μ(r)/M(r) exists (where μ(r) = max|aₙrⁿ| and M(r) = max|f(z)| on |z|=r), must it be 0? DISPROVED: Clunie-Hayman showed the limit can be any λ ∈ [0, 1/2].

title: Erdős Problem #228: Flat Littlewood Polynomials
description: For all large n, does there exist a polynomial P of degree n with ±1 coefficients such that √n ≪ |P(z)| ≪ √n for all |z|=1? Answer: YES (BBMST 2019).

title: Erdős Problem #229: Zeros of Derivatives of Entire Functions
description: Given discrete sets (Sₙ) in ℂ, can we find a transcendental entire function whose derivatives vanish on each Sₙ? Answer: YES (Barth-Schneider 1972).

title: Erdős Problem #23: Triangle-Free Graphs and Bipartiteness
description: Can every triangle-free graph on 5n vertices be made bipartite by deleting at most n² edges?

title: Erdős Problem #230: Ultraflat Polynomials on the Unit Circle
description: For unimodular polynomials P(z) = Σ a_k z^k with |a_k| = 1, does max_{|z|=1} |P(z)| ≥ (1+c)√n for some c > 0? ANSWER: NO. Kahane (1980) constructed 'ultraflat' polynomials achieving (1+o(1))√n.

title: Erdős Problem #231: Abelian Squares in Strings
description: Must a string of length 2^k - 1 over k letters contain an abelian square? NO for k ≥ 4 (Keränen 1992).

title: Erdos Problem #232: Density of Unit-Distance Avoiding Sets
description: What is the maximum upper density of a measurable set in R^2 with no two points at distance 1? Is m_1 <= 1/4? SOLVED: Yes, m_1 <= 0.247 < 1/4.

title: Erdős Problem #233: Sum of Squares of Prime Gaps
description: Prove that the sum of squares of prime gaps satisfies Σ dₙ² ≪ N(log N)², where dₙ = pₙ₊₁ - pₙ is the n-th prime gap.

title: Erdős Problem #234: Density of Normalized Prime Gaps
description: For every c ≥ 0, the density f(c) of integers n for which (p_{n+1} - p_n)/log n < c exists and is a continuous function of c. Gallagher showed this holds under RH with exponential distribution. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #235: Gaps Between Coprime Integers
description: Do gaps between integers coprime to Nₖ = 2·3·...·pₖ have a limiting distribution? YES - Hooley (1965) proved f(c) = 1 - e^{-c} (exponential distribution).

title: Erdős Problem #236: Growth of Prime Plus Power Representations
description: Is it true that f(n) = o(log n), where f(n) counts solutions to n = p + 2^k with p prime? Erdős proved infinitely many n have f(n) ≫ log log n, showing the conjecture is tight if true.

title: Erdős Problem #237: Prime Plus Set Representations
description: For A ⊆ ℕ with |A ∩ [1,N]| ≫ log(N), is limsup f(n) = ∞ where f(n) counts n = p + a? YES (Chen-Ding 2022), even for infinite A.

title: Erdős Problem #238: Consecutive Primes with Large Gaps
description: For c₁, c₂ > 0, can we find > c₁·log(x) consecutive primes ≤ x with all gaps > c₂? Proved for small c₁ (Erdős); general case OPEN.

title: Erdos Problem #239: Mean of Multiplicative Plus-Minus-One Functions
description: For multiplicative f : N -> {-1, 1}, does lim (1/N) sum_{n<=N} f(n) always exist? YES, proved by Wirsing (1967), generalized by Halasz (1968).

title: Erdős Problem #24: Pentagons in Triangle-Free Graphs
description: Does every triangle-free graph on 5n vertices contain at most n^5 copies of C5? Yes! Proved independently by Grzesik (2012) and Hatami et al. (2013) using flag algebras.

title: Erdős Problem #240: Gaps Between P-Smooth Numbers
description: Is there an infinite set of primes P such that gaps between consecutive P-smooth numbers → ∞? YES - Tijdeman (1973) proved for any ε > 0, exists infinite P with gaps ≫ aᵢ^{1-ε}.

title: Erdős Problem #241: Maximum Size of B₃ Sets
description: Let f(N) be the maximum size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with all three-element sums distinct. Is f(N) ~ N^{1/3}? Bose–Chowla achieved N^{1/3}; Green's upper bound is ~1.519·N^{1/3}. OPEN ($100 prize).

title: Erdős Problem #242: The Erdős-Straus Conjecture
description: For every n >= 2, can 4/n be expressed as a sum of three unit fractions 1/x + 1/y + 1/z? Proved for all n except primes in 6 residue classes mod 840. This famous conjecture remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #243: Sylvester's Sequence Characterization
description: If a strictly increasing integer sequence has quadratic growth (aₙ/aₙ₋₁² → 1) and rational reciprocal sum, must it eventually follow the Sylvester recurrence?

title: Erdos Problem #244: Prime Plus Powers of C
description: For any real C > 1, does the set of integers of the form p + floor(C^k), for some prime p and k >= 0, have positive lower density? Originally asked to Erdos by Kalmar. Romanoff (1934) proved the answer is yes when C is a positive integer. Ding (2025) proved this holds for almost all C > 1.

title: Erdos Problem #245: Sumset Growth Ratio
description: For an infinite set A of natural numbers with zero density, the limsup of |A+A|/|A| is at least 3. Proved by Freiman (1973).

title: Erdős Problem #246: Completeness of {a^k b^l : k, l ≥ 0}
description: Let (a, b) = 1. The set {a^k b^l : k, l ≥ 0} is complete — every sufficiently large integer is a sum of distinct elements from this set. YES (Birch 1959).

title: Transcendence of Lacunary Sums
description: A problem about the transcendence of infinite series with lacunary (rapidly growing) exponents. Erdős proved transcendence under strong growth conditions, but the general conjecture remains open.

title: Erdős #247: Transcendence of Lacunary Sums
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #247: transcendence of lacunary binary sums Σ 1/2^{n_k} when the sequence n_k grows fast. Defines HasWeakGrowth (lim sup n_k/k = ∞) and HasStrongGrowth (super-polynomial). Proves 2^k satisfies strong growth. Axiomatizes Erdős's 1975 result: strong growth implies transcendence. Proves the conjecture (open general case) is implied by the axiom for factorial and 2^k sequences. 22 theorems, 7 definitions, 1 axiom.

title: Erdos Problem #248: Bounded Prime Factors of Consecutive Integers
description: Are there infinitely many n such that the number of distinct prime divisors of n+k grows at most linearly in k for all k >= 1?

title: Erdős Problem #249: Irrationality of Totient Power Sum
description: Is the sum ∑ φ(n)/2^n irrational, where φ is Euler's totient function? Status: OPEN. Formalization proves convergence, positivity, and upper bound (0 axioms).

title: Erdős Problem #25: Logarithmic Density of Congruence-Sieved Sets
description: Let n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers with associated residue classes aᵢ (mod nᵢ). Let A be the set of integers m such that for every i, either m < nᵢ or m ≢ aᵢ (mod nᵢ). Must the logarithmic density of A exist? OPEN.

title: Erdos Problem #250: Irrationality of the Sigma-Power Series
description: Is the sum Sigma sigma(n)/2^n irrational? Yes, proved by Nesterenko using modular functions.

title: Erdős Problem #251: Irrationality of Σ pₙ/2ⁿ
description: Is the sum Σ pₙ/2ⁿ irrational, where pₙ is the nth prime? This OPEN problem asks about the arithmetic nature of a beautiful constant involving primes and powers of 2.

title: Erdős #252: Irrationality of Divisor Power Sums
description: For k ≥ 1, is the infinite sum Σ σₖ(n)/n! irrational? Proved for k ≤ 4; OPEN for k ≥ 5.

title: Erdős Problem #253: Subset Sums in Arithmetic Progressions
description: If a slowly growing sequence has subset sums hitting every arithmetic progression infinitely often, must all large integers be subset sums? Disproved by Cassels.

title: Erdős Problem #254: Subset Sum Representation
description: If A ⊆ ℕ has unbounded growth in dyadic intervals and Σ{θn} = ∞ for all θ ∈ (0,1), must every sufficiently large integer be a sum of distinct elements of A? Cassels (1960) proved a related result under stronger hypotheses.

title: Erdős Problem #255: Discrepancy of Sequences in [0,1]
description: For any sequence in [0,1], must some interval have unbounded discrepancy? YES (Schmidt 1968). Discrepancy ≫ log N for almost all intervals (Tijdeman-Wagner 1980), and this is optimal.

title: Erdős Problem #256: Maxima of Products on the Unit Circle
description: Is log f(n) ≫ n^c for some c > 0, where f(n) = min over all a₁ ≤ ... ≤ aₙ of max_{|z|=1} |∏(1-z^{aᵢ})|? NO - Belov-Konyagin (1996) proved log f(n) ≪ (log n)⁴.

title: Erdős Problem #257: Irrationality of Lambert Sums
description: Is ∑_{n∈A} 1/(2^n - 1) irrational for every infinite set A? Solved for A = ℕ (Erdős 1948) and primes (Tao-Teräväinen 2025), open in general.

title: Erdős Problem #258: Irrationality of Divisor Sum Series
description: Is the sum of τ(n)/(a₁·...·aₙ) irrational for sequences with aₙ → ∞? Solved for monotone sequences by Erdős-Straus (1971).

title: Erdős Problem #259: Irrationality of Squarefree Sums
description: Is ∑_n μ(n)² · n/2^n irrational? Yes — proved by Chen and Ruzsa (1999). They showed any infinite subseries over squarefree numbers is irrational.

title: Erdős Problem #26: Thick Sequences and Behrend Sets
description: If A is a thick sequence (divergent reciprocal sum), must some shift A+k have density 1 coverage?

title: Erdős Problem #260: Irrationality of Sparse Sequence Series
description: If a₁ < a₂ < ⋯ is increasing with aₙ/n → ∞, is ∑ aₙ/2^{aₙ} necessarily irrational?

title: Erdős Problem #261: Reciprocal Power-of-Two Representations
description: Can every positive integer n be represented as n/2^n = Σ k/2^k over a set of distinct positive integers? Cusick proved infinitely many n work; the full conjecture remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #262: Irrationality Sequences
description: How slowly can an 'irrationality sequence' grow? The sequence must satisfy limsup (log₂ log₂ a_n)/n ≥ 1 (Hančl 1991). Example: 2^{2^n} works; n! fails.

title: Erdős #263: Irrationality Sequences
description: Is 2^{2^n} an irrationality sequence? Must such sequences have a_n^{1/n} → ∞? A sequence is an irrationality sequence if all perturbations give irrational reciprocal sums.

title: Erdős Problem #264: Irrationality Sequences
description: A sequence aₙ is an 'irrationality sequence' if ∑1/(aₙ+bₙ) is irrational for all bounded bₙ. Is 2ⁿ or n! such a sequence? Kovač-Tao (2024) showed 2ⁿ is not; n! remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #265: Growth Rates of Sequences with Rational Sums
description: How fast can a sequence grow if both ∑ 1/aₙ and ∑ 1/(aₙ-1) are rational?

title: Erdős Problem #266: Shifted Sums and Irrationality
description: Stolarsky conjectured that for any convergent ∑1/aₙ, some shift t makes ∑1/(aₙ+t) irrational. Kovač-Tao (2024) disproved this: some sequences give rational sums for ALL rational shifts.

title: Erdős Problem #267: Irrationality of Fibonacci Reciprocal Sums
description: If n₁ < n₂ < ... is a sequence with n_{k+1}/n_k ≥ c > 1, must Σ 1/F_{n_k} be irrational? PARTIALLY SOLVED: Special cases proved, general conjecture OPEN.

title: Erdős #268: Interior of Harmonic Subseries Points
description: For X ⊆ ℝ^d of points (Σ 1/n, Σ 1/(n+1), ...) as A ranges over infinite sets with convergent harmonic sum, does X have nonempty interior? YES for all d ≥ 1 (Kovač 2024, Kovač-Tao 2024).

title: Erdos Problem #269: LCM Series Irrationality
description: For P a finite set of primes with |P|>=2, let {a_n} be the P-smooth numbers and L_n=[a_0,...,a_{n-1}]. Is the sum 1/L_1 + 1/L_2 + ... irrational? OPEN for finite P. Solved (always irrational) for infinite P.

title: Erdős #27: Almost Covering Systems
description: Does there exist C > 1 such that ε-almost covering systems exist with moduli in [N, CN] for all ε, N? Answer: NO (disproved by FFKPY).

title: Erdős Problem #270: Irrationality of Product-Reciprocal Series
description: For f(n) → ∞, is Σ 1/((n+1)⋯(n+f(n))) always irrational? NO - any positive real α is achievable. The non-decreasing case remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #271: Stanley Sequences
description: For any n, define the greedy AP-free sequence A(n) starting 0, n. Can the aₖ be explicitly determined? How fast do they grow? Partial results exist but the general problem is OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #272: Intersection Properties of Subsets
description: Maximum number of sets A_1,...,A_t ⊆ {1,...,N} with all pairwise intersections being non-empty arithmetic progressions. Answer: t ~ N²/2. Solved by Szabó (1999).

title: Erdős Problem #273: Covering Systems with Prime-Minus-One Moduli
description: Is there a covering system all of whose moduli are of the form $p - 1$ for primes $p \geq 5$? Selfridge found one when $p \geq 3$ is allowed (using divisors of 360). The case $p \geq 5$ remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #274: Exact Coverings by Cosets (Herzog-Schönheim)
description: Can a group be exactly covered by cosets with pairwise distinct indices? NO for abelian groups (Sun 2004). OPEN in general.

title: Erdős Problem #275: Covering Congruences
description: If r congruences {aᵢ (mod nᵢ)} cover 2^r consecutive integers, they cover all integers. This bound is tight: {2^(i-1) (mod 2^i)} shows 2^r-1 doesn't suffice.

title: Erdős Problem #276: Composite Lucas Sequence Without Common Factor
description: Does there exist a Lucas sequence (a_{n+2} = a_{n+1} + a_n) with all terms composite yet no integer dividing every term? Graham (1964) gave a construction via covering congruences. The deeper question of necessity remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #277: Covering Systems and Abundancy
description: For every c > 0, does there exist n with σ(n) > cn but no covering system has all moduli dividing n? SOLVED: YES (Haight 1979).

title: Erdős Problem #278: Maximum Covering Density of Congruence Systems
description: Given moduli {n₁,...,nᵣ}, choose residues to maximize the density of covered integers. Simpson (1986) proved minimum is achieved with equal residues. Maximum density remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #279: Covering with Shifted Prime Progressions
description: For k ≥ 3, can residue classes aₚ (mod p) be chosen for all primes p so that every large integer is aₚ + tp for some prime p and t ≥ k? Even k = 3 is open.

title: Erdős Problem #28: The Erdős–Turán Conjecture on Additive Bases
description: If A ⊆ ℕ is an additive basis of order 2 (A+A covers all but finitely many integers), must the representation function r(n) be unbounded? $500 bounty. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #28: Erdős-Turán Conjecture on Additive Bases
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #28 (prize: $500): if A+A contains all sufficiently large integers, must lim sup r_A(n) = ∞? Develops representation function theory, asymptotic basis structure, density lower bounds (|A∩[0,N]| ≥ √N), and axiomatizes the known partial results (Grekos 2003: r_A≥6 infinitely often, Borwein: r_A≥8 infinitely often). 15 theorems, 2 axioms.

title: Erdős Problem #280: Covering Congruences and Sieve Methods
description: For sequences n₁ < n₂ < ⋯ with nₖ > (1+ε)k log k, Erdős conjectured the count of integers avoiding specified congruence classes is Ω(k). Disproved by Cambie's trivial counterexample: nₖ = 2^k gives count = 1.

title: Erdős Problem #281: Covering Congruences and Density
description: If a sequence of moduli has full covering (every congruence class choice leaves density-0 uncovered), must finitely many classes already achieve density < ε for every ε > 0?

title: Erdős Problem #282: Greedy Algorithm for Egyptian Fractions
description: Does the greedy Egyptian fraction algorithm terminate when x has odd denominator and A = odd integers? Fibonacci (1202): yes for A = ℕ. Erdős–Graham conjecture squares fail. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #283: Egyptian Fractions and Polynomial Values
description: Can every sufficiently large m be represented as p(n₁) + ... + p(nₖ) where the n's also form an Egyptian fraction summing to 1? Solved for p(x) = x (Graham 1963) and p(x) = x² (Alekseyev 2019). General case OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #284: Maximum First Denominator for Egyptian Fraction Representations of 1
description: The maximum first denominator f(k) in a k-term Egyptian fraction representation of 1 satisfies f(k) = (1+o(1))·k/(e-1). Solved by Croot (2001).

title: Erdős Problem #285: Egyptian Fractions Asymptotics
description: Let f(k) be the minimal largest denominator in a k-term Egyptian fraction representation of 1. Is f(k) = (1+o(1))·e/(e-1)·k? YES — proved by Martin (2000). The constant e/(e-1) ≈ 1.582 comes from harmonic series structure.

title: Erdős Problem #286: Unit Fractions in Short Intervals
description: For k ≥ 2, can 1 be expressed as a sum of k distinct unit fractions with denominators in an interval of width (e-1+o(1))k? Croot (2001) proved yes; the constant (e-1) is optimal.

title: Erdős Problem #287: Gap in Egyptian Fraction Representations of 1
description: For 1 = 1/n₁ + ⋯ + 1/nₖ with distinct integers, must max(nᵢ₊₁ - nᵢ) ≥ 3? The example 1 = 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 shows 3 is optimal. Gap ≥ 2 is proven. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #288: Integer Harmonic Sums Over Interval Pairs
description: Are there only finitely many pairs of intervals (I₁, I₂) such that Σ_{I₁} 1/n + Σ_{I₂} 1/n is a positive integer? Example: 1/3+1/4+1/5+1/6+1/20 = 1. OPEN.

title: Unit Fractions from Disjoint Intervals
description: For all sufficiently large k, do there exist k disjoint non-adjacent intervals I₁,...,Iₖ ⊂ ℕ (each of size ≥ 2) with ∑ᵢ ∑_{n ∈ Iᵢ} 1/n = 1? Hickerson–Montgomery found 5 intervals summing to 2.

title: Erdős Problem #29: Explicit Economical Additive Basis
description: Is there an explicit construction of A ⊆ ℕ such that A + A = ℕ but r_A(n) = o(n^ε) for every ε > 0? SOLVED by Jain-Pham-Sawhney-Zakharov (2024).

title: Corrected Basis Size Lower Bound
description: Corrects the false basis_size_lower_bound by using [0,N] instead of [1,N]. Proves |A ∩ [0,N]|² ≥ N+1 for any additive basis A, via a counting argument: every n ∈ {0,...,N} is a+b with a,b ∈ A ∩ [0,N], so N+1 elements in the sumset implies |A ∩ [0,N]|² ≥ N+1.

title: Erdős Problem #290: Denominator Non-Monotonicity in Harmonic Sums
description: Must there exist b > a such that adding 1/(b+1) to ∑_{a≤n≤b} 1/n decreases the reduced denominator? SOLVED: YES (van Doorn 2024) with b(a) < 4.374a.

title: Erdős Problem #291: Harmonic Number Divisibility
description: Do both gcd(a_n, L_n) = 1 and gcd(a_n, L_n) > 1 occur infinitely often, where H_n = a_n/L_n? Part 2 trivially YES; Part 1 OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #292: Egyptian Fractions Summing to 1
description: Let A be the set of n such that there exist 1 ≤ m₁ < ... < mₖ = n with Σ(1/mᵢ) = 1. Does A have density 1? YES (Martin 2000).

title: Erdős Problem #293: Missing Denominators in Egyptian Fractions
