description: Let v(k) be the smallest integer not appearing in any k-term Egyptian fraction decomposition of 1. Current bounds: e^{ck²} ≤ v(k) ≤ k·c₀^{2^k}. The enormous gap remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #294: Egyptian Fractions and the t(N) Function
description: Let t(N) be the least t with no Egyptian representation of 1 using denominators in [t,N]. Estimate t(N).

title: Erdős Problem #295: Egyptian Fractions with Large Denominators
description: Let k(N) be the smallest number of terms needed to write 1 as a sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators ≥ N. Is k(N) - (e-1)N → ∞?

title: Erdős Problem #296: Disjoint Unit Fraction Partitions
description: How many disjoint sets A₁,...,Aₖ ⊆ {1,...,N} can have Σ 1/n = 1 for each set? Erdős asked if k(N) = o(log N). Answer: NO. Hunter-Sawhney (via Bloom 2021) proved k(N) = (1-o(1))·log N.

title: Erdős Problem #297: Counting Egyptian Fraction Representations of 1
description: How many A ⊆ {1,...,N} satisfy Σ 1/n = 1? Answer: 2^{(0.91...+o(1))N}. Solved independently by three teams in 2024.

title: Erdős Problem #298: Unit Fractions from Sets of Positive Density
description: Does every set A ⊆ ℕ of positive density contain some finite S ⊂ A such that ∑_{n ∈ S} 1/n = 1? YES (Thomas Bloom, 2021). Prize: $500. A Lean 3 formalization exists at github.com/b-mehta/unit-fractions.

title: Erdős Problem #299: Bounded Gap Sequences and Unit Fractions
description: Is there an infinite sequence with bounded gaps such that no finite sum of reciprocals equals 1? The answer is NO, as proved by Bloom (2021).

title: Erdos Problem #3: Arithmetic Progressions in Large Sets
description: If A has divergent reciprocal sum, must A contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions? OPEN with $5,000 prize. Connected to Szemeredi's theorem and Green-Tao.

title: Erdős Problem #30: Sidon Sets
description: Is h(N) = N^{1/2} + O_ε(N^ε) where h(N) is the maximum Sidon set size in {1,...,N}? OPEN with $1,000 prize. Best upper bound has N^{1/4} error term.

title: Erdős Problem #300: Maximum Subsets Avoiding Unit Fraction Sum 1
description: Let A(N) be the max size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with no subset of unit fractions summing to 1. SOLVED: A(N) = (1 - 1/e + o(1))N by Liu-Sawhney (2024), disproving the Erdős-Graham conjecture.

title: Egyptian Fraction Avoidance Sets
description: Maximum subset of {1,...,N} with no 1/a = 1/b₁+...+1/bₖ using distinct elements. Lower: N/2 (half-interval). Upper: (25/28)N (van Doorn). Conjecture: f(N) = (1/2+o(1))N.

title: Erdős Problem #302: Unit Fraction Sum-Free Sets
description: Let f(N) be the largest subset of {1,...,N} with no solution to 1/a = 1/b + 1/c. Is f(N) = (1/2+o(1))N? Answer: NO. Known: 5/8 ≤ lim f(N)/N ≤ 9/10. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #303: Monochromatic Unit Fraction Solutions
description: In any finite colouring of the integers, does there exist a monochromatic solution to 1/a = 1/b + 1/c with distinct a, b, c? A Ramsey-theoretic problem solved affirmatively by Brown and Rödl (1991).

title: Erdős Problem #304: Egyptian Fractions Complexity
description: For integers 1 ≤ a < b, let N(a,b) denote the minimal number of distinct unit fractions summing to a/b. Let N(b) = max N(a,b). Erdős (1950) proved log log b ≪ N(b) ≪ log b/log log b. Vose (1985) improved to N(b) ≪ √(log b). Open: Is N(b) ≪ log log b?

title: Maximum Denominator in Egyptian Fraction Representations
description: For integers 1 ≤ a < b, let D(a,b) be the minimum maximum denominator needed to represent a/b as an Egyptian fraction. Is D(b) = max_a D(a,b) bounded by b(log b)^{1+o(1)}? Solved by Yokota (1988), improved by Liu-Sawhney (2024).

title: Erdős Problem #306: Egyptian Fractions with Semiprime Denominators
description: Can every positive rational a/b with b squarefree be expressed as an Egyptian fraction where each denominator is a product of exactly 2 distinct primes? The 2-prime case is OPEN; the 3-prime case for integers was solved by Butler, Erdős, and Graham (2015).

title: Erdős #307: Prime Reciprocal Products
description: Are there two finite sets of primes P, Q with (Σ 1/p)(Σ 1/q) = 1? Prime version: OPEN. Coprime version: SOLVED by Cambie with (1 + 1/5)(1/2 + 1/3) = 1.

title: Prime Reciprocal Products: Sorry Elimination
description: Eliminates sorries and axioms from Erdős 307 formalization: proves product_rigidity (was axiom), one_helps_balance, and no_two_three_solution. Documents remaining work: p-adic disjointness and computational size bound.

title: Erdős Problem #308: Representable Integers via Unit Fractions
description: What integers can be written as sums of distinct unit fractions 1/1 + 1/2 + ... with denominators ≤ N? Croot (1999) proved the representable set is contiguous and f(N) ≈ ⌊H_N⌋.

title: Erdős Problem #309: Integers as Sums of Distinct Unit Fractions
description: How many integers can be written as sums of distinct unit fractions with denominators from {1,...,N}? Answer: Θ(log N) such integers, answering Erdős's question negatively.

title: Erdős Problem #31: Additive Complements
description: For any infinite A ⊆ ℕ, there exists B with density 0 such that A + B covers all but finitely many positive integers.

title: Erdos Problem #310: Unit Fractions from Dense Subsets
description: For any dense subset A of {1,...,N}, can we find S in A such that the sum of 1/n for n in S equals a/b with bounded denominator? YES, proved by Liu-Sawhney (2024).

title: Erdős Problem #311: Minimal Deviation of Unit Fraction Sums from 1
description: Is δ(N) = e^{-(c+o(1))N} for c ∈ (0,1), where δ(N) is the minimal nonzero |1 - Σ 1/n| over A ⊆ {1,...,N}? Lower: e^{-(1+o(1))N}. Upper: exp(-cN/(log N log log N)³) (Tang). Open.

title: Erdős Problem #312: Subset Sums of Unit Fractions
description: Does there exist c > 0 such that for K > 1, every large multiset with reciprocal sum > K has a subset summing to within exp(-cK) of 1? Known: polynomial bound c/K² holds (Erdős-Graham). OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #313: Primary Pseudoperfect Numbers
description: Are there infinitely many m such that ∑ 1/p = 1 − 1/m for some set of distinct primes P? These m are called primary pseudoperfect numbers. Only 8 are known (OEIS A054377). Each m equals the product of its primes.

title: Erdős Problem #314: Harmonic Sum Error Term
description: Let m(n) be minimal with partial harmonic sum ≥ 1, and ε(n) the overshoot. Is lim inf n²ε(n) = 0? SOLVED by Lim-Steinerberger (2024): YES, with infinitely many n achieving ε(n)n² ≪ (log log n / log n)^{1/2}.

title: Erdős Problem #315: Sylvester's Sequence and the Vardi Constant
description: For Sylvester's sequence u_n with Σ 1/u_n = 1, is lim u_n^{1/2^n} = c₀ ≈ 1.264 the maximum growth rate among all such sequences? YES - proved by Kamio and Li-Tang (2025).

title: Erdős Problem #316: Partitioning Sets by Reciprocal Sums
description: Can every finite set with reciprocal sum < 2 be partitioned into two parts each with sum < 1? Answer: NO - disproved by Sándor (1997).

title: Erdős Problem #317: Signed Unit Fraction Approximations
description: Is there c > 0 such that for every n, we can find δ_k ∈ {-1,0,1} with 0 < |∑δ_k/k| < c/2^n? Also: for large n, must nonzero such sums exceed 1/lcm(1,...,n)? OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #318: Signed Unit Fractions with Zero Sum
description: Given A ⊆ ℕ and f:A→{±1}, must ∃ finite S ⊂ A with ∑f(n)/n = 0? YES for arithmetic progressions.

title: Erdős Problem #319: Maximum Irreducible Signed Unit-Fraction Sum
description: Find max |A| for A ⊆ {1,...,N} with a signing δ : A → {±1} giving Σ δ(n)/n = 0 irreducibly. Known: |A| ≥ (1−1/e+o(1))N (Adenwalla/Croot). Open.

title: Erdős Problem #32: Additive Complements of Primes
description: Is there a set A with |A ∩ [1,N]| = o((log N)²) such that every large integer is p + a for prime p and a ∈ A? Partially solved: Ruzsa proved O(ω(N)·log N) is achievable and Ω(e^γ·log N) is necessary. The $50 question of whether O(log N) is achievable remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #320: Distinct Sums of Unit Fractions
description: Estimate S(N), the number of distinct sums ∑_{n∈A} 1/n for A ⊆ {1,...,N}. OPEN - Bleicher-Erdős (1975-76) gave bounds with iterated logarithms. BGMS (2025) improved the lower bound.

title: Erdős Problem #321: Distinct Subset Sums of Unit Fractions
description: Let R(N) be the max size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with all reciprocal subset sums distinct. Bleicher–Erdős: R(N) = Θ(N/log N) up to iterated log factors. The precise correction is open.

title: Erdős Problem #322: Representations as Sums of k-th Powers
description: Does r_k(n) > n^c for infinitely many n, where r_k(n) counts representations of n as sum of k k-th powers? k=3: YES (Mahler 1936). k≥4: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #323: Sums of k-th Powers Counting Function
description: How many integers ≤ x are sums of m nonneg k-th powers? Conjectured: f_{k,k}(x) ≫ x^{1-ε} and f_{k,m}(x) ≫ x^{m/k} for m < k.

title: Distinct Polynomial Pair Sums
description: Does there exist f(x) ∈ ℤ[x] such that all sums f(a) + f(b) with a < b are distinct? Conjectured for f(x) = x⁵. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #325: Sums of Three k-th Powers
description: Let f_{k,3}(x) count integers ≤ x that are sums of three k-th powers. Is it true that f_{k,3}(x) ≫ x^{3/k} for k ≥ 3?

title: Erdős Problem #326: Additive Bases and Non-Convergent Subsequences
description: Let A be an additive basis of order 2. Must there exist a subset B which is also a basis such that the growth ratio of B has no limit?

title: Sum-Divides-Product Avoidance
description: How large can A ⊆ {1,...,N} be if a+b ∤ ab for all distinct a,b ∈ A? Equivalently, no pair has 1/a+1/b a unit fraction. Odd numbers give N/2; van Doorn shows 25/28·N is a threshold.

title: Parametrization of Sum-Divides-Product Pairs
description: Explicit parametrization of all pairs (a,b) with (a+b)|ab via coprime factorizations. Proves the construction, verifies concrete examples, shows (3,6) is the smallest such pair, and counts pairs in {1,...,N}.

title: Erdős Problem #328: Partitioning Sets with Bounded Representation Function
description: Can sets A with bounded convolution r_A ≤ C be partitioned into pieces with strictly smaller convolution? DISPROVED: NO for all C (Nešetřil-Rödl 1985).

title: Erdős Problem #329: Maximum Density of Sidon Sets
description: For a Sidon set A (where all pairwise sums are distinct), how large can limsup |A ∩ {1,...,N}| / √N be? Known bounds: 1/√2 ≤ sup ≤ 1. The exact supremum remains OPEN.

title: Erdős #33: Additive Complements of Squares
description: For sets A such that every integer is n² + a for some a ∈ A, what is the minimum possible density? Best known: liminf ≥ 4/π ≈ 1.273 and limsup ≤ 2φ^(5/2) ≈ 6.66.

title: Erdős Problem #330: Minimal Bases with Positive Density
description: Does there exist a minimal asymptotic additive basis A with positive density such that for every n ∈ A, the integers unrepresentable without n also have positive upper density? Open (Erdős–Nathanson).

title: Erdős Problem #331: Common Differences in Dense Sets
description: For A, B ⊆ ℕ with |A ∩ {1,...,N}| ≫ N^{1/2} and |B ∩ {1,...,N}| ≫ N^{1/2}, must there be infinitely many common differences a₁-a₂ = b₁-b₂ ≠ 0? DISPROVED by Ruzsa.

title: Erdős Problem #332: Difference Sets and Bounded Gaps
description: Let A ⊆ ℕ and D(A) be the set of integers occurring infinitely often as a₁ - a₂. What conditions on A ensure D(A) has bounded gaps? Positive upper density suffices (Prikry).

title: Erdős Problem #333: Sparse Sumset Bases
description: For any zero-density A ⊆ ℕ, does there exist B with A ⊆ B+B and |B ∩ [1,N]| = o(√N)? NO - Erdős-Newman (1977) Theorem 2 implies counterexamples exist, though this was overlooked.

title: Erdős Problem #334: Smooth Number Representation
description: Find the best function f(n) such that every n can be written as n = a + b where both a and b are f(n)-smooth (not divisible by any prime p > f(n)).

title: Erdős Problem #335: Density Additivity Characterization
description: Characterize A, B ⊆ ℕ with positive density satisfying d(A+B) = d(A) + d(B). Known examples use fractional part sets {n : {nθ} ∈ X} for irrational θ. Are all such pairs generated by group rotation constructions?

title: Erdős Problem #336: Additive Bases and Exact Order
description: Find lim h(r)/r² where h(r) is the maximal exact order of a basis of order r. Known: 1/3 ≤ lim ≤ 1/2. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #337: Additive Bases and Sumset Growth
description: For sparse additive bases A, is |A+A ∩ [1,N]| / |A ∩ [1,N]| → ∞? Answer: NO (Turjányi 1984). Generalized to h-fold sumsets by Ruzsa-Turjányi.

title: Erdős Problem #338: Restricted Order of Additive Bases
description: What are the necessary and sufficient conditions for an additive basis to have a restricted order? Can the restricted order be bounded in terms of the order? When does restricted order equal order?

title: Erdős Problem #339: Additive Bases and Distinct Element Sums
description: If A is a basis of order r, must sums of r DISTINCT elements have positive lower density? YES - proved by Hegyvári-Hennecart-Plagne (2003). Also: upper density is preserved.

title: Erdos Problem #34: Consecutive Sums in Permutations
description: Is S(pi) = o(n^2) for all permutations? DISPROVED - there exist permutations with S(pi) >= n^2/4.

title: Erdős Problem #340: Growth of the Greedy Sidon Sequence
description: The Mian-Chowla sequence {1,2,4,8,13,21,...} is the greedy Sidon set. Is |A ∩ [1,N]| >> N^{1/2-ε}? Known lower bound: Ω(N^{1/3}). Also: does A-A have positive density? Status: OPEN.

title: Greedy Sidon Sequence Infrastructure (Erdos Problem #340)
description: Comprehensive Sidon set library for Erdos Problem #340: defines Sidon sets, proves closure under subsets, difference injectivity, counting arguments (|diffSet| = n(n-1)/2), the pigeonhole upper bound max(A) >= n(n-1)/2, and the weak upper bound |A| <= sqrt(2N) + 1. Axiomatizes the greedy Sidon sequence and Erdos's conjecture that its growth is N^(1/2-epsilon). Imported by Erdos44Problem and Erdos44SidonLowerBound.

title: Erdős Problem #341: Dickson's Sum-Free Extension
description: Given a finite set A of positive integers, extend by always choosing the smallest integer not expressible as a sum of two previous elements. Is the difference sequence a_{m+1} - a_m eventually periodic? An old problem of Dickson.

title: Erdős Problem #342: The Ulam Sequence U(1,2)
description: In the Ulam sequence a₁=1, a₂=2, where a_{n+1} is the least integer > aₙ uniquely representable as aᵢ+aⱼ (i<j), do infinitely many twin pairs (a, a+2) occur? OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #343: Subcompleteness of Dense Multisets
description: If A ⊆ ℕ has positive lower density (|A ∩ {1,...,N}| ≫ N), must P(A) contain an infinite arithmetic progression? SOLVED: YES (Szemerédi-Vu 2006), threshold is sharp (Folkman 1966).

title: Subcomplete Sequences and Arithmetic Progressions
description: If A ⊆ ℕ has counting function |A ∩ {1,...,N}| ≫ N^{1/2}, must the subset sums P(A) contain an infinite arithmetic progression? Solved by Szemerédi-Vu (2006).

title: Erdős Problem #345: Completeness Thresholds for Power Sequences
description: Let T(n^k) be the completeness threshold for the k-th power sequence. Are there infinitely many k with T(n^k) > T(n^{k+1})? Known: T(n)=1, T(n²)=128, T(n³)=12758.

title: Erdős Problem #346: Complete Sequences and the Golden Ratio
description: If a lacunary sequence is strongly complete but fragile (removing any infinite subset destroys completeness), must a_{n+1}/a_n → φ?

title: Erdős Problem #347: Complete Sequences with Ratio Tending to 2
description: Is there a monotone integer sequence with ratio limit 2 such that every cofinite subsequence has subset sums of density 1? Solved affirmatively by ebarschkis (based on Tao-van Doorn ideas).

title: Erdős Problem #348: Robustness of Complete Sequences
description: For what values of 0 ≤ m < n is there a complete sequence that remains complete after removing any m elements but becomes incomplete after removing some n elements?

title: Erdős Problem #349: Completeness of Exponential Floor Sequences
description: For what (t,α) is ⌊tα^n⌋ a complete sequence? Conjectured for all t > 0 and 1 < α < (1+√5)/2. Whether ⌊(3/2)^n⌋ is odd/even infinitely often is unknown. Open.

title: Erdős #35: Schnirelmann Density and Additive Bases
description: If B is an additive basis of order k, does d_s(A+B) ≥ α + α(1-α)/k hold for all A? Solved affirmatively via Plünnecke's stronger inequality d_s(A+B) ≥ α^{1-1/k}.

title: Erdős Problem #350: Sum of Reciprocals of Dissociated Sets
description: If A is a finite dissociated set (all subset sums distinct) of positive integers, prove that the sum of reciprocals is less than 2. Proved by Ryavec.

title: Erdős Problem #351: Strong Completeness of Polynomial-Reciprocal Sequences
description: Is {p(n) + 1/n : n in N} strongly complete for all polynomials p(x)? General case open; solved for p(x) = x and p(x) = x².

title: Erdős Problem #352: Triangles of Area 1 in Measurable Sets
description: Is there c > 0 such that every measurable set A in R^2 with measure >= c contains a triangle of area 1? Conjectured c = 4pi/sqrt(27). Open problem.

title: Erdős Problem #353: Geometric Configurations in Sets of Infinite Measure
description: Let A ⊆ ℝ² have infinite Lebesgue measure. Must A contain vertices of an isosceles trapezoid, triangle, or right triangle of area 1? SOLVED: YES for all three (Koizumi 2025). Parallelograms can fail (Kovač 2023).

title: Erdős Problem #354: Completeness of Binary Floor Sequences
description: Let α, β > 0 with α/β irrational. Is the multiset {⌊2ᵏα⌋} ∪ {⌊2ᵏβ⌋} complete (representing all large integers)? OPEN in general.

title: Erdős Problem #355: Lacunary Sequences and Rational Representation
description: Can a lacunary sequence's reciprocal sums cover all rationals in an open interval? YES for lacunarity constant in (1,2), proved by van Doorn and Kovač (2025).

title: Erdős Problem #356: Consecutive Sums in Strictly Increasing Sequences
description: Is there c > 0 such that strictly increasing sequences a₁ < ... < aₖ ≤ n can achieve cn² distinct consecutive sums? YES, proved by Beker (2023).

title: Erdős #357: Distinct Consecutive Sums
description: Let f(n) = max k for 1 ≤ a₁ < ... < aₖ ≤ n with all consecutive sums distinct. Is f(n) = o(n)? Known: f(n) ≥ (2+o(1))√n.

title: Erdos Problem #358: Sums of Consecutive Terms
description: Does there exist an infinite sequence A such that the count of representations of n as a sum of consecutive terms tends to infinity? Or even f(n) >= 2 for all large n?

title: Erdos Problem #359: MacMahon's Prime Numbers of Measurement
description: What is the density of MacMahon's sequence where each term is the smallest integer not expressible as a sum of consecutive earlier terms? Conjectured: a_k ~ (k log k) / (log log k).

title: Erdős Problem #36: Minimum Overlap Problem
description: Erdős Problem #36: Partition $\{1,\ldots,2N\}$ into equal sets $A, B$. Minimize over all partitions the maximum overlap $\max_k |\{(a,b) \in A \times B : a - b = k\}|$. Does the limit $c = \lim M(N)/N$ exist, and what is its value? Known bounds: $0.379 < c < 0.381$. A 203-line formalization with 3 axioms. Small values M(1)..M(5) computationally verified via native_decide. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #360: Partition Sum-Free Classes
description: Determine the growth rate of f(n), the minimum number of classes to partition {1,...,n-1} so n is not a sum of distinct elements from any class. Solved: f(n) ≍ n^{1/3}(n/φ(n)) / (log n)^{1/3}(log log n)^{2/3}.

title: Erdős Problem #361: Largest Non-Representing Subsets
description: For c > 0, what is the maximum size of A ⊆ {1,...,⌊cn⌋} such that n is not a subset sum from A? Does this depend on n irregularly? Possibly Θ(√n).

title: Erdős Problem #362: Subset Sum Concentration
description: For a finite set A of size N, how many subsets can sum to a fixed value t? Sárközy-Szemerédi (1965) proved the bound 2^N / N^(3/2). With fixed cardinality, Halász (1977) proved 2^N / N². Stanley (1980) found the extremal set.

title: Erdős Problem #363: Square Products from Disjoint Intervals
description: Are there only finitely many collections of disjoint intervals I₁,...,Iₙ with |Iᵢ| ≥ 4 such that the product ∏ᵢ ∏_{m ∈ Iᵢ} m is a perfect square?

title: Erdős Problem #364: Consecutive Powerful Numbers
description: A positive integer n is powerful if p | n implies p² | n. Are there three consecutive powerful numbers? The quadruple case is impossible (proved), but the triple case remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #365: Consecutive Powerful Numbers
description: Do all pairs of consecutive powerful numbers come from Pell equations? Must one be a square? Is the count O((log x)^O(1))?

title: Erdős Problem #366: Consecutive k-Full Numbers
description: Are there any 2-full (powerful) n such that n+1 is 3-full (cubeful)? A number is k-full if every prime factor appears with multiplicity at least k. Known: (8,9) and (12167,12168) are 3-full/2-full pairs, but no 2-full/3-full pairs are known.

title: Erdős Problem #367: Products of 2-Full Parts
description: For fixed k ≥ 1, is ∏_{n ≤ m < n+k} B₂(m) ≪ n^{2+o(1)}? The strong bound ≪ n² holds for k ≤ 2 but fails for k ≥ 3 (van Doorn). OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #368: Largest Prime Factor of n(n+1)
description: Study of F(n), the largest prime factor of n(n+1). Pólya proved F(n) → ∞; Mahler showed F(n) ≫ log log n; Pasten (2024) improved to F(n) ≫ (log log n)²/(log log log n). Erdős conjectured F(n) ≈ (log n)².

title: Erdős Problem #369: Consecutive Smooth Numbers
description: For ε > 0 and k ≥ 2, does {1,…,n} contain k consecutive n^ε-smooth integers for all large n? Open even for k=2. Balog-Wooley: infinitely many exist. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #37: Essential Components and Lacunary Sets
description: Can a lacunary set A ⊂ ℕ be an essential component? NO (Ruzsa 1987). Essential components need |A ∩ {1,...,N}| ≥ (log N)^{1+c}, but lacunary sets have only O(log N) elements. Open: Is {2^m · 3^n} essential?

title: Consecutive Smooth Numbers
description: Are there infinitely many n such that both n and n+1 have their largest prime factor less than their square root? Steinerberger found an elegant solution using n = m^2 - 1.

title: Erdős #371: Density of P(n) < P(n+1)
description: Let P(n) be the largest prime factor of n. Show that {n : P(n) < P(n+1)} has density 1/2. Conditionally solved by Wang (2021); logarithmic density proved by Teräväinen (2018).

title: Erdős Problem #372: Descending Largest Prime Factors
description: Let P(n) denote the largest prime factor of n. Are there infinitely many n such that P(n) > P(n+1) > P(n+2)?

title: Erdos Problem #373: Factorials as Products of Factorials
description: Show that n! = a_1! * a_2! * ... * a_k! with n-1 > a_1 >= ... >= a_k >= 2 has only finitely many solutions. Conditionally solved under ABC conjecture (Luca 2007).

title: Erdős Problem #374: Factorial Products as Perfect Squares
description: For F(m) = min k with a₁!···aₖ! a square (a₁<···<aₖ=m), study |Dₖ∩{1,...,n}| for Dₖ = {m: F(m)=k}. D₂ = squares. Dₖ = ∅ for k>6. Min D₆ = 527. Open for 3≤k≤6.

title: Erdos Problem #375: Grimm's Conjecture on Consecutive Composites
description: For any k consecutive composites n+1,...,n+k, can we assign distinct prime divisors? Open - if true, implies strong prime gap bounds.

title: Erdős Problem #376: Central Binomial Coefficients Coprime to 105
description: Are there infinitely many n such that C(2n,n) is coprime to 105 = 3×5×7? OPEN for three primes. EGRS (1975) solved the two-prime case.

title: Erdős Problem #377: Primes Not Dividing Central Binomial
description: Is there an absolute constant C such that ∑_{p≤n, p∤C(2n,n)} 1/p ≤ C for all n? The main conjecture is OPEN, but EGRS75 proved f(n) averages to γ₀ = ∑log(k)/2^k and is ≤ c·log(log(n)) for c < 1.

title: Erdos Problem #378: Density of Squarefree Binomial Coefficients
description: Does the density of n for which C(n,k) is squarefree for at least r values of k exist and is it positive? YES to both, resolved via Granville-Ramare.

title: Erdos Problem #379: Binomial Coefficients and Prime Power Divisibility
description: Let S(n) be the largest s such that every C(n,k) for 1 <= k < n is divisible by some p^s. Is limsup S(n) = infinity?

title: Erdős #38: Essential Components and Density Boosting
description: Does there exist a set B that is NOT an additive basis but still has the density-boosting property: for any set A with Schnirelmann density α, some translate A ∪ (A+b) achieves density ≥ α + f(α)?

title: Erdős Problem #380: Bad Intervals and Greatest Prime Factors
description: An interval [u,v] is bad if the greatest prime factor of ∏m occurs with exponent > 1. Is B(x) ~ #{n ≤ x : P(n)² | n}? Erdős–Graham proved B(x) > x^{1-o(1)}.

title: Erdős Problem #381: Counting Highly Composite Numbers
description: Is Q(x) ≫_k (log x)^k for every k, where Q(x) counts highly composite numbers up to x? DISPROVED by Nicolas (1971) - Q(x) has polynomial growth in log x.

title: Erdős Problem #382: Prime Powers in Factorial Products
description: For intervals [u,v] where the largest prime dividing u(u+1)...v has exponent ≥ 2, is v−u = v^o(1)? Can v−u be arbitrarily large? Ramachandra showed v−u ≤ v^{1/2+o(1)}. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #383: Prime Divisors of Consecutive Squares
description: For every k, are there infinitely many primes p such that p is the largest prime divisor of ∏_{i=0}^k (p² + i)?

title: Erdős Problem #384: Prime Divisors of Binomial Coefficients
description: If 1 < k < n−1 then C(n,k) is divisible by a prime p < n/2. SOLVED by Ecklund (1969). The only exception is C(7,3) = 35 = 5 × 7.

title: Erdős Problem #385: Composite Numbers and Least Prime Divisors
description: Is F(n) = max{m + p(m) : m < n, m composite} greater than n for all large n, and does F(n) - n tend to infinity?

title: Erdős Problem #386: Binomial Coefficients as Products of Consecutive Primes
description: Let 2 ≤ k ≤ n − 2. Can C(n,k) be the product of consecutive primes infinitely often? Known examples include C(21,2) = 2·3·5·7, C(7,3) = 5·7, and C(15,6) = 5·7·11·13. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #387: Divisors of Binomial Coefficients Near n
description: Is there an absolute constant c > 0 such that for all 1 ≤ k < n, the binomial coefficient C(n,k) has a divisor in the interval (cn, n]?

title: Erdős Problem #388: Products of Consecutive Integers
description: Can one classify all solutions of ∏(m₁+i) = ∏(m₂+j) where k₁, k₂ > 3 and the blocks are disjoint? Erdős conjectured only finitely many solutions exist. Generalizes to proportional products a·∏(m₁+i) = b·∏(m₂+j).

title: Divisibility of Consecutive Integer Products
description: Is it true that for every n ≥ 1 there exists k such that n(n+1)···(n+k−1) divides (n+k)···(n+2k−1)? The minimal k for n = 4 is 207 (Mehta). OEIS A375071 catalogs minimal k values.

title: Erdős Problem #39: Infinite Sidon Set Growth
description: Does there exist an infinite Sidon set with counting function approaching N^{1/2}?

title: Erdős Problem #390: Factorial Factorization with Large Factors
description: Let f(n) = min m such that n! = a₁⋯aₖ with n < a₁ < ⋯ < aₖ = m. Known: f(n) - 2n ≍ n/log n (EGS 1982). Is there c with f(n) - 2n ~ c·n/log n? OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #391: Factorizing n! with Large Minimum Factor
description: Let t(n) be maximal such that n! = a₁···aₙ with t(n) = a₁ ≤ ··· ≤ aₙ. Is lim t(n)/n = 1/e? YES, proved by Alexeev-Conway-Rosenfeld-Sutherland-Tao-Uhr-Ventullo (2025).

title: Erdős Problem #392: Optimal Factorization of n!
description: Let A(n) be the minimum number of factors needed to write n! = a₁...aₜ with each aᵢ ≤ n². Then A(n) = n/2 - n/(2 log n) + o(n/log n).

title: Erdős Problem #393: Factorial Factorization Span
description: Let f(n) = minimal m such that n! = a₁·...·aₜ with a₁ < ... < aₜ = a₁ + m. Study the behavior of f(n). Known: F_m(N) = o(N), conditional f(n) → ∞.

title: Erdős Problem #394: Divisibility by Consecutive Integer Products
description: Let t_k(n) be the least m with n | m(m+1)···(m+k-1). Erdős-Hall (1978) proved Σ t₂(n) ≪ (log log log x / log log x)x². Questions about x²/(log x)^c bounds and hierarchy Σ t_{k+1} = o(Σ t_k) remain OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #395: Reverse Littlewood-Offord Problem
description: For unit complex vectors, is P(|ε₁z₁ + ... + εₙzₙ| ≤ √2) ≥ c/n? YES (HJNS 2024).

title: Optimal Constant in Reverse Littlewood-Offord
description: Structural theorems about the optimal constant c in the reverse Littlewood-Offord problem P(|sum| ≤ √2) ≥ c/n. Formalizes the critical role of the √2 threshold, monotonicity in threshold, tightness of the 1/n rate, and the counterexample exceeding threshold 1.

title: Erdős Problem #396: Descending Factorials Dividing Central Binomials
description: For every k, does there exist n such that n(n−1)⋯(n−k) divides C(2n,n)? Pomerance proved individual factors divide for infinitely many n. The full product conjecture remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #397: Products of Central Binomial Coefficients
description: Are there only finitely many solutions to products of central binomial coefficients being equal? Disproved by Somani (2026).

title: Erdős Problem #398: The Brocard-Ramanujan Conjecture
description: Are the only solutions to n! + 1 = m² when n = 4, 5, 7? This classic conjecture, dating to Brocard (1876) and Ramanujan, remains open despite computational verification to 10^9.

title: Erdős Problem #399: Factorial Diophantine Equations
description: Is it true that there are no solutions to n! = x^k ± y^k with xy > 1 and k > 2? Disproved by Barfield: 10! = 48^4 - 36^4.

title: Erdős Problem #4: Large Prime Gaps
description: Erdős Problem #4: For any $C > 0$, are there infinitely many $n$ with $p_{n+1} - p_n > C \cdot \log n \cdot \log\log n \cdot \log\log\log\log n / (\log\log\log n)^2$? SOLVED (YES) by Maynard (2016) and Ford-Green-Konyagin-Tao (2016) independently, with the combined FGKMT (2018) establishing the stronger result. This 243-line formalization axiomatizes 9 landmark results from Rankin (1938) through FGKMT (2018), defines `primeGap` and `erdosFunction` with iterated logarithms, and states the conjecture's resolution. 1 sorry remains. Erdős's $10,000 prize for gaps exceeding $(\log n)^{1+c}$ remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #40: Representation Function and Dense Sets
description: For which g(N) → ∞ does |A ∩ {1,...,N}| >> N^{1/2}/g(N) imply limsup r_A(n) = ∞? Solving for any g → ∞ implies the Erdős–Turán conjecture (Problem #28). $500 bounty. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #400: Factorial Divisibility and Sum Excess
description: For k ≥ 2, let g_k(n) = max{(a₁+⋯+aₖ)-n : a₁!⋯aₖ! | n!}. Is Σ g_k(n) ~ cₖ·x·log x? Is g_k(n) concentrated around cₖ·log x?

title: Erdős Problem #401: Factorial Divisibility with Prime Products
description: Does there exist f(r) → ∞ such that for infinitely many n, there exist a₁, a₂ with a₁ + a₂ > n + f(r)·log(n) where a₁!·a₂! | n!·2ⁿ·3ⁿ·...·pᵣⁿ? YES (Barreto-Leeham 2026). The 'for all large n' version is FALSE (Sothanaphan).

title: Graham's GCD Conjecture
description: For any finite set A ⊂ ℕ, there exist a, b ∈ A such that gcd(a, b) ≤ a/|A|. Graham's conjecture was proved by Balasubramanian and Soundararajan in 1996.

title: Erdős Problem #403: Powers of 2 as Sums of Distinct Factorials
description: Does 2^m = a₁! + a₂! + ... + aₖ! (with distinct aᵢ) have only finitely many solutions? YES - the largest is 2^7 = 2! + 3! + 5! = 128 (Lin/Frankl 1976).

title: Erdős Problem #404: Prime Power Divisibility of Factorial Sums
description: For which (a, p) is there a bound on k such that p^k divides some sum of factorials starting at a? Let f(a, p) be the supremum. Lin proved f(2, 2) ≤ 254. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #405: Factorial Plus Power Equals Prime Power
description: Let $p$ be an odd prime. The equation $(p-1)! + a^{p-1} = p^k$ has only finitely many solutions (Brindza–Erdős, 1991). Yu and Liu (1996) gave a complete resolution: the only solutions are $(p,a,k) \in \{(3,1,1), (3,5,3), (5,1,2)\}$, corresponding to $2! + 1 = 3$, $2! + 25 = 27$, and $4! + 1 = 25$.

title: Erdős Problem #406: Powers of 2 with Only Digits 0 and 1 in Base 3
description: Are there only finitely many powers of 2 whose base-3 representation uses only digits 0 and 1? Known examples: $1 = 2^0$, $4 = 2^2$, $256 = 2^8$. These are numbers simultaneously equal to a power of 2 and a sum of distinct powers of 3. Saye (2022) verified no new examples for $2^n$ with $n \leq 5.9 \times 10^{21}$.

title: Erdős Problem #407: Newman's Conjecture on 2^a + 3^b + 2^c·3^d
description: Is w(n) bounded, where w(n) counts representations n = 2^a + 3^b + 2^c·3^d? Solved: w(n) ≤ 9 always, w(n) ≤ 4 for large n (EGST 1988, Bajpai-Bennett 2024).

title: Erdős Problem #408: Iterated Totient Function
description: Does f(n)/log(n) have a distribution function, where f(n) is the number of iterations of Euler's totient needed to reach 1? EGPS (1990) proved YES conditionally on Elliott-Halberstam.

title: Totient Iteration to Primes
description: How many iterations of n mapsto phi(n) + 1 are needed before reaching a prime? F(n) = o(n) trivially; can infinitely many n reach the same prime? What is the density of n reaching a fixed prime? A problem of Finucane.

title: Erdős Problem #41: B_h Sequences and Density Bounds
description: For infinite B_3 sets (distinct triple sums), is liminf |A ∩ {1,...,N}| / N^(1/3) = 0?

title: Erdős Problem #410: Iterated Sum of Divisors Growth
description: Does lim_{k → ∞} σₖ(n)^{1/k} = ∞ for all n ≥ 2, where σₖ is the k-th iterate of the sum of divisors function?

title: Erdős Problem #411: Iterated Totient Sums and Doubling
description: Define $g(n) = n + \varphi(n)$ and let $g^k$ denote the $k$-th iterate. For which $n$ and $r$ does $g^{k+r}(n) = 2 \cdot g^k(n)$ for all large $k$? Known $r = 2$ solutions: $n = 10, 94$. Cambie found ratio-3 and ratio-4 solutions. Steinerberger (2025) reduced the $r = 2$ case to $\varphi(n) + \varphi(n + \varphi(n)) = n$. OPEN in general.

title: Erdős Problem #412: Iterated Sum of Divisors Convergence
description: Do all iterated sum-of-divisors sequences eventually meet? For every m,n ≥ 2, is there i,j such that σᵢ(m) = σⱼ(n)? Open. Selfridge provided evidence suggesting NO.

title: Erdős Problem #413: Barriers for the Omega Function
description: Are there infinitely many n such that m + ω(m) ≤ n for all m < n?

title: Erdős Problem #414: Merging Orbits of h(n) = n + τ(n)
description: Define h(n) = n + τ(n) and iterate. Do all orbits eventually merge? For any m, n ≥ 1, do there exist i, j with h^i(m) = h^j(n)? Erdős and Graham believed yes. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #415: Ordering Patterns in Euler's Totient Function
description: Let F(n) = largest k such that ALL k! ordering patterns appear in some φ(m+1),...,φ(m+k). Erdős proved F(n) ≍ log log log n. The exact constant and which pattern fails first remain OPEN.

title: Counting Totient Values
description: Let V(x) count the number of n ≤ x such that φ(m) = n is solvable. Does V(2x)/V(x) → 2? Is there an asymptotic formula for V(x)? Despite remarkable progress by Pillai, Erdős, Maier-Pomerance, and Ford, both questions remain open.

title: Erdős Problem #417: Counting Totient Values
description: Does the limit V(x)/V'(x) exist, where V'(x) counts distinct totients from inputs at most x and V(x) counts all totient values at most x?

title: Erdos Problem #418: Non-Cototients
description: Are there infinitely many positive integers not of the form n - phi(n)? Yes - integers 2^k * 509203 are non-cototients.

title: Erdős Problem #419: Limit Points of τ((n+1)!)/τ(n!)
description: What is the set of limit points of τ((n+1)!)/τ(n!)? SOLVED: The limit points are exactly {1} ∪ {1 + 1/k : k ≥ 1} = {1, 2, 3/2, 4/3, 5/4, ...}.

title: Erdős Problem #42: Sidon Sets with Disjoint Difference Sets
description: For every maximal Sidon set A ⊆ {1,...,N}, does there exist a Sidon set B of size M with (A−A) ∩ (B−B) = {0}? Proved for M ≤ 3 (Sedov). Open in general.

title: Erdős Problem #420: Divisor Function Ratios for Factorials
description: For F(f,n) = τ((n+⌊f(n)⌋)!)/τ(n!), study when F→∞ and when F is dense in (1,∞). Partially solved by EGIP96: liminf F(c log n, n) = 1 and lim F(n^{4/9}, n) = ∞.

title: Erdős Problem #421: Distinct Products in Dense Sequences
description: Is there a strictly increasing sequence d₁ < d₂ < ... with density 1 such that all interval products ∏_{u ≤ i ≤ v} d_i are distinct?

title: Erdős Problem #422: Hofstadter-Type Recursive Sequence
description: f(1)=f(2)=1, f(n) = f(n-f(n-1))+f(n-f(n-2)). Not even known if well-defined for all n. Does f miss infinitely many integers? OEIS A005185. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #423: Sums of Consecutive Terms Sequence
description: Let a₁=1, a₂=2. For k≥3, aₖ is the least integer > a_{k-1} that is a sum of at least two consecutive terms. What is the asymptotic behaviour? OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #424: Sequence Generated by a_i · a_j − 1
description: Start with {2,3}, iteratively append a_i · a_j − 1. Does the resulting set have positive density? No element ≡ 1 (mod 3) appears, so density ≤ 2/3. OEIS A005244.

title: Erdős Problem #425: Multiplicative Sidon Sets
description: Let F(n) be the maximum size of A ⊆ {1,...,n} such that all pairwise products ab (a < b) are distinct. Erdős proved π(n) + c₁·n^(3/4)·(log n)^(-3/2) ≤ F(n) ≤ π(n) + c₂·n^(3/4)·(log n)^(-3/2). The exact constant c (if it exists) is unknown. Alexander disproved the real version conjecture.

title: Erdős Problem #426: Unique Subgraphs
description: Can a graph on n vertices have ≫ 2^(n choose 2)/n! unique subgraphs? Answer: NO (Bradač-Christoph 2024). Unique subgraphs are rare.

title: Erdős Problem #427: Divisibility of Prime Sums
description: Is it true that for every n and d, there exists k such that d divides the sum p_{n+1} + ... + p_{n+k}, where p_r denotes the r-th prime? Solved by Pilatte using Shiu's theorem on strings of congruent primes.

title: Erdős Problem #428: Prime Offsets with Positive Density
description: Is there A ⊆ ℕ with liminf |A∩[1,x]|/π(x) > 0 such that for infinitely many n, all n-a are prime for a ∈ A?

title: Erdős Problem #429: Sparse Admissible Sets and Prime Shifts
description: Is sparsity + admissibility sufficient for a prime shift? Answer: NO (Weisenberg 2024 constructed arbitrarily sparse admissible sets with no prime shift).

title: Sidon Sets with Disjoint Difference Sets
description: If A, B are Sidon sets in {1,...,N} with (A-A) ∩ (B-B) = {0}, must C(|A|,2) + C(|B|,2) ≤ C(f(N),2) + O(1)? OPEN ($100).

title: Erdos Problem #430: Composite Numbers in Greedy Large-Factor Sequences
description: Define a greedy decreasing sequence in [1,n) where each term has all prime factors exceeding n minus the term. Must this sequence contain a composite for large n? Selfridge's computations suggest yes. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #431: Inverse Goldbach Problem
description: Are there two infinite sets A and B such that A + B agrees with the set of prime numbers up to finitely many exceptions? Known as Ostmann's 'inverse Goldbach problem'. The answer is conjectured to be NO.

title: Erdős Problem #432: Pairwise Coprime Sumsets
description: Let A, B ⊆ ℕ be infinite. How dense can A + B be if all elements are pairwise coprime? Asked by Straus (Erdős–Graham 1980, p.85). OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #433: Maximum Frobenius Numbers
description: For g(k,n) = max{G(A) : A ⊆ {1,...,n}, |A| = k, gcd(A) = 1}, prove that g(k,n) ~ n²/(k-1). SOLVED by Dixmier (1990) who gave precise bounds.

title: Erdős #434: Extremal Frobenius Problem
description: Which k-subset of {1,...,n} maximizes non-representable integers? Answer: {n-k+1,...,n} (Kiss 2002).

title: Erdős Problem #435: Binomial Coefficient Representation
description: For n not a prime power, the largest integer not representable as Σ c_i·C(n,i) with c_i≥0 equals Σ_k (Σ_{d≤a_k} C(n,p_k^d))·(p_k-1) - n. SOLVED by Hwang-Song (2024).

title: Erdos Problem #436: Consecutive kth Power Residues
description: For prime p and k,m >= 2, let r(k,m,p) be the minimal r such that r,...,r+m-1 are kth power residues mod p. Let Lambda(k,m) = lim sup r(k,m,p). Hildebrand (1991) proved Lambda(k,2) finite for all k. Lambda(k,3) for odd k >= 5 remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #437: Square Partial Products
description: For 1 ≤ a₁ < ... < aₖ ≤ x, how many partial products can be squares? Can there be > x^(1-ε) squares? YES, proved by Bui-Pratt-Zaharescu (2024) with precise bounds via hyperelliptic curves.

title: Erdős Problem #438: Square-Free Sumsets
description: How large can A ⊆ {1,...,N} be if A+A contains no square numbers? The maximum density is exactly 11/32, achieved by a mod 32 construction (Massias) and proved tight by Khalfalah-Lodha-Szemerédi (2002).

title: Erdős Problem #439: Monochromatic Solutions to x + y = z²
description: In any finite coloring of the integers, must there be distinct x ≠ y of the same color with x + y a perfect square? SOLVED by Khalfalah-Szemerédi (2006): YES.

title: Erdős Problem #44: Extending Sidon Sets
description: Can any Sidon set be extended to achieve near-optimal density (1-eps)sqrt(M)? An OPEN conjecture with auxiliary results about Sidon set bounds proved.

title: Erdős Problem #440: LCM of Consecutive Sequence Elements
description: For infinite sequence A, let A(x) count indices i with lcm(aᵢ, aᵢ₊₁) ≤ x. Is A(x) = O(√x)? YES, and liminf A(x)/√x ≤ 1 always, with equality for A = ℕ (Erdős-Szemerédi 1980).

title: Erdős Problem #441: LCM-Bounded Subsets
description: Find the maximum size g(N) of A ⊆ {1,...,N} such that lcm(a,b) ≤ N for all a,b ∈ A. Is Erdős' construction optimal? Answer: NO - Chen and Dai proved for infinitely many N, the optimal set is strictly larger than Erdős' construction. The asymptotic g(N) ~ (9N/8)^{1/2} is known.

title: Erdős #442: LCM Sums Over Dense Subsets
description: If a subset A ⊆ ℕ has reciprocal sum growing faster than log log x, must the normalized LCM sum diverge? NO — Tao (2024) constructed a counterexample and proved the threshold is sharp.

title: Erdős Problem #443: Common Products k(m-k) and l(n-l)
description: For m,n ≥ 1, how large can the intersection |{k(m-k) : 1≤k≤m/2} ∩ {l(n-l) : 1≤l≤n/2}| be? Can it be arbitrarily large? Is it ≤(mn)^{o(1)}? YES to both - proved by Hegyvári (2025) and Cambie.

title: Erdős Problem #444: Generalized Divisor Functions
description: Let A ⊆ ℕ be infinite and d_A(n) count divisors of n in A. Is limsup max d_A(n) / (Σ 1/a)^k = ∞ for all k? SOLVED: YES by Erdős-Sárközy (1980) — the maximum grows faster than any power of the harmonic sum.

title: Erdős Problem #445: Multiplicative Inverses in Short Intervals
description: For c > 1/2, can we find a,b ∈ (n, n+p^c) with ab ≡ 1 (mod p) for large primes p? Heath-Brown proved this for c > 3/4 using Kloosterman sums. The range c ∈ (1/2, 3/4] remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #446: Density of Integers with Divisors in (n, 2n)
description: Let δ(n) denote the density of integers divisible by some d ∈ (n, 2n). Ford (2008) proved δ(n) ≍ 1/((log n)^α (log log n)^{3/2}) where α ≈ 0.08607, and disproved δ₁(n) = o(δ(n)).

title: Erdős Problem #447: Union-Free Collections of Sets
description: How large can a union-free collection ℱ of subsets of [n] be (no A ∪ B = C with distinct A, B, C ∈ ℱ)? Kleitman (1971) proved |ℱ| < (1+o(1)) C(n, ⌊n/2⌋).

title: Erdős Problem #448: Divisors in Dyadic Intervals
description: Is τ⁺(n) < ε·τ(n) for almost all n? NO (DISPROVED) - Erdős-Tenenbaum showed exceptions have positive density.

title: Close Divisor Pairs
description: Erdős Problem #449 asks whether 'close' divisor pairs (d₁, d₂) with d₁ < d₂ < 2d₁ are rare compared to total divisors. Specifically: is r(n) < ε·τ(n) for almost all n? The answer is NO - for any K > 0, a positive density set has r(n) > K·τ(n).

title: Erdős #45: Monochromatic Egyptian Fractions
description: For k ≥ 2, does there exist n_k such that any k-coloring of proper divisors of n_k contains a monochromatic D' with Σ 1/d = 1? YES (Croot 2003). Bounds: n_k ≈ exp(C^k) doubly exponential (Sawhney).

title: Erdős Problem #450: Divisor Density in Short Intervals
description: How large must y be so that ≤ ε fraction of integers in (x,x+y) have a divisor in (n,2n)? Cambie: 'for all x' fails in some regimes. Erdős–Graham 1980, p.89. OPEN.

title: Primes in (k, 2k) Avoiding Products
description: Estimate n_k, the smallest n > 2k such that (n-1)(n-2)⋯(n-k) has no prime factor in (k, 2k). Conjectured superpolynomial but sub-exponential.

title: Erdős Problem #452: Largest Interval with ω(n) > log log n
description: Let ω(n) count distinct prime factors. What is the largest interval I ⊆ [x,2x] where ω(n) > log log n for all n ∈ I? Known: |I| ≥ log x/(log log x)². Conjecture: (log x)^k is achievable for any k.

title: Erdős Problem #453: Prime Products and Squares
description: Is it true that for all large n, there exists i < n with p_n² < p_{n+i}·p_{n-i}? SOLVED: NO. Pomerance (1979) proved infinitely many n have p_n² > p_{n+i}·p_{n-i} for all i < n, using convex hull geometry on log primes.

title: Erdős 453: Axiom Elimination for Prime Product Bound
description: Eliminates 2 of 4 axioms and the sorry from Erdős Problem #453 by proving nthPrime_is_prime and nthPrime_strictMono from Mathlib's Nat.nth API, and nthPrime_values via Nat.nth_count + decide.

title: Erdős #454: Prime Sum Deviations
description: Let f(n) = min_{i<n} (p_{n+i} + p_{n-i}). Is limsup(f(n) - 2p_n) = ∞? Pomerance (1979) proved limsup ≥ 2. The problem remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #455: Monotone Prime Gap Sequences
description: If primes q₁ < q₂ < ... have non-decreasing gaps, must q_n grow faster than n²?

title: Erdős Problem #456: Smallest Prime ≡ 1 (mod n) vs Smallest Totient Divisor
description: Compare pₙ (smallest prime ≡ 1 mod n) with mₙ (smallest m with n | φ(m)). Is mₙ < pₙ for almost all n? Does pₙ/mₙ → ∞? Three open questions about their relationship.

title: Erdős Problem #457: Small Prime Divisors of Consecutive Products
description: Is there ε > 0 such that infinitely many n have all primes p ≤ (2+ε)log(n) dividing the product of ⌊log n⌋ consecutive integers starting at n+1? Equivalently, is q(n, log n) ≥ (2+ε)log(n) infinitely often? Open.

title: LCM Inequality for Primes
description: Let lcm(1,...,n) denote the least common multiple of {1,...,n}. Is it true that for all k ≥ 1, lcm(1,...,p_{k+1}-1) < p_k · lcm(1,...,p_k)? Erdős and Graham call this 'almost certainly' true, but proving it requires something close to Legendre's conjecture.

title: Erdős Problem #459: Estimate f(u) - Smooth Number Gaps
description: Let f(u) be the largest v such that no m ∈ (u,v) is smooth with respect to u. Estimate f(u). Solved: trivial bounds u+2 ≤ f(u) ≤ u², with f(p) = p² for primes and f(n) = (1+o(1))n for almost all n.

title: Monochromatic Unit Fraction Representations
description: Does every finite colouring of ℕ have a monochromatic solution to 1 = Σ 1/nᵢ? Proved by Croot. Erdős–Graham generalization to arbitrary rationals also holds.

title: Erdős Problem #460: Greedy Coprime Sieve Reciprocals
description: Let $a_0 = 0$, $a_1 = 1$. Define $a_k$ as the least integer $> a_{k-1}$ with $\gcd(n - a_k, n - a_i) = 1$ for all $i < k$. Does $\sum_{0 < a_i < n} \frac{1}{a_i} \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$? OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #461: Distinct Smooth Components in Short Intervals
description: Let $s_t(n)$ be the $t$-smooth component of $n$ and $f(n,t)$ count distinct values of $s_t(m)$ for $m \in \{n+1,\ldots,n+t\}$. Is $f(n,t) \gg t$? Erdős–Graham proved $f(n,t) \gg t/\log t$.

title: Erdős Problem #462: Least Prime Factor Sums in Short Intervals
description: Let $p(n)$ be the least prime factor of $n$. The sum $\sum_{n < x,\, n \text{ composite}} p(n)/n \sim c \cdot \sqrt{x}/(\log x)^2$. Does a short interval of length $C\sqrt{x}(\log x)^2$ capture a bounded fraction of this sum?

title: Erdős Problem #463: Composites Near Their Least Prime Factor
description: Is there f(n) → ∞ such that for all large n, some composite m satisfies n + f(n) < m < n + p(m), where p(m) is the least prime factor of m? Erdős also asks whether n − F(n) ~ c√n.

title: Erdős Problem #464: Lacunary Sequences and Density of Fractional Parts
description: For lacunary A (n_{k+1} ≥ (1+ε)n_k), must there exist irrational θ with {‖θn_k‖} not dense? SOLVED: YES (de Mathan/Pollington 1979-80). Best bound: ε/log(1/ε) (Peres-Schlag 2010).

title: Erdős Problem #465: Points with Distances Avoiding Integers
description: Let N(X,δ) be the maximum number of points in a circle of radius X such that all pairwise distances avoid integers by at least δ. Is N(X,δ) = o(X)? Is N(X,δ) < X^{1/2+o(1)}? Both answered YES by Sárközy (1976) and Konyagin (2001).

title: Erdős #466: Points in a Circle with Fractional Distance Separation
description: Is there δ > 0 such that arbitrarily many points fit in a large disk with all pairwise distances bounded away from integers by ≥ δ? PROVED: Graham showed N(X,1/10) ≥ (log X)/10; Sárközy (1976) proved N(X,δ) > X^{1/2−δ^{1/7}}, nearly matching Konyagin's upper bound X^{1/2}.

title: Erdős Problem #467: Dual Covering by Prime Residue Classes
description: For large $x$, can we choose residue classes $a_p$ for each prime $p \leq x$ and partition the primes into $A \sqcup B$ so that every $n < x$ is covered by both $A$ and $B$ independently? An open problem in covering congruences from Erdős–Graham (1980).

title: Partial Sums of Divisors
description: Let D_n = partial sums of divisors of n (excluding 1). How large is D_n \ ⋃_{m<n} D_m? If f(N) = min{n : N ∈ D_n}, is f(N) = o(N)? Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #469: Primitive Pseudoperfect Numbers
description: A primitive pseudoperfect number is a sum of distinct proper divisors, with no proper divisor having this property. Does Σ_{n ∈ A} 1/n converge? OEIS A006036. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #47: Unit Fractions from Dense Sets
description: If A ⊆ {1,…,N} has ∑ 1/a > δ log N, must some S ⊆ A have ∑ 1/n = 1? Yes — proved by Bloom (2021). Liu–Sawhney improved the quantitative bound. SOLVED.

title: Erdős Problem #470: Weird Numbers
description: A number n is called weird if σ(n) ≥ 2n (abundant) but n is not pseudoperfect (cannot be expressed as the sum of any subset of its proper divisors). Erdős asked two OPEN questions: (1) Are there any odd weird numbers? (2) Are there infinitely many primitive weird numbers?

title: Erdős Problem #471: Ulam's Prime Sequence Problem
description: Given a finite set of primes Q₀, define Qᵢ₊₁ = Qᵢ ∪ {primes that are sums of 3 distinct elements of Qᵢ}. Does there exist Q₀ such that Qᵢ becomes arbitrarily large? YES, proved via Vinogradov's theorem by Mrazović-Kovač and Alon.

title: Erdős Problem #472: Ulam Prime Sequences
description: Given an initial finite sequence of primes, extend by taking q_{n+1} as the smallest prime of the form q_n + q_i − 1. Does there exist a seed making the sequence infinite? Starting with 3, 5 gives 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, …

title: Erdős Problem #473: Prime Sum Permutations
description: Is there a permutation a₁, a₂, ... of positive integers such that a_k + a_{k+1} is always prime? SOLVED: YES (Odlyzko). Related: greedy algorithm doesn't produce all primes as sums (197 missing).

title: Erdős Problem #474: Coloring ℝ² for Uncountable Sets
description: Under what set-theoretic assumptions can ℝ² be 3-colored such that every uncountable A has A² containing pairs of all colors? PARTIALLY RESOLVED: works under CH (Erdős), fails with large c (Shelah), open for c = ℵ₂.

title: Erdős Problem #475: Graham's Rearrangement Conjecture
description: Given A ⊆ 𝔽ₚ\{0}, does there exist an ordering with all partial sums distinct? Proven for t ≤ 12, t ≥ p-3, t ≤ exp((log p)^{1/4}). General case OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #476: The Erdős-Heilbronn Conjecture
description: For A ⊆ 𝔽ₚ, is |A +̂ A| ≥ min(2|A| - 3, p) where A +̂ A denotes sums of distinct pairs? YES, proved by da Silva-Hamidoune (1994).

title: Erdős Problem #477: Polynomial Complements of Integer Sets
description: Is there a polynomial f: ℤ → ℤ of degree ≥ 2 and a set A ⊆ ℤ such that every integer has a unique representation a + f(n)? Sekanina (1959) showed no for f(x) = x². Erdős–Graham conjecture: no for all such f. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #478: Factorial Residues Modulo Primes
description: Let p be a prime and A_p = { k! mod p : 1 ≤ k < p }. Is it true that |A_p| ~ (1 - 1/e) · p? The factorial residue set is conjectured to cover a density (1 - 1/e) fraction of residues, motivated by the birthday-type heuristic for multiplicative random walks. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #479: Powers of 2 Modulo n
description: Is it true that, for all k ≠ 1, there are infinitely many n such that 2^n ≡ k (mod n)? This is Graham's conjecture.

title: Erdos Problem #48: Infinitely Many Pairs with phi(n) = sigma(m)
description: Are there infinitely many integers n, m such that phi(n) = sigma(m)? YES, proved by Ford-Luca-Pomerance (2010).

title: Erdős Problem #480: Sequence Approximation in the Unit Interval
description: For any sequence in [0,1], are there infinitely many pairs (m,n) with |x_{m+n} - x_m| ≤ 1/(√5·n)? Solved by Chung-Graham (1984) with optimal constant.

title: Erdős Problem #481: Affine Sequence Iteration and Eventual Repetition
description: For affine maps T with Σ(1/aᵢ) > 1, iterating from A₁=(1) must eventually produce repeated elements. Proved by Klarner (1982) using free semigroup theory.

title: Erdős Problem #482: Binary Digits via Recurrence
description: The recurrence a₁ = 1, a_{n+1} = ⌊√2(aₙ + 1/2)⌋ has the property that a_{2n+1} - 2a_{2n-1} gives the n-th binary digit of √2. Stoll (2005-2006) generalized to √m and other algebraic numbers.

title: Erdős Problem #483: Growth Rate of Schur Numbers
description: Is f(k) < c^k for some c, where f(k) is the Schur number (min N forcing monochromatic a+b=c in k-coloring)? S(1)=2 and S(2)=5 proved from SchursTheorem. S(k) defined via Nat.find with monotonicity. Open.

title: Erdős #484: Monochromatic Sums in Colorings
description: Prove ∃ c > 0 such that any k-coloring of {1,...,N} has at least cN integers representable as monochromatic sums a+b (same color, a≠b). SOLVED: Erdős-Sárközy-Sós (1989) proved N/2 − O(N^{1−1/2^{k+1}}) even sums; for k=2, N/2 − O(log N) is tight (2-adic valuation obstruction).

title: Minimum Terms in Squared Polynomials
description: Let f(k) be the minimum number of terms in P(x)², where P ranges over polynomials with exactly k non-zero terms. Is f(k) → ∞ as k → ∞?

title: Erdős #485 OQ: Exact Growth Rate of f(k) — Minimum Terms in Squared Polynomials
description: Open question about the exact asymptotic growth rate of f(k), the minimum number of terms in P(x)² over polynomials with k terms. Known: c·log k ≤ f(k) ≤ k^(1-c). The enormous gap between logarithmic and polynomial growth is unresolved.

title: Erdos #485 OQ: Combinatorial Proof of f(k) -> infinity via Sumsets
description: Open question: can f(k) -> infinity be proved combinatorially via sumset bounds, rather than algebraically? Formalizes the sumset framework connecting polynomial squaring to additive combinatorics. Proves the positive-coefficient case completely and identifies the cancellation barrier for general polynomials.

title: Erdős Problem #486: Logarithmic Density for Modular Avoidance Sets
description: For any choice of forbidden residue classes modulo each n, must the set of integers avoiding all forbidden classes have a logarithmic density?

title: LCM Triples in Dense Sets
description: Let A ⊆ ℕ have positive density. Must there exist distinct a, b, c ∈ A such that lcm(a,b) = c? YES - follows from Kleitman's 1971 theorem on union-free collections.

title: Erdős Problem #488: Divisibility Density in Multiples of Finite Sets
description: Let A be a finite set and B = {n ≥ 1 : a | n for some a ∈ A}. Is |B ∩ [1,m]|/m < 2·|B ∩ [1,n]|/n for all m > n ≥ max(A)? The constant 2 is optimal.

title: Erdős Problem #489: Gaps Between B-Free Numbers
description: For sparse A, does lim (1/x)Σ(b_{i+1}-b_i)² exist for A-free numbers B? OPEN in general; YES for squarefree numbers (Erdős).

title: Erdős Problem #49: Sets with Increasing Euler Totient Values
description: Let A ⊆ {1,…,N} with φ(a₁) < ⋯ < φ(aₜ). The primes form such a set. Tao (2023) proved |A| ≤ (1+o(1))π(N), confirming primes are asymptotically largest.

title: Erdős Problem #490: Distinct Products of Two Sets
description: If A, B ⊆ {1,...,N} have all products ab distinct, is |A||B| ≪ N²/log N? SOLVED: YES (Szemerédi 1976). Optimal example achieves N²/(2 log N).

title: Does lim max|A||B|·log N/N² Exist?
description: Formalizes the open question from Erdős Problem #490: does lim max|A||B|·log N/N² exist, where the maximum is over pairs with distinct products in {1,...,N}? Proves the product ratio is sandwiched between positive constants (Szemerédi upper bound and prime construction lower bound) and that any limit must lie in [c, C]. Three axioms encoding deep number-theoretic bounds, nine theorems, zero sorries.

title: Erdős Problem #491: Characterization of Additive Functions
description: If f: ℕ → ℝ is additive and |f(n+1) - f(n)| < c for all n, then f(n) = c'·log(n) + O(1). Proved by Wirsing (1970).

title: Erdős Problem #492: Uniform Distribution Relative to a Fixed Sequence
description: Is f(αn) uniformly distributed in [0,1) for almost all α, where f is a generalized fractional part? DISPROVED by Schmidt (1969).

title: Erdős Problem #493: Product Minus Sum Representation
description: Does there exist k such that every sufficiently large integer n = prod(ai) - sum(ai) for ai >= 2? Yes, k=2 works: n = 2(n+2) - (2+(n+2)). SOLVED. Fully verified (0 axioms, 0 sorries).

title: Erdős Problem #494: Set Determination from k-Sums
description: Given a finite set A in the complex plane and k >= 1, does the multiset of k-sums (sums of k distinct elements) together with |A| uniquely determine A? For k > 2, yes for sufficiently large |A|.

title: Erdős Problem #495: The Littlewood Conjecture
description: For all real α, β, is lim inf n·‖nα‖·‖nβ‖ = 0? The Littlewood conjecture on multiplicative Diophantine approximation, open since c. 1930.

title: Erdős Problem #496: Oppenheim Conjecture
description: For irrational α > 0 and any ε > 0, there exist positive integers x, y, z with |x² + y² − αz²| < ε. Proved by Margulis (1987) using unipotent dynamics on homogeneous spaces.

title: Erdős Problem #497: Counting Antichains (Dedekind's Problem)
description: How many antichains exist in P([n])? Kleitman (1969) proved the answer is 2^{(1+o(1))·C(n, ⌊n/2⌋)}, determining the logarithmic order of the Dedekind numbers.

title: Erdős Problem #498: Complex Littlewood–Offord Problem
description: For complex z₁,...,zₙ with |zᵢ| ≥ 1, at most C(n,⌊n/2⌋) signed sums Σεᵢzᵢ fall in any unit disc. Solved by Kleitman (1965), generalized to Hilbert spaces (1970).

title: Erdős Problem #499: Diagonals of Doubly Stochastic Matrices
description: Does every n×n doubly stochastic matrix have a diagonal with product ≥ n^{-n}? YES, proved by Marcus-Minc (1962).

title: Erdős Problem #5: Limit Points of Normalized Prime Gaps
description: Is the set S of limit points of (p_{n+1} - p_n)/log(p_n) equal to [0, ∞)? Known: 0 ∈ S (GPY), ∞ ∈ S (Westzynthius), S has positive measure (Erdős–Ricci), at least 1/3 coverage (Merikoski). Open.

title: Erdős Problem #5: Prime Gap Limit Points
description: Formalizes Erdős Problem #5: is the set S = {lim (p_{n+1}-p_n)/log(n)} of prime gap ratio limit points equal to [0,∞)? Develops prime gap and normalized gap functions, axiomatizes known partial results (Westzynthius large gaps, Zhang bounded gaps, Hildebrand-Maier large limit points), and proves S is closed, non-empty, and unbounded. 29 theorems, 3 axioms.

title: Erdős Problem #50: Singularity of the Totient Distribution Function
description: Schoenberg proved the density f(c) = d({n : φ(n)/n < c}) exists for all c. Erdős showed f is purely singular. $250 prize: is it true that f'(x) > 0 for no x?

title: Erdős Problem #500: Turán Density of K₄³
description: Determine ex₃(n, K₄³): the maximum number of 3-edges on n vertices avoiding K₄³. Turán (1941) conjectured π(K₄³) = 5/9. Best bounds: 5/9 ≤ π ≤ 0.5612 (Razborov 2010). Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős #501: Independent Sets for Outer Measure Families
description: For bounded sets A_x with outer measure < 1, must infinite independent sets exist? Answer depends on set-theoretic axioms!

title: Erdős Problem #502: Two-Distance Sets in Euclidean Space
description: What is the maximum size f(n) of a set A ⊆ ℝⁿ with exactly two distinct pairwise distances? Bannai–Bannai–Stanton proved f(n) ≤ C(n+2,2); a projection construction gives f(n) ≥ C(n+1,2). Status: SOLVED.

title: Erdős Problem #503: Maximum Isosceles Sets in Rⁿ
description: What is the maximum size of A ⊆ ℝⁿ with every triple isosceles? f(2)=6 (Kelly), f(3)=8 (Croft). General: C(n+1,2)+1 ≤ f(n) ≤ C(n+2,2) (Blokhuis/Alweiss). OPEN for n ≥ 4.

title: Erdős Problem #504: Maximum Angle in Point Sets
description: Determine α_n, the supremum of angles α such that every n-point set in the plane contains three points forming an angle at least α.

title: Erdős Problem #505: Borsuk's Conjecture
description: Can every diameter-1 set in ℝⁿ be partitioned into ≤ n+1 parts of smaller diameter? TRUE for n ≤ 3, FALSE for n ≥ 64 (Brouwer–Jenrich 2014). Open for 4 ≤ n ≤ 63.

title: Erdős Problem #506: Minimum Number of Circles from n Points
description: What is the minimum number of distinct circles determined by n points in ℝ², not all concyclic? Elliott (1967): ≥ C(n-1,2) for n > 393. Segre: fails for n = 8. Open for small n.

title: Erdős Problem #507: Heilbronn's Triangle Problem
description: Estimate α(n), the smallest area such that every n-point set in the unit disk contains a triangle of area ≤ α(n). Best bounds: (log n)/n² ≪ α(n) ≪ 1/n^{7/6+o(1)}. Status: OPEN.

title: The Hadwiger-Nelson Problem
description: What is the chromatic number of the plane? Known: 5 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7. Lower bound 5 by de Grey (2018). Upper bound 7 by hexagonal tiling (Isbell). Open.

title: Erdős Problem #509: Covering Polynomial Sublevel Sets with Discs
description: Can the sublevel set {z ∈ ℂ : |f(z)| ≤ 1} of a monic polynomial be covered by closed discs with total radius ≤ 2? Cartan proved 2e works, Pommerenke improved to 2.59, but the conjectured optimal bound of 2 remains open.

title: Erdős #51: Totient Preimage Growth
description: Is there an infinite set A ⊂ ℕ of totient values such that the smallest preimage n_a of each a ∈ A satisfies n_a/a → ∞? That is, can the minimal solution to φ(n) = a grow much faster than a? OPEN.

title: Erdős #510: Chowla's Cosine Problem
description: For finite A ⊂ ℕ of size N, must there exist θ with ∑ cos(nθ) < −c√N for absolute c > 0? Best known: −cN^{1/7} (Bedert 2025). Sidon sets show √N is optimal. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #511: Bounded Components of Polynomial Lemniscates
description: For a monic polynomial f(z), is the number of connected components of {z : |f(z)| < 1} with diameter > c bounded independently of degree? NO - disproved by Pommerenke (1961).

title: Erdős Problem #512: Littlewood's Conjecture on Exponential Sums
description: For finite A ⊂ ℤ with |A| = N, is ∫₀¹ |∑_{n∈A} e(nθ)| dθ ≫ log N? SOLVED: YES (Konyagin 1981, McGehee-Pigno-Smith 1981).

title: Erdős Problem #513: Maximum Term of a Power Series
description: For transcendental entire f(z) = Σ aₙzⁿ, determine sup liminf_{r→∞} μ(r)/M(r) where μ(r) = max_n |aₙrⁿ| and M(r) = max_{|z|=r} |f(z)|. Known: value ∈ (1/2, 2/π - c]. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #514: Growth of Entire Functions Along Paths
description: For a transcendental entire function f(z), does there exist a path L such that |f(z)/z^n| → ∞ as z → ∞ along L for every n? Part 1 proved by Boas (unpublished); parts 2 and 3 remain open.

title: Erdős Problem #515: Path Integrals of Inverse Entire Functions
description: For transcendental entire f, does there exist a path C → ∞ such that ∫_C |f|^{-λ} dz < ∞ for ALL λ > 0? SOLVED: YES by Lewis-Rossi-Weitsman (1984).

title: Erdős Problem #516: Gap Series and the Minimum Modulus Problem
description: For entire functions with Fabry gaps (nₖ/k → ∞), is lim sup (log m(r))/(log M(r)) = 1? YES - proved by Fuchs (1963).

title: Erdős Problem #517: Lacunary Entire Functions and Value Distribution
description: Do entire functions with Fabry gaps (nₖ/k → ∞) assume every value infinitely often? The main conjecture is OPEN, but Biernacki proved the stronger Fejér gap case.

title: Erdős Problem #518: Monochromatic Path Covers
description: Can K_n with any two-coloring be covered by √n monochromatic paths of the same color? SOLVED: Yes (Pokrovskiy-Versteegen-Williams 2024).

title: Power Sums of Complex Numbers
description: Turán's power sum problem: For z₁,...,zₙ ∈ ℂ with z₁=1, is there an absolute c>0 such that max_k |∑zᵢᵏ| > c? YES (Atkinson 1961). Best known: c > 1/2 (Biró 2000). Optimal ≈ 0.7.

title: Erdős Problem #52: The Sum-Product Conjecture
description: For a finite set A of integers, is max(|A+A|, |A·A|) ≫ |A|^{2-ε} for every ε > 0? Erdős–Szemerédi proved a super-linear bound; Bloom (2025) achieved |A|^{1.335}. OPEN ($250 prize).

title: Erdős Problem #520: Rademacher Multiplicative Functions
description: For a Rademacher multiplicative function f, does there exist a constant c > 0 such that almost surely limsup (∑_{m≤N} f(m)) / √(N log log N) = c?

title: Erdős Problem #521: Real Roots of Random ±1 Polynomials
description: For random ±1 polynomials, is Rₙ/log n → 2/π almost surely? Erdős-Offord (1956) proved E[Rₙ] = (2/π + o(1))log n. Do (2024) proved a.s. limit 1/π for roots in [-1,1]. Full a.s. convergence remains OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #522: Random Polynomial Roots in the Unit Disk
description: For random polynomials with ±1 coefficients, does the number of roots in the unit disk converge to n/2 almost surely? Yakir (2021) proved convergence in probability.

title: Erdős Problem #523: Maximum of Random Polynomials on Unit Circle
description: For random ±1 polynomials, max_{|z|=1} |f(z)| = (C+o(1))√(n log n)? SOLVED: YES with C = 1 (Halász 1973).

title: Erdős #524: Maximum of Random Sign Polynomials
description: Determine the correct order of magnitude of M_n(t) = max_{x∈[-1,1]} |Σ_{k≤n} (±1)·x^k| for a.e. t ∈ (0,1), where signs come from binary digits of t. Known: n^{1/2-ε} ≪ M_n ≪ √(n/log log n) i.o. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #525: Littlewood Polynomials and Minimum Modulus
description: For Littlewood polynomials (±1 coefficients), what is m(f) = min|f(z)| on |z|=1? SOLVED: m(f) = o(1) almost surely (Kashin 1987), m(f) ≈ n^{-1/2} (Konyagin 1994), exact distribution identified (Cook-Nguyen 2021).

title: Multivariate Littlewood Polynomials
description: Explores higher-dimensional Littlewood polynomials on the d-torus T^d. The square-root cancellation heuristic predicts m(f) ≈ n^(-d/2). Open for d ≥ 2.

title: Erdős Problem #526: Circle Coverage by Random Arcs (Dvoretzky's Problem)
description: Given arc lengths a_n → 0 with Σa_n = ∞, when do random arcs cover the unit circle with probability 1? Shepp (1972) proved the necessary and sufficient condition is Σ exp(a_1+...+a_n)/n² = ∞.

title: Erdős Problem #527: Convergence of Random Power Series on Unit Circle
description: For aₙ with Σ|aₙ|² = ∞ and |aₙ| = o(1/√n), does Σ εₙaₙzⁿ converge for some |z| = 1 for almost all sign choices? YES, and the convergence set has Hausdorff dimension 1 (Michelen-Sawhney 2025).

title: Erdős Problem #528: Connective Constant for Self-Avoiding Walks
description: Let f(n,k) count n-step self-avoiding walks in ℤ^k. Determine C_k = lim f(n,k)^{1/n}. The limit EXISTS (Hammersley-Morton 1954) by submultiplicativity, bounds k ≤ C_k ≤ 2k-1, Kesten's asymptotic C_k = 2k-1-1/(2k)+O(1/k²), and C_2 = 2.6381585... numerically. Exact closed forms remain OPEN for all k.

title: Erdős Problem #529: Self-Avoiding Walk End-to-End Distance
description: Study the expected end-to-end distance d_k(n) of self-avoiding walks in Z^k. High dimensions (k >= 5) resolved with d_k(n) ~ sqrt(n). Lower dimensions remain open with conjectured anomalous exponents.

title: Erdős Problem #53: Sums and Products of Distinct Elements
description: For every k, if |A| is sufficiently large, are there at least |A|^k integers representable as sums or products of distinct elements of A? PROVED by Chang (2003). Erdős–Szemerédi upper bound: exp(c(log|A|)² log log|A|).

title: Erdős Problem #530: Maximum Sidon Subsets of Finite Sets
description: For a finite set A of size N, what is the maximum size ℓ(N) of a Sidon subset? Komlós–Sulyok–Szemerédi: N^{1/2} ≪ ℓ(N) ≤ (1+o(1))N^{1/2}. Conjectured: ℓ(N) ~ N^{1/2}. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #531: Folkman's Theorem - Monochromatic Subset Sums
description: Estimate F(k), the minimal N such that any 2-coloring of {1,...,N} has a k-element set with monochromatic subset sums. Lower bound: F(k) ≥ 2^{2^{k-1}/k}.

title: Erdős Problem #532: Hindman's Theorem (IP Sets)
description: If ℕ is finitely colored, must some color class be an IP set? Proved by Hindman (1974): YES, for any finite coloring there exists an infinite set A such that all finite subset sums of A are monochromatic.

title: Erdős Problem #533: Triangle-Free Subsets in K₅-Free Dense Graphs
description: Must a K₅-free graph on n vertices with ≥ δn² edges contain a triangle-free subset of ≫ n vertices? True for δ > 1/16 (EHSSS). Fails for K₇ at δ = 1/4 (Erdős–Rogers). Open.

title: Erdős Problem #534: Maximum GCD-Intersecting Sets
description: What is the largest subset A ⊆ {1,...,N} containing N such that gcd(a,b) > 1 for all distinct a,b ∈ A? Solved by Ahlswede-Khachatrian (1996) who proved the optimal sets use multiples of {2q₁,...,2qⱼ, q₁⋯qⱼ}.

title: Erdős Problem #535: GCD-Free r-Subsets
description: For r ≥ 3, estimate f_r(N): the maximum size of A ⊆ {1,...,N} with no r elements having equal pairwise gcds. Known: N^{1/2+o(1)} upper (Abbott-Hanson), N^{c/log log N} lower (Erdős). Gap remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #536: Equal Pairwise LCMs in Dense Sets
description: If A ⊆ {1,...,N} has |A| ≥ εN, must there be distinct a,b,c ∈ A with [a,b]=[b,c]=[a,c]? Weisenberg: yes for ε > 221/225. Fails for four elements. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #537: Three Numbers with Equal Prime Products
description: Let ε > 0 and N be large. If A ⊆ {1,...,N} has |A| ≥ εN, must there exist a₁,a₂,a₃ ∈ A and distinct primes p₁,p₂,p₃ with a₁p₁ = a₂p₂ = a₃p₃? NO, disproved by Ruzsa's counterexample.

title: Erdős Problem #538: Reciprocal Sums with Bounded Prime Representations
description: For A ⊆ {1,...,N} with at most r representations m = p·a (p prime, a ∈ A), find the best upper bound for Σ 1/n. Erdős showed ≪ r·log N/log log N. OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #539: GCD-Reduced Quotients
description: For A ⊆ ℕ of size n, what is the minimum size of { a/gcd(a,b) : a,b ∈ A }? Bounds: n^{1/2} ≪ h(n) ≪ n^{2/3}. Exact behavior unknown.

title: Erdős Problem #54: Ramsey 2-Complete Sets
description: A set A is Ramsey 2-complete if every 2-colouring yields monochromatic sums covering all large integers. Conlon–Fox–Pham (2021) showed the minimum growth rate is Θ((log N)²).

title: Erdős Problem #540: Zero-Sum Subsets (Erdős-Heilbronn Conjecture)
description: If A ⊆ ℤ/Nℤ has size ≫ √N, must A contain a non-empty zero-sum subset? YES, proved by Szemerédi (1970). Optimal threshold √(2N) for primes (Balandraud 2012).

title: Erdős Problem #541: Graham's Conjecture on Zero-Sum Subsequences
description: If a sequence of p residues modulo p has the property that all nonempty zero-sum subsets have the same cardinality r, must at most 2 distinct residues appear in the sequence? This was conjectured by Graham and proved by Erdős-Szemerédi (1976) for large primes, then by Gao-Hamidoune-Wang (2010) for all moduli.

title: Erdős Problem #542: Reciprocal Sums Under LCM Constraints
description: If A ⊆ {1,...,n} with lcm(a,b) > n for distinct a,b ∈ A, must ∑ 1/a ≤ 31/30? Solved by Schinzel-Szekeres (1959).

title: Erdős Problem #543: Random Subset Sums in Abelian Groups
description: Is f(N) ≤ log₂ N + o(log log N), where f(N) is the minimal random subset size to span an abelian group via subset sums? DISPROVED — the O(log log N) term is optimal.

title: Erdős Problem #544: Consecutive Ramsey Number Differences
description: Show that R(3, k+1) − R(3, k) → ∞. Prove or disprove that R(3, k+1) − R(3, k) = o(k).

title: Erdős Problem #545: Ramsey Numbers and Maximally Complete Graphs
description: Is the Ramsey number R(G) maximized when G is 'as complete as possible' for a given number of edges? Counterexamples exist for m in {2,3,4,5,7,8,9}, but the asymptotic version remains open.

title: Erdős #546: Ramsey Numbers and Edge Count
description: For a graph G with no isolated vertices and m edges, is R(G) ≤ 2^{O(√m)}? Solved by Sudakov (2011). The ≥3 color version remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #547: Tree Ramsey Numbers
description: For any tree T on n vertices, R(T) ≤ 2n - 2. The bound is tight: stars achieve R(S_n) = 2n - 2.

title: Erdős Problem #548: The Erdős-Sós Conjecture
description: Every graph on n vertices with more than (k-1)n/2 edges contains every tree on k+1 vertices. This famous conjecture of Erdős and Sós remains open, with partial results for girth >= 5, C4-free graphs, and large k.

title: Erdős Problem #549: Ramsey Numbers for Bipartite Trees
description: Conjecture: R(T) = 4k-1 for bipartite (k, 2k) trees. DISPROVED by Norin-Sun-Zhao! The double star has R(T) >= 4.2k. Best bounds: 4.2k <= R <= 4.21526k.

title: Erdős Problem #55: Ramsey r-Complete Sets
description: A set A is Ramsey r-complete if every r-coloring has a monochromatic subset whose sums cover all large integers. The optimal growth rate is Θ(r(log N)²).

title: Erdős #550: Ramsey Numbers for Trees and Multipartite Graphs
description: For T a tree on n vertices and G = K_{m₁,...,mₖ}, prove R(T,G) ≤ (χ(G)-1)(R(T,K_{m₁,m₂})-1)+m₁. Chvátal (1977): R(T,Kₘ) = (m-1)(n-1)+1 is the foundational result.

title: Erdős #551: Ramsey Numbers for Cycles vs Complete Graphs
description: Prove R(C_k, K_n) = (k-1)(n-1) + 1 for k ≥ n ≥ 3 (except n=k=3). Bondy-Erdős (1973): k > n²-2. Nikiforov (2005): k ≥ 4n+2. Keevash-Long-Skokan (2021): k ≥ C log n / log log n.

title: Erdős #552: Ramsey Number R(C₄, Sₙ)
description: Determine R(C₄, Sₙ) for the 4-cycle and star graph. Is R(C₄, Sₙ) ≤ n + √n - c for infinitely many n? Connected to prime gaps.

title: Erdős Problem #553: Multi-Color Ramsey Asymptotics
description: Show R(3,3,n)/R(3,n) → ∞. The third color dramatically increases the off-diagonal threshold. Solved by Alon-Rödl (2005): R(3,3,n) ≍ n³(log n)^O(1) vs R(3,n) ≪ n²/log n.

title: Erdős Problem #554: Odd Cycle vs Triangle Ramsey Numbers
description: Show that for any n >= 2, the ratio R(C_{2n+1}; k) / R(K_3; k) tends to 0 as k tends to infinity, where R(G; k) is the k-color Ramsey number of G.

title: Erdős Problem #555: Ramsey Numbers of Even Cycles
description: Determine R(C₂ₙ; k), the multicolor Ramsey number of even cycles. Erdős showed k^{1+1/(2n)} ≪ R(C₂ₙ; k) ≪ k^{1+1/(n-1)}. For C₄, Chung-Graham gave k²-k+1 < R(C₄;k) ≤ k²+k+1. The exact growth rate is open.

title: Erdős Problem #556: 3-Color Ramsey Number for Cycles
description: Show that R(C_n;3) ≤ 4n-3, where R(G;3) is the 3-color Ramsey number. PROVED: bound is tight for odd n (KSS 2005), and R(C_n;3) = 2n for even n (Benevides-Skokan 2009).

title: Erdős Problem #557: Multicolor Ramsey Numbers of Trees
description: Is R(T; k) ≤ k·n + O(1) for any tree T on n vertices and k colors? The star lower bound R(S_n; k) ≥ k(n-1)+1 shows this would be tight. Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #558: Multicolor Ramsey Numbers for Complete Bipartite Graphs
description: Determine R(K_{s,t}; k), the minimum m such that any k-coloring of K_m contains monochromatic K_{s,t}. Key results: R(K_{2,2}; k) ~ k², R(K_{3,3}; k) ~ k³.

title: Erdős Problem #559: Size Ramsey Numbers for Bounded Degree Graphs
description: Does R̂(G) ≪_d n for bounded-degree graphs G? DISPROVED for d ≥ 3 by Rödl-Szemerédi (2000). The size Ramsey number R̂(G) is the minimum edges m such that some graph H with m edges is Ramsey for G.

title: Erdős Problem #56: Weakly Divisible Sets
description: Is the set of multiples of the first k primes the largest subset of {1,...,N} with no k+1 pairwise coprime elements?

title: Erdos Problem #560: Size Ramsey Number of Complete Bipartite Graphs
description: Determine the size Ramsey number R_hat(K_{n,n}) - the minimum edges in a graph H such that any 2-coloring contains a monochromatic K_{n,n}. Known bounds: (1/60)n^2*2^n to (3/2)n^3*2^n.

title: Size Ramsey Numbers for Unions of Stars
description: For unions of stars F₁ = ∪_{i≤s} K_{1,nᵢ} and F₂ = ∪_{j≤t} K_{1,mⱼ}, prove that the size Ramsey number R̂(F₁,F₂) = Σ_{k=2}^{s+t} max{nᵢ + mⱼ - 1 : i + j = k}. The uniform case (all nᵢ equal, all mⱼ equal) was proven by Burr-Erdős-Faudree-Rousseau-Schelp (1978).

title: Erdős Problem #562: Hypergraph Ramsey Number Tower Growth
description: For r ≥ 3, prove that log_{r-1} R_r(n) ≍ n, where R_r(n) is the r-uniform hypergraph Ramsey number. Upper bound: twr_{r-1}(O(n²)) from Erdős–Rado. Lower: twr_{r-1}(Ω(n)). Status: OPEN.

title: Erdős Problem #563: Balanced 2-Colorings and Subset Edge Density
description: F(n,alpha) = smallest m with a 2-coloring of K_n where every m-subset has > alpha fraction in each color. Conjecture: F(n,alpha) ~ c_alpha log n for alpha < 1/2. Known: Theta(log n) by probabilistic method.

title: Erdős Problem #564: Hypergraph Ramsey Numbers
description: Is there a constant c > 0 such that R₃(n) ≥ 2^{2^{cn}}? An open problem asking whether the lower bound for 3-uniform hypergraph Ramsey numbers can match the tower height of the upper bound.

title: Erdős Problem #565: Induced Ramsey Numbers
description: Is R*(G) ≤ 2^{O(n)} for any graph G on n vertices, where R*(G) is the induced Ramsey number? SOLVED by Aragão, Campos, Dahia, Filipe, and Marciano (2025): YES!

title: Erdős Problem #566: Ramsey Size Linearity for Sparse Graphs
description: If every k-vertex subgraph of G has at most 2k−3 edges, is G Ramsey size linear? True for ≤ n+1 edges (EFRS 1993), false for 2n−2 edges. Implies Problem #567. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #567: Ramsey Size Linearity of Q₃, K₃,₃, H₅
description: Are Q₃ (3-cube), K₃,₃ (complete bipartite), and H₅ (C₅ + two chords) Ramsey size linear? Special case of #566. Bradač–Gishboliner–Sudakov: K₄ subdivisions with ≥ 6 vertices are linear. Open.

title: Erdős Problem #568: Ramsey Size Linearity from Tree and Clique Bounds
description: If R(G, Tₙ) ≪ n for all trees and R(G, Kₙ) ≪ n² for all complete graphs, must G be Ramsey size linear? Posed by EFRS (1993). Open.

title: Erdős Problem #569: Odd Cycle Ramsey Numbers Linear in Edges
description: For k ≥ 1, determine the best constant c_k such that R(C_{2k+1}, H) ≤ c_k · m for any graph H on m edges without isolated vertices. The EFRS93 bound R ≤ c·k·m is known, but optimal c_k remains open.

title: Erdős Problem #57: Odd Cycles in Graphs with Infinite Chromatic Number
description: If G has infinite chromatic number and a₁ < a₂ < ⋯ are its odd cycle lengths, then ∑ 1/aᵢ = ∞. Solved by Liu-Montgomery (2020).

title: Erdős Problem #570: Cycle-Graph Ramsey Numbers
description: For k ≥ 3 and graph H with m edges (no isolated vertices), is R(C_k, H) ≤ 2m + ⌈(k-1)/2⌉? YES - fully resolved through work spanning 1993-2024.

title: Erdős Problem #571: Rational Turán Exponents for Bipartite Graphs
description: Is every rational α ∈ [1,2) a Turán exponent? Does there exist a bipartite graph G with ex(n;G) ≍ n^α for each such α? OPEN. Bukh-Conlon solved the finite family variant.
