description: The p-adic valuation of C(n,k) equals the number of carries when adding k and n-k in base p. A beautiful connection between combinatorics and positional numeral systems.

title: Multinomial Analogs of Kummer's Theorem
description: Extends Kummer's theorem from binomial to multinomial coefficients via iterated binomial decomposition. The p-adic valuation of a multinomial coefficient equals the total carries when adding the parts in base p.

title: q-Kummer Theorem: Cyclotomic Factorization of q-Binomials
description: The q-binomial coefficient [n choose k]_q factors as a product of cyclotomic polynomials Phi_d^e_d, where e_d = floor(n/d) - floor(k/d) - floor((n-k)/d) counts carries in base d. This generalizes classical Kummer from primes to ALL positive integers d >= 2.

title: Lagrange's Four Squares Theorem
description: Every natural number can be expressed as the sum of four squares, a profound result connecting number theory to quaternion algebra.

title: Distribution of Four-Square Representations Among Orderings
description: Studies how representations n = a²+b²+c²+d² distribute among orderings, classifying all contribution patterns (trivial, all-equal, three-equal, two-pair, two-equal, two-distinct types) and proving each type family has a fixed contribution size. Complete contribution value set {1,8,16,24,32,48,64,96,192,384} determined. Orbit-stabilizer structure for all types proved. 105 theorems, 0 axioms.

title: Lagrange's Theorem
description: Lagrange's theorem: for a finite group $G$ and subgroup $H \leq G$, $|H|$ divides $|G|$. Wiedijk 100 theorem #71, formalized in Lean 4 via Mathlib's coset theory. Derives six corollaries including element order divisibility, $g^{|G|}=1$, Fermat's little theorem from the group $(\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z})^\times$, and prime-order cyclicity.

title: The Orbit-Stabilizer Theorem (Generalization of Lagrange)
description: The orbit-stabilizer theorem: for a group $G$ acting on a set $X$, $|G| = |\text{Orb}(x)| \times |\text{Stab}(x)|$ for any $x \in X$. This fundamental result generalizes Lagrange's theorem (the special case where $G$ acts on $G/H$) and implies Burnside's lemma, the class equation, and the nontriviality of $p$-group centers.

title: Hall's Theorem for Solvable Groups (Converse of Lagrange)
description: Formalizes Hall's theorem (1928) — the partial converse of Lagrange's theorem for solvable groups. A Hall subgroup has order coprime to its index; Hall's theorem states every Hall divisor of a solvable group's order yields a subgroup, and all such subgroups are conjugate. Proves Hall subgroup properties, Sylow-Hall relationship, index-2 Hall criterion, coprimality infrastructure, the A₄ counterexample (6|12 but no subgroup of order 6), and normal Hall uniqueness.

title: Burnside Counting Lemma from Orbit-Stabilizer
description: The Burnside counting lemma (Cauchy-Frobenius) follows from the orbit-stabilizer theorem, which generalizes Lagrange's theorem. The chain: Lagrange -> Orbit-Stabilizer -> Burnside.

title: Law of Cosines
description: The generalization of the Pythagorean theorem to arbitrary triangles: c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab*cos(C), which reduces to the Pythagorean theorem when C = 90 degrees.

title: Spherical Law of Cosines
description: The spherical analogue of the planar law of cosines: cos(c) = cos(a)cos(b) + sin(a)sin(b)cos(C), for a spherical triangle on the unit sphere S² with arc-length sides a, b, c and dihedral angle C opposite side c. Proved using inner product decomposition of unit vectors in ℝ³.

title: Hyperbolic Law of Cosines
description: Axiomatizes the hyperbolic law of cosines cosh(c) = cosh(a)·cosh(b) - sinh(a)·sinh(b)·cos(C) and its dual (second law of cosines relating angles). The laws are encoded as structure fields (assumptions), not proved from a hyperbolic metric model. Proves the hyperbolic Pythagorean theorem (C=π/2 gives cosh(c) = cosh(a)·cosh(b)), the angle defect (A+B+C < π), and key hyperbolic function identities from Mathlib. 13 theorems, 2 structures, 3 structure-encoded axioms.

title: Stewart's Theorem from Law of Cosines
description: Derives Stewart's theorem b²m + c²n = a(d² + mn) from the law of cosines applied to sub-triangles with supplementary angles. Includes median length formula as special case.

title: Laws of Large Numbers
description: The Laws of Large Numbers describe how sample averages converge to expected values. The Weak Law shows convergence in probability, while the Strong Law shows almost sure convergence.

title: LLN for Heavy-Tailed Distributions (Open Question)
description: What happens with heavy-tailed distributions where variance is infinite? The standard WLLN proof via Chebyshev's inequality requires finite variance (E[X²] < ∞), but many important distributions (Pareto α ∈ (1,2), stable laws, Lévy) have infinite variance with finite first moment. We prove: Kolmogorov's SLLN requires only E[|X|] < ∞ — NOT finite variance — so both SLLN and WLLN hold for heavy-tailed distributions with finite mean.

title: Lebesgue Measure
description: Lebesgue measure extends the notion of length/area/volume to a rich class of sets, enabling the powerful Lebesgue integral that revolutionized analysis.

title: Dirichlet Function Integral via Almost Everywhere Zero
description: A complete proof that the Dirichlet function (indicator of rationals) has Lebesgue integral zero over [0,1], resolving an axiom from the parent Lebesgue Measure proof. Uses Mathlib's ae filter and integral_eq_zero_of_ae to show that since ℚ has measure zero, the indicator 𝟙_ℚ is zero almost everywhere, giving ∫₀¹ 𝟙_ℚ = 0. Also proves the function is nowhere continuous and extends the result to arbitrary sets.

title: Modified Dirichlet Function (Thomae's Function) — Lebesgue Integral Zero
description: The modified Dirichlet function f(p/q) = 1/q (Thomae's function) has Lebesgue integral 0, because it equals 0 almost everywhere on the irrationals.

title: Hölder's Inequality for Lebesgue Integration
description: A complete formalization of Hölder's inequality in the measure-theoretic setting, replacing the placeholder in the parent Lebesgue Measure proof. Covers Young's inequality, the Lebesgue integral Hölder bound, Cauchy-Schwarz as the p=q=2 specialization, Minkowski's inequality for Lp spaces, and L² as an inner product space. 10 theorems, 0 sorries.

title: Infinite-Dimensional Measure Theory
description: Explores why Lebesgue measure fails in infinite dimensions (no translation-invariant σ-finite measure) and what replaces it (Gaussian/Wiener measures). Proves the orthonormal separation argument.

title: Legendre's Conjecture (Partial)
description: Legendre's conjecture (1798) — one of the oldest open problems in number theory — asserts that for every positive integer n, there exists a prime between n² and (n+1)². This formalization verifies the conjecture for n = 1 to 20 using explicit prime witnesses checked by native_decide, proves the gap formula (n+1)² - n² = 2n + 1, and states the full conjecture as an axiom.

title: Leibniz's Series for Pi
description: The Leibniz formula for pi: the alternating series 1 - 1/3 + 1/5 - 1/7 + ... converges to pi/4.

title: Optimal Convergence Rate for Arctangent-Based Pi Series
description: The Leibniz series converges at rate Θ(1/N): error |π/4 - Sₙ| ≤ 1/(2N+1), which is sharp. Machin-type formulas achieve exponential O(1/m^(2N)) rates.

title: Machin's Formula from the Arctan Addition Formula
description: Derives Machin's formula pi/4 = 4*arctan(1/5) - arctan(1/239) step by step from three applications of the arctan addition formula arctan(x) + arctan(y) = arctan((x+y)/(1-xy)). No pre-packaged Mathlib lemma is used for the final identity.

title: L'Hopital's Rule
description: A fundamental technique for evaluating limits of indeterminate forms: if f(x)/g(x) approaches 0/0 or infinity/infinity, then the limit equals the limit of f'(x)/g'(x).

title: L'Hôpital's Rule: ∞/∞ Form
description: The ∞/∞ form of L'Hôpital's rule: if g(x) → ∞ and f'(x)/g'(x) → c, then f(x)/g(x) → c. Complements Mathlib's 0/0 form.

title: Liouville's Theorem on Transcendental Numbers
description: Liouville numbers are transcendental. This provides the first explicit construction of transcendental numbers via rational approximation bounds.

title: The Principle of Mathematical Induction
description: For any predicate P on natural numbers, if P(0) holds and P(n) implies P(n+1) for all n, then P(n) holds for all n. Peano's fifth axiom and the foundation of recursive proofs.

title: Transfinite Induction over Ordinals
description: Connects Lean's WellFounded recursion to transfinite induction over ordinals. Proves transfinite induction via Ordinal.induction, the zero/successor/limit trichotomy, course-of-values induction, and the equivalence with the well-ordering principle.

title: Mean Value Theorem
description: If f is continuous on [a,b] and differentiable on (a,b), there exists c where f'(c) = (f(b)-f(a))/(b-a).

title: Taylor's Theorem with Lagrange Remainder
description: Formalizes the higher-order Mean Value Theorem (Taylor's theorem with Lagrange remainder). Defines the Taylor polynomial, axiomatizes the Lagrange remainder, proves MVT is the n=0 case, and derives the second-order Taylor expansion.

title: Vector-Valued Mean Value Inequality
description: The classical MVT equality f'(c) = slope generalizes to the mean value inequality for vector-valued functions: ‖f(b) - f(a)‖ ≤ C·(b-a) when ‖f'(t)‖ ≤ C. Proves 17 theorems with 0 sorries covering the core inequality, scalar MVT as special case, circular counterexample, Lipschitz consequences, ODE uniqueness bounds, and Banach space generalizations.

title: Minkowski's Fundamental Theorem
description: A convex, centrally symmetric body with volume greater than 2^n times the covolume of a lattice contains a non-zero lattice point. The founding result of the geometry of numbers.

title: Dirichlet's Approximation Theorem via Minkowski's Lattice Point Theorem
description: Dirichlet's approximation theorem (for any real α and positive integer Q, there exist integers p, q with 1 ≤ q ≤ Q and |qα − p| < 1/Q) proved as a corollary of Minkowski's fundamental theorem via a parallelogram of area 4(Q+1)/Q > 4.

title: Morley's Theorem
description: The three angle trisectors of any triangle, taken in pairs, meet to form an equilateral triangle. A surprising result discovered in 1899.

title: Conway's Backward Construction for Morley's Theorem
description: Formalizes Conway's backward proof approach to Morley's theorem: the ear construction, angle identities, side length formula, and the reduction to a symmetric computation. All supporting lemmas proved; the coordinate verification remains.

title: Motivic Class of Genus 0 Maps to Flag Varieties
description: The motivic class of based rational maps from P¹ to flag varieties equals the class of GL_n times affine space in the Grothendieck ring of varieties.

title: Motivic Classes of Maps to Partial Flag Varieties
description: Extends the Bryan et al. motivic class theorem to partial flag varieties. Formalizes q-analog infrastructure (q-numbers, q-factorials), Grassmannian motivic classes via recursive Schubert cell decomposition, the Gaussian binomial identity, and states the conjectured extension to partial flags with parabolic subgroups.

title: Napoleon's Theorem
description: If equilateral triangles are constructed externally on the sides of any triangle, their centroids form an equilateral triangle. A classical result of elementary geometry.

title: Global Regularity for Navier-Stokes
description: A conditional regularity theorem for the Navier-Stokes Millennium Prize Problem. We identify the precise structural obstruction (scale-bridging concentration) and formulate the minimal Bubble Persistence hypothesis B′ under which all known tools close: B′ → Type I → ESŠ → regularity.

title: Navier-Stokes Existence and Smoothness
description: Comprehensive formalization of the Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness problem (Millennium Prize). Includes complete 2D global existence proof (no axioms), 3D conditional regularity via NSAxioms structure (5 structure-encoded assumptions), and 110 parts covering the full landscape of NS theory: ancient solutions, ESS theorem, CKN partial regularity, Leray-Hopf theory, Serrin regularity, BKM criterion, weak-strong uniqueness, Kolmogorov turbulence, Onsager conjecture, convex integration, Fujita-Kato mild solutions, helicity, Liouville theorems, Tao barrier, Koch-Tataru, backward uniqueness, geometric regularity, profile decomposition, global attractors, determining modes, and exact turbulence results. 20,000+ lines, 1200+ definitions/theorems, 0 sorries, 5 structure-encoded assumptions (NSAxioms).

title: 2D Navier-Stokes: Quantitative Enstrophy Decay and Energy Identity
description: For 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes with Poincaré inequality, can we formalize quantitative enstrophy decay and the exact integrated energy identity? We prove: (1) E(t) ≤ E(s)·exp(-2νμ₁(t-s)) for all 0 ≤ s ≤ t (uniform decay), (2) ∫₀ᵀ -2νP(t) dt = E(T) - E(0) (FTC applied to the enstrophy ODE), and (3) ∫₀ᵀ 2νP dt ≤ E(0) (total dissipation bounded by initial enstrophy).

title: 2D Navier-Stokes: Gronwall Stability, Uniqueness, and Well-Posedness
description: For 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes, can we formalize L² stability, uniqueness, and continuous dependence on initial data using the Gronwall inequality? We prove: (1) W(t) ≤ W(0)·exp(C·E(0)·t) (Gronwall stability bound), (2) W(0) = 0 implies W(t) = 0 (uniqueness), (3) for any ε > 0, there exists δ > 0 such that W(0) ≤ δ implies W(t) ≤ ε on [0,T] (continuous dependence). Together these establish Hadamard well-posedness for 2D Navier-Stokes.

title: Newton's Log-Concavity Inductive Step
description: Proves the key binomial coefficient inequality for Newton's log-concavity theorem: bc^3 + adc^2 + ac^3 >= 2b^2cd + b^3d where a, b, c, d are consecutive binomial coefficients. Uses absorption identities to reduce to a polynomial identity verified by linear_combination. Imported by AmgmInequalityOQ02OQ02 and NewtonIndStep2.

title: Newton's Inequality: e_k² ≥ e_{k-1} · e_{k+1}
description: Formalizes Newton's inequality for elementary symmetric polynomials of nonnegative reals: the sequence of elementary symmetric means ē_k = e_k / C(n,k) is log-concave. Proves log-concavity of binomial coefficients, explicit small cases (n=2,3), and consequences including the first Maclaurin inequality.

title: Irrationality of nth Roots
description: A general theorem proving that for any n >= 2 and m >= 1, if m is not a perfect nth power, then the nth root m^(1/n) is irrational. Subsumes all specific irrationality proofs for square roots, cube roots, fourth roots, and beyond.

title: Nth Root Irrationality via Irreducible Polynomials
description: Algebraic irrationality via irreducible polynomials: proves that roots of irreducible polynomials of degree >= 2 over Q are irrational, applies Eisenstein's criterion to show X^n - p is irreducible for prime p, and derives irrationality of nth roots of primes. Imported by InverseGalois, InverseGaloisD4, InverseGaloisF20, and AngleTrisectionOQ02.

title: P vs NP Problem
description: One of the seven Millennium Prize Problems. Can every problem whose solution can be verified quickly also be solved quickly?

title: PAC Learning and VC Dimension
description: Finite VC dimension iff PAC learnable. Sample complexity O((d + log(1/delta))/epsilon^2). The fundamental theorem of statistical learning.

title: Independence of the Parallel Postulate
description: Euclid's parallel postulate is independent of the other axioms of geometry. There exist consistent geometries (Euclidean and hyperbolic) that differ on this postulate.

title: Parallel Postulate Independence: Beltrami-Klein Verification
description: Constructs the Beltrami-Klein disk model of hyperbolic geometry with explicit coordinate geometry and proves the hyperbolic parallel property concretely, establishing independence of the parallel postulate via model construction.

title: Euler's Partition Theorem
description: The number of partitions of n into odd parts equals the number of partitions into distinct parts. A beautiful bijection in combinatorics.

title: Rogers-Ramanujan and Schur Partition Identities
description: Formalizes the Rogers-Ramanujan and Schur partition identities in Lean 4. Defines partition sets via gap conditions and modular arithmetic, states the identities as axioms (verified computationally), and proves structural properties including that gap ≥ 2 partitions are necessarily distinct.

title: Euler Partition Identities for Overpartitions
description: Defines overpartitions (partitions with optional overlined parts) and formalizes their connection to Euler's partition identity.

title: Pascal's Hexagon Theorem
description: If a hexagon is inscribed in a conic section, the three pairs of opposite sides meet at collinear points. A fundamental result in projective geometry.

title: Solutions to Pell's Equation
description: Pell's equation x^2 - Dy^2 = 1 always has infinitely many solutions when D is not a perfect square, all generated from a unique fundamental solution.

title: Pell Equation: Size of the Fundamental Solution
description: Investigation of the Pell regulator R(D) = log(x₁ + y₁√D) for the fundamental solution to x² - Dy² = 1. States the heuristic conjecture R(D) = O(√D log D), proves basic bounds, and formalizes connections to class numbers and computational complexity.

title: Perfect Number Theorem
description: The Euclid-Euler theorem: a number is even and perfect if and only if it has the form 2^(p-1)(2^p - 1) where 2^p - 1 is a Mersenne prime.

title: Transcendence of Pi
description: Pi is transcendental: it is not a root of any polynomial with integer coefficients. This proves the impossibility of squaring the circle with ruler and compass.

title: Pick's Theorem
description: The area of a simple lattice polygon equals I + B/2 - 1, where I is the number of interior lattice points and B is the number of boundary lattice points.

title: Pick's Theorem via Triangulation
description: Constructive proof strategy for Pick's theorem via triangulation into primitive lattice triangles. Proves the base case (primitive triangles), the shoelace formula, Pick's formula for rectangles, and the additivity lemma when merging polygons. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Ehrhart Polynomials for Lattice Polytopes
description: Ehrhart polynomials generalize Pick's formula to higher dimensions: for a d-dimensional lattice polytope P, the lattice point count of nP is a polynomial of degree d in n. Verified on cubes, simplices, cross-polytopes (octahedra), and their products, with Ehrhart-Macdonald reciprocity, h*-vector palindromy, and reflexive polytope characterization.

title: The Number of Platonic Solids
description: There are exactly five Platonic solids (regular convex polyhedra): the tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron.

title: Classification of Regular Polytopes in Higher Dimensions
description: Extends the Platonic solids classification to 4D and higher dimensions using the Coxeter-Schlaefli determinant. Proves there are exactly 6 regular 4-polytopes, 3 regular 5-polytopes, and verifies the high-dimensional stabilization pattern.

title: Classification of Archimedean (Semi-Regular) Solids
description: Formalizes the 13 Archimedean solids: convex vertex-transitive polyhedra with regular faces that are neither Platonic nor prisms/antiprisms. Defines vertex types, verifies angle defects computationally, records Euler formula data, and proves structural properties.

title: The Poincaré Conjecture
description: Every simply connected, closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere. Solved by Grigori Perelman in 2002-2003 using Ricci flow with surgery.

title: Explicit Prime Gap Bounds from Bertrand's Postulate
description: Derives explicit bounds on prime gaps and the n-th prime from Bertrand's postulate: pi(2n) > pi(n) for n >= 1, iterated doubling bounds pi(2^k * n) >= pi(n) + k, small value computations of pi, and the exponential bound p_n <= 2^(n+1) by induction. Imported by BoundedPrimeGaps and BertrandsPostulateOQ03.

title: The Prime Number Theorem
description: The prime counting function pi(x) is asymptotically equivalent to x/ln(x). This describes the distribution of prime numbers among positive integers.

title: Divergence of Prime Reciprocals
description: The sum of reciprocals of all prime numbers diverges: 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/5 + 1/7 + 1/11 + ... = infinity.

title: Erdős's Elementary Proof of Prime Divergence
description: Erdős's elementary proof that there are infinitely many primes via smooth number counting, without analytic infrastructure.

title: Primitive Roots Modulo Primes
description: For any prime p, there are exactly φ(p-1) primitive roots modulo p. Uses the cyclic structure of (ℤ/pℤ)* and Mathlib's counting theorem.

title: Alteration Method (Probabilistic Method)
description: Random construction + deterministic fix-up for existence proofs in graph theory and combinatorics.

title: Probabilistic Method Applications
description: Classical applications: Ramsey bounds, chromatic number, property B, independent sets. Demonstrates the probabilistic method library.

title: First Moment Method (Probabilistic Method)
description: If E[X] > t, then some outcome exceeds t. Foundation of the probabilistic method, with Erdos's 1947 proof that R(k,k) >= 2^(k/2).

title: Probabilistic Method: Finset to MeasureTheory Bridge
description: Bridges the gallery's Finset-based probabilistic method to Mathlib's MeasureTheory. Shows finite probability is a special case of measure-theoretic probability, with linearity of expectation proved from integral_add.

title: Lovasz Local Lemma
description: If bad events are each unlikely and mostly independent, they can all be avoided. Crown jewel of the probabilistic method.

title: Second Moment Method (Probabilistic Method)
description: Chebyshev and Paley-Zygmund inequalities for concentration and existence proofs in combinatorics.

title: Product of Segments of Chords
description: If two chords of a circle intersect at point P, then the product of the segments of one chord equals the product of the segments of the other: PA * PB = PC * PD.

title: Ptolemy's Inequality via Complex Numbers
description: The algebraic identity (z₁-z₃)(z₂-z₄) = (z₁-z₂)(z₃-z₄) + (z₂-z₃)(z₁-z₄) yields Ptolemy's inequality via the triangle inequality in ℂ

title: Ptolemy's Theorem
description: For a cyclic quadrilateral, the product of diagonals equals the sum of products of opposite sides: AC·BD = AB·CD + BC·DA

title: Puiseux's Theorem
description: The field of Puiseux series (fractional power series) is algebraically closed. This provides a concrete algebraic closure of the Laurent series field.

title: Pythagorean Theorem
description: The Pythagorean Theorem (Wiedijk #4): $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$. Formalized in Lean 4 via Mathlib's inner product space framework — orthogonality $\langle v,w \rangle = 0$ implies $\|v+w\|^2 = \|v\|^2 + \|w\|^2$ by bilinearity. Includes the converse, $\mathbb{R}^2$ specialization, and the $(3,4,5)$ verification. 214 lines, 0 sorries, 0 axioms, badge: original.

title: Pythagorean Theorem in Non-Euclidean Geometry
description: The Pythagorean theorem across four geometries: cosh(c) = cosh(a)cosh(b) in hyperbolic space, cos(c) = cos(a)cos(b) on the sphere, a² + b² = c² in Euclidean space, and τ² = t² − x² in Minkowski spacetime. Includes Lorentz boost invariance, rapidity composition, and the twin paradox.

title: Formula for Pythagorean Triples
description: All primitive Pythagorean triples (a,b,c) with a² + b² = c² are given by a = m² - n², b = 2mn, c = m² + n² for coprime m > n > 0.

title: Density of Primitive Pythagorean Triples
description: Proves that the number of primitive Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse c ≤ N is asymptotically N/(2π). Decomposes the result into sector lattice point density (π/8), coprime fraction (6/π²), and parity correction (2/3). Includes parity involutions, column decomposition, and computational verification. 97 theorems, 7 axioms, 0 sorries.

title: Pythagorean Triples via Gaussian Integers
description: Shows that the parametric formula for Pythagorean triples (m²-n², 2mn, m²+n²) is the squaring map in ℤ[i]. Norm multiplicativity gives the Brahmagupta-Fibonacci identity and a product rule for triples. Fully verified, 0 axioms.

title: Law of Quadratic Reciprocity
description: Quadratic Reciprocity (Wiedijk #7): Gauss's 'golden theorem' — for distinct odd primes $p, q$, $(p/q)(q/p) = (-1)^{(p-1)(q-1)/4}$, i.e., the Legendre symbols agree unless both $p \equiv q \equiv 3 \pmod{4}$. Formalized in Lean 4 via Mathlib's `ZMod.quadraticReciprocity`. Includes the first and second supplements. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Quadratic Reciprocity as a Computation Algorithm
description: The Law of Quadratic Reciprocity combined with multiplicativity yields a GCD-like algorithm for computing Legendre symbols, demonstrated with verified examples

title: Verified Recursive Legendre Symbol Computation
description: Implements the Legendre/Jacobi symbol computation as an explicit recursive function with a termination proof and full correctness verification against Mathlib's jacobiSym

title: The Ramanujan Sum Fallacy
description: A demonstration of how Lean catches the famous fallacious 'proof' that 1+2+3+... = -1/12, showing why mathematical rigor matters.

title: Ramsey R(4,k) Bounds: Probabilistic Method Extensions
description: Formalizes Ramsey theory bounds for R(4,k) via the probabilistic method. Proves the Erdős 1947 lower bound R(k,k) ≥ 2^(k/2), the Spencer improvement, the Conlon-Fox-Sudakov upper bound, and the R(4,k) quadratic lower bound R(4,k) ≥ Ω(k²/log k). 74 theorems, 15 axioms for the deep analytic bounds.

title: Ramsey's Theorem
description: Frank Ramsey's foundational theorem in combinatorics: for any 2-coloring of the complete graph K_n with sufficiently large n, there exists a monochromatic clique.

title: Ramsey Theory for Hypergraphs
description: Extends Ramsey's theorem from graphs (k=2) to k-uniform hypergraphs. The hypergraph Ramsey theorem states that for any k, r, n, sufficiently large sets have monochromatic k-subsets under any r-coloring.

title: Randomized MaxCut Approximation
description: A formal proof that a simple randomized algorithm achieves a 1/2-approximation for the NP-Complete Maximum Cut problem, using linearity of expectation.

title: Goemans-Williamson 0.878-Approximation for MaxCut
description: Formalization of the Goemans-Williamson (1995) semidefinite programming approach to MaxCut, achieving an approximation ratio of α_GW ≈ 0.878 via hyperplane rounding of SDP relaxation.

title: Weighted MaxCut Approximation
description: Extends randomized MaxCut to weighted graphs: random partition achieves W/2 cut weight. Goemans-Williamson 0.878 approximation.

title: Riemann Hypothesis Consequences
description: Formalizes consequences of the Riemann Hypothesis including the Mertens function bound |M(x)| = O(√x), Möbius function properties, Chebyshev theta function, and computed values. Uses Mathlib's built-in RiemannHypothesis definition.

title: The Riemann Hypothesis
description: A comprehensive formalization of the Riemann Hypothesis (6594 lines, 540+ proved theorems, 32 axioms, 0 sorries). States RH using Mathlib's zeta function, proves GRH→RH, establishes 14 equivalent formulations (K₁₀ network + BSY, Riesz, Báez-Duarte, Volchkov integral criteria) with 91 pairwise equivalences, shows ¬RH forces 4 distinct off-line zeros, moment growth rates, Selberg class, de Bruijn-Newman constant, random matrix theory, and arithmetic consequences.

title: Roth's Theorem (Szemeredi k=3)
description: Every subset of [N] with no 3-term arithmetic progression has size o(N). The k=3 case of Szemeredi's theorem, proved by Roth via Fourier analysis.

title: Quantitative Bounds for Roth's Theorem
description: Formalizes the Roth number r₃(N) — the maximum size of a 3-AP-free subset of [N] — and states the major quantitative bounds from Roth (1953) through Kelley-Meka (2023).

title: Roth's Theorem via Triangle Removal Lemma
description: The Ruzsa-Szemerédi (1978) construction encoding 3-term arithmetic progressions as triangles in a tripartite graph, providing an alternative proof of Roth's theorem via the triangle removal lemma.

title: Density Increment Generalization to k-APs via Gowers Norms
description: Formalizes the generalization of Roth's density increment to k-term arithmetic progressions using Gowers uniformity norms. Gowers norms and k-AP counting operator defined constructively. For k=3, explicit density increment proved from RothTheorem infrastructure.

title: Russell's 1+1=2
description: The legendary proof that 1+1=2, which famously took 362 pages in Principia Mathematica but is trivial in modern type theory.

title: Schauder Fixed Point Theorem
description: Generalizes Brouwer's fixed point theorem to infinite-dimensional spaces: every continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a locally convex space has a fixed point. Includes the full hierarchy from Brouwer through Schauder and Tychonoff, with applications to ODEs and contractions.

title: Schauder Projection Lemma
description: The Schauder projection lemma: given a compact set K in a normed space and epsilon > 0, there exists a continuous map approximating the identity on K with image in a finite-dimensional convex hull. Proved from first principles using partition of unity.

title: Kakutani Fixed Point Theorem for Set-Valued Maps
description: Formalizes the Kakutani fixed point theorem framework: set-valued maps, upper hemicontinuity, and the main theorem for compact convex sets. Recovers Brouwer as a corollary.

title: Schroeder-Bernstein Theorem
description: If there exist injections f: A to B and g: B to A, then there exists a bijection between A and B. This establishes that cardinality is antisymmetric.

title: Knaster-Tarski Proof of Schroeder-Bernstein
description: The Schroeder-Bernstein theorem proved via the Knaster-Tarski fixed point theorem: the monotone operator T(S) = (range g)ᶜ ∪ g''(f''S) on Set α has a least fixed point S* that partitions α into the bijection h(a) = f(a) for a ∈ S*, h(a) = g⁻¹(a) otherwise.

title: Constructive Schroeder-Bernstein for Finite Types
description: For finite types with decidable equality, the orbit classification at the heart of Cantor-Bernstein-Schroeder is decidable. We construct a bijection from mutual injections with fully computable orbit classification, answering OQ-04: constructive CBS for specific set classes.

title: Shannon Noisy Channel Coding Theorem
description: Reliable communication at any rate below channel capacity C = max I(X;Y). The central result of information theory.

title: BSC Capacity Proof and Random Coding Foundation
description: Proves the binary symmetric channel capacity formula C(BSC(p)) = log 2 - h(p) from first principles, independently proving the bsc_capacity_eq axiom from the parent formalization. Establishes the random coding existence lemma (probabilistic method). Inherits 4 axioms from the parent import; introduces no new axioms or sorries.

title: Binary Entropy Function: Properties and Concavity
description: Formalizes the binary entropy function h(p) = -p ln p - (1-p) ln(1-p) with full proofs of boundary values, symmetry, non-negativity, maximum at p=1/2 (= ln 2 nats = 1 bit), the sharp upper bound h(p) ≤ ln 2 via binary Gibbs inequality, the zero-characterization h(p)=0 iff p∈{0,1}, and concavity on [0,1] from Mathlib's convexity of x·log(x).

title: Shannon Entropy
description: H(X) = -sum p(x) log p(x). Foundation of information theory: non-negativity, chain rule, data processing inequality.

title: Kolmogorov Complexity and Shannon Entropy
description: H(X) = E[K(X)] + O(1): the fundamental link between information-theoretic and algorithmic notions of information. Shannon entropy equals expected Kolmogorov complexity up to a constant for computable distributions.

title: Strong Subadditivity of Shannon Entropy
description: Strong subadditivity H(X,Y,Z) + H(Y) ≤ H(X,Y) + H(Y,Z): the deepest inequality in classical information theory. Defines 3-variable marginal distributions, proves their properties, states the entropy chain rule, subadditivity, and SSA with clear proof strategies.

title: Shannon Source Coding Theorem
description: Shannon's source coding theorem (1948): the entropy $H(X) = -\sum_x p(x)\log p(x)$ is the fundamental limit of lossless data compression. For an i.i.d. source, compression to rate $R > H(X)$ bits per symbol is achievable with vanishing error, while any code at rate $R < H(X)$ fails. Proved via the Asymptotic Equipartition Property (AEP), which shows that probability concentrates on a typical set of $\approx 2^{nH}$ sequences. Currently a placeholder formalization with theorem stubs proving True.

title: Rate-Distortion Theory
description: Shannon's rate-distortion theory (1959): the minimum rate for lossy compression at distortion D is R(D) = min I(X;X̂) subject to E[d(X,X̂)] ≤ D. Formalizes distortion measures, test channels, the rate-distortion function, Hamming/binary entropy, and the Gaussian case R(D) = ½ log(σ²/D) with proved non-negativity, monotonicity, and boundary properties.

title: Huffman Coding Optimality
description: Huffman coding minimizes average code length among prefix-free codes. Entropy bounds H(p)/ln2 ≤ L* < H(p)/ln2 + 1.

title: Shapley-Folkman Lemma
description: Every point in the convex hull of a Minkowski sum of N sets in d-dimensional space can be decomposed so that at most d summands come from convex hulls rather than the original sets. A fundamental result connecting convex analysis and mathematical economics.

title: Solution of the Cubic Equation
description: Cardano's formula provides explicit radical solutions to cubic equations x³ + px + q = 0 via cube roots of the discriminant. Wiedijk #37. Fully proved in Lean 4 with all three roots via cube roots of unity.

title: Vieta's Formulas for the Cubic via Cardano's Roots
description: Proves that the three Cardano roots of x³ + px + q = 0 satisfy Vieta's formulas (sum = 0, pairwise products = p, triple product = -q) and derives the complete factorization into linear factors.

title: Discriminant of the Depressed Cubic
description: Δ = -4p³ - 27q² = (x₁-x₂)²(x₁-x₃)²(x₂-x₃)² for the depressed cubic x³+px+q=0. Includes root nature from discriminant sign.

title: Casus Irreducibilis: When Real Roots Require Complex Cube Roots
description: Formalizes the casus irreducibilis: when the depressed cubic x³+px+q=0 has three distinct real roots (Δ>0), Cardano's formula necessarily involves non-real complex cube roots. Proves D<0 implies non-real arguments, verifies a concrete example (x³-7x+6=0), and states Wantzel's impossibility theorem.

title: Resolvent Cubic Reduces to Cardano's Formula
description: Proves that Ferrari's resolvent cubic for the quartic equation reduces to a depressed cubic solvable by Cardano's formula, completing the quartic-cubic-Cardano solution chain.

title: Vieta's Formulas for the General Cubic
description: For the general cubic x³ + ax² + bx + c = (x-r₁)(x-r₂)(x-r₃), Vieta's formulas give a = -(r₁+r₂+r₃), b = r₁r₂+r₁r₃+r₂r₃, c = -r₁r₂r₃. Proved over any commutative ring by polynomial coefficient comparison.

title: Sophie Germain Primes
description: A prime p is a Sophie Germain prime if 2p+1 is also prime. We prove that all Sophie Germain primes greater than 3 must have the form 6k-1 (equivalently, p ≡ 5 mod 6).

title: n-Dimensional Sperner's Lemma via Abstract Triangulation
description: Formalization of Sperner's lemma in arbitrary dimension d for any abstract triangulation satisfying adjacency axioms. Proves the Sperner Parity Theorem: the number of fully-colored simplices has the same parity as the number of boundary doors on the last face. The proof uses the door-counting argument with a fixed-point-free involution pairing interior doors.

title: Freudenthal Adjacency Theorem: Interior Facets Belong to Exactly 2 Simplices
description: The Freudenthal triangulation divides the n-cube [0,1]^n into n! simplices indexed by permutations of {0,...,n-1}. This formalization proves the Freudenthal Adjacency Theorem: each interior (n-1)-facet belongs to exactly 2 simplices. Representing simplices as nodup lists and their vertex sets as prefix Finsets, the proof reduces to a clean combinatorial lemma: if |B \ A| = 2, there are exactly 2 sets S with A ⊆ S ⊆ B and |S| = |A| + 1.

title: Brouwer Fixed Point via Displacement Coloring (n-dimensional)
description: Connects the n-dimensional Sperner's lemma to the Brouwer fixed point theorem via the displacement coloring construction. Defines barycentric displacement, proves the displacement coloring satisfies the Sperner boundary condition in arbitrary dimension, and proves the approximate fixed point and Brouwer FPT theorems.

title: Basic Lean Examples
description: A collection of simple example proofs demonstrating basic Lean tactics including non-negativity of squares and implication transitivity.

title: Generalized Non-Negativity of Squares
description: Generalizes square_nonneg from ℤ to any LinearOrderedSemiring using Mathlib's mul_self_nonneg. Shows the parent's case-analysis proof technique also generalizes. Includes consequences: sum of squares non-negativity and an AM-GM variant.

title: Square Root of 2 is Irrational (From Axioms)
description: A complete proof that sqrt(2) is irrational built from first principles, demonstrating the classical proof by contradiction with even/odd analysis.

title: Irrationality of √p for Any Prime p (From Axioms)
description: Generalizes the √2 irrationality proof to all primes: for any prime p, there are no coprime a, b with a² = p·b². Built from scratch using Euclid's criterion for primality.

title: Irrationality of Square Roots
description: The classic proof that √2 is irrational, generalized to show √n is irrational for any non-perfect-square n. Covers √2, √3, √5, √6, √7 and the general theorem.

title: Irrationality of √2 + √3
description: Proves that √2 + √3 is irrational by contradiction: if √2 + √3 = r ∈ ℚ, then squaring gives r² = 5 + 2√6, so √6 = (r² - 5)/2 ∈ ℚ, contradicting the irrationality of √6. Also proves √6 irrational using Mathlib's irrational_sqrt_natCast_iff. 3 theorems, 0 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Stirling's Formula
description: Stirling's approximation for factorials: n! ~ sqrt(2*pi*n) * (n/e)^n. The ratio approaches 1 as n goes to infinity.

title: Higher-Order Stirling Expansion
description: Formalizes the first correction term in Stirling's asymptotic expansion: n! ~ √(2πn)(n/e)^n(1 + 1/(12n) + O(1/n²)). Shows this eliminates an axiom.

title: Stirling Approximation for the Gamma Function
description: Extends Stirling's formula from n! to the Gamma function at integer points: Γ(n+1) ~ √(2πn)·(n/e)^n for n : ℕ. Bridges Mathlib's Stirling.factorial_isEquivalent_stirling to the Gamma function via Γ(n+1)=n!, derives bounds, proves Γ(1/2)=√π, half-integer formulas, and the duplication formula. 0 axioms, 0 sorries. Note: the continuous formula for real x is stated as an open question.

title: Number of Subsets of a Set
description: A finite set with n elements has exactly 2^n subsets. This fundamental result connects set theory to binary counting.

title: Subset Counting for Multisets
description: Generalizes the subset counting theorem to multisets: a multiset with n elements has 2^n submultisets, and the number of k-element submultisets is C(n,k).

title: Subset Counting for Multisets
description: Generalizes |P(S)| = 2^n to multisets: a multiset with n elements has 2^n submultisets. Proves the multiset powerset theorem, the multiset choose theorem (C(n,k) submultisets of size k), and the connection between set and multiset cases.

title: Sum of Divisors Function: Properties and Classification
description: Formalizes the arithmetic function σ(n) = Σ_{d|n} d with concrete values, multiplicativity, prime power formula, and number classification. Proves σ(p) = p+1 for all primes, σ(mn) = σ(m)σ(n) when gcd(m,n)=1, σ(p^k) = Σ p^i, and classifies deficient/perfect/abundant numbers. Verifies amicable pairs (220,284) and (1184,1210). Proves 12 is the smallest abundant number. 81 theorems, 4 definitions, 0 axioms.

title: Sum of kth Powers (Faulhaber's Formulas)
description: Closed-form formulas for sums of consecutive kth powers (k=1 through k=5), including the remarkable identity that the sum of cubes equals the square of the sum.

title: Unified Faulhaber Formula via Bernoulli Numbers (OQ-01)
description: The general Faulhaber formula for sums of k-th powers is formalized in Lean 4 using Mathlib's Bernoulli infrastructure. All five specific formulas (k=1 through k=5) are derived as special cases of the single unified identity via pure computation — no induction needed.

title: Sum of Powers: Extension to Non-Integer Exponents
description: Extends Faulhaber's formulas to real exponents via the p-series ζ(s) = ∑ 1/n^s. Proves convergence dichotomy (iff s > 1), recovers ζ(2) = π²/6 and ζ(4) = π⁴/90, establishes term and zeta monotonicity, and bridges real-exponent theory to integer power sums.

title: Euler-Maclaurin Asymptotics for Power Sums
description: Asymptotic formula for power sums: sum_{i=0}^{n-1} i^k / n^{k+1} -> 1/(k+1) as n -> infinity. Axiomatizes Bernoulli polynomial leading behavior and monic polynomial asymptotics. Proves k=0 and k=1 special cases exactly.

title: Sylow's Theorems
description: Sylow's Theorems (Wiedijk #72): for a finite group $G$ and prime $p \mid |G|$, (1) Sylow $p$-subgroups exist, (2) they are all conjugate, (3) their number $n_p \equiv 1 \pmod{p}$ and $n_p \mid |G|/p^k$. Formalized in Lean 4 via Mathlib's `Sylow` infrastructure. The strongest partial converse to Lagrange's theorem. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Classification of Groups of Order pq via Sylow Theorems
description: For distinct primes p < q: if p does not divide (q-1), the only group of order pq is cyclic. If p divides (q-1), there are exactly two groups (cyclic + non-abelian semidirect product). Proves the Sylow counting arguments (n_q = 1, n_p ∈ {1,q}), normality of unique Sylow subgroups, and states the classification theorem with concrete examples (orders 6, 15, 21, 35).

title: Pro-p Sylow Theory for Profinite Groups
description: Generalizes the classical Sylow theorems to profinite groups. Proves conjugation preserves Sylow pro-p structure (closedness, pro-p, maximality), that uniqueness implies normality, plus compactness, trivial subgroup is pro-p, pro-p/p-group equivalence, classical Sylow bridge, counting theorem. 5 axioms, 0 sorries, 10 proved theorems.

title: Sylow-Based Simplicity Proof for A₅
description: Formalizes the Sylow counting argument for the simplicity of A₅. Proves |A₅| = 60 = 2²·3·5, computes the exact Sylow numbers n₂ = 5, n₃ = 10, n₅ = 6, shows no Sylow subgroup is normal, and verifies the conjugacy class arithmetic {1,12,12,15,20} prevents intermediate normal subgroups.

title: Szemeredi Core Definitions
description: Shared definitions and basic lemmas for the Szemeredi regularity pipeline: edge density, epsilon-regular pairs, regular partitions, and partition energy. Imported by both SzemerediRegularity and SzemerediCounting.

title: Counting and Removal Lemma
description: The triangle removal lemma and graph counting lemma. Regular pairs behave like random graphs for subgraph counting, and graphs with few triangles can be made triangle-free cheaply.

title: Szemeredi's Theorem (Case Assembly & Axiom Reduction)
description: Assembles Szemerédi's theorem by cases: k=1,2 proved trivially, k=3 via Mathlib's Roth/corners chain, k>=4 axiomatized. Reduces the full theorem to a single axiom requiring hypergraph regularity.

title: Hypergraph Regularity Core Definitions
description: Core definitions for hypergraph regularity: k-uniform hypergraphs, k-partite density, and epsilon-regularity. Generalizes graph regularity (SzemerediCore) to the hypergraph setting of Gowers (2007).

title: Szemeredi Regularity Lemma (Energy Machinery & Mathlib Bridge)
description: Energy machinery (density convexity, split identities) and compatibility bridge exposing Mathlib's Szemerédi regularity lemma through a combinatorics-oriented API.

title: Szemeredi's Theorem (k=3 via Mathlib)
description: Dense subsets of natural numbers contain arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions. The k=3 case (Roth's theorem) is fully proved using Mathlib's corners theorem chain.

title: Taylor Series Convergence for Sin and Cos
description: Proves that the Taylor series of sin and cos converge to sin(x) and cos(x) for all real x. The key insight: since all iterated derivatives of sin and cos are bounded by 1 (period-4 cycling through {sin, cos, -sin, -cos}), the remainder bound |x|^{n+1}/n! is strictly tighter than the analogous exp bound.

title: Alternating Series Estimation for Sin/Cos Taylor Series
description: Sharpens the Taylor series remainder bounds for sin and cos using the alternating series estimation theorem, providing tighter error bounds than the standard Lagrange remainder.

title: Taylor's Theorem
description: A smooth function can be approximated by its Taylor polynomial, with explicit remainder terms (Lagrange and Cauchy forms).

title: Taylor Series Convergence of exp via the Cauchy Remainder
description: Proves that the Taylor series of exp converges to exp(x) for all real x, with an explicit convergence rate. Using the Lagrange and Cauchy remainder forms, establishes exp(x) = sum x^n/n!, an error bound |e - S_n(1)| <= 3/n!, and the Cauchy remainder applied to exp.

title: Universality of Three-Place Identity
description: Tom Etter's Universality Theorem: three-place relative identity is foundationally adequate for all of mathematics, establishing mutual interpretability with ZF set theory.

title: Etter's Stereo Equality Theorem
description: Formalizes Etter's Stereo Equality Theorem: two equivalence relations suffice to encode three-place relative identity. Proves the forward and reverse constructions, round-trip properties, and shows why a single equivalence relation is insufficient. 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

title: Sum of Angles of a Triangle
description: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle equals 180° (π radians). One of the most fundamental results in Euclidean geometry.

title: The Triangle Inequality
description: The fundamental inequality stating that the sum of any two sides of a triangle exceeds the third side. For real numbers: |x + y| ≤ |x| + |y|.

title: Ultrametric Triangle Inequality
description: In non-Archimedean (ultrametric) spaces, the triangle inequality strengthens to d(x,z) ≤ max(d(x,y), d(y,z)). This forces every triangle to be isosceles, every ball to be clopen, and distinct balls to be disjoint — properties realized by p-adic norms.

title: Sum of Reciprocals of Triangular Numbers
description: The sum of reciprocals of triangular numbers equals 2: ∑(2/(n(n+1))) = 2. A beautiful telescoping series result.

title: Reciprocal Sums of Higher Figurate Numbers
description: Defines k-gonal (figurate) numbers and proves telescoping partial fractions for triangular reciprocals, with convergence of square reciprocals by p-series comparison. Includes the elegant identity that every hexagonal number is triangular.

title: Alternating Sum of Triangular Reciprocals
description: The alternating sum of reciprocals of triangular numbers equals 4·ln(2) - 2: ∑(-1)^{n+1}·2/(n(n+1)) = 4·ln(2) - 2 ≈ 0.7726.

title: Generalized Alternating Reciprocal Product Sum
description: Generalizes ∑(-1)^{n+1}/(n(n+1)) to ∑(-1)^{n+1}/(n(n+k)) for arbitrary k ≥ 1, giving a closed form involving the alternating harmonic partial sums.

title: Twin Primes in Special Forms
description: Twin prime pairs (p, p+2) where both are prime must have the form (6k-1, 6k+1) for p > 3. A structural theorem constraining where twin primes can occur.

title: Unit Distance Graph Independence Numbers and Hadwiger-Nelson Bounds
description: Formalizes independence number theory for unit distance graphs in the plane and proves the Hadwiger-Nelson chromatic number bounds 5 ≤ χ(ℝ²) ≤ 7 (axiomatized). Develops abstract independence set theory for simple graphs, proves structural theorems about the unit distance graph, and connects independence numbers to chromatic bounds. 65 theorems, 2 axioms.

title: Vieta's Formulas
description: Vieta's formulas relate polynomial coefficients to sums and products of roots. For x^2 - bx + c = 0 with roots r, s: r + s = b and r * s = c.

title: Newton's Identities: Power Sums and Elementary Symmetric Polynomials
description: Newton's identities express power sums pₖ = Σxᵢᵏ in terms of elementary symmetric polynomials eⱼ. Proved for 2, 3, and 4 variables: the recursive form pₖ = Σ(-1)^{i-1} eᵢ pₖ₋ᵢ + (-1)^{k-1} k eₖ, plus the inversion formulas recovering eₖ from power sums. Applications to discriminants, matrix traces, and the sum-of-cubes factorization.

title: Generalized Newton's Identities via MvPolynomial
description: Newton's identities generalized to arbitrary n variables using Mathlib's MvPolynomial infrastructure. Defines concrete power sums and elementary symmetric polynomials for Fin n → R, bridges them to MvPolynomial.psum and MvPolynomial.esymm via the aeval evaluation homomorphism, and derives the general Newton recurrence from Mathlib's combinatorial proof.

title: Weak Goldbach Conjecture (Ternary Goldbach)
description: Formalizes the Weak Goldbach Conjecture (proved by Helfgott 2013): every odd integer >5 is a sum of three primes. Axiomatizes Vinogradov's circle method, Helfgott's proof, Schnirelmann density, Ramare's 6-prime bound, Tao's 5-prime bound, and Chen's theorem. Proves structural reductions: binary Goldbach implies ternary, Lévy's conjecture verified for small cases. 27 theorems, 9 axioms.

title: Wilson's Theorem
description: A natural number n > 1 is prime if and only if (n-1)! is congruent to -1 modulo n. A beautiful characterization connecting factorials and primality.

title: Wilson's Theorem: Complete Classification for Non-Prime Moduli
description: Extends Wilson's theorem to all moduli n≥2: for composite n>4, n∣(n-1)!; for n=4, (n-1)! ≡ 2 (mod 4); for primes, (p-1)! ≡ -1 (mod p). Formalizes Wilson primes (p∣(p-1)!+1 with p²), verifies 5, 13 are Wilson primes, and proves the Gauss-Wilson classification (product of units ≡ -1 iff n ∈ {1,2,4,p^k,2p^k}). 33 theorems, 0 axioms.

title: Gauss-Wilson Theorem: Product of Units and Cyclic Groups
description: Formalizes the Gauss-Wilson theorem: ∏(ℤ/nℤ)* = -1 iff (ℤ/nℤ)* is cyclic, proved via involution lemma and self-inverse classification. Full proof that cyclic → product = -1 and non-cyclic → product = 1. Verifies Gauss-Wilson for all n ≤ 300 and confirms no Wilson primes between 14 and 100. 20 theorems, 0 axioms.

title: Gauss's Generalization of Wilson's Theorem
description: For n ≥ 3, the product of all integers coprime to n (mod n) equals -1 if and only if n is 4, an odd prime power p^k, or twice an odd prime power 2p^k. This characterizes exactly when the multiplicative group (ℤ/nℤ)× is cyclic.

title: Abstract Group-Theoretic Product Formula: Unique Involution
description: In any finite commutative group with a unique non-trivial involution τ (τ² = 1, τ ≠ 1), the product of all elements equals τ. Every even-order cyclic group has exactly one such involution (the half-generator g^(|G|/2)), and odd-order groups have product 1. This provides the abstract group-theoretic core of the Gauss–Wilson theorem.

title: Wolstenholme's Theorem
description: For prime p >= 5, the binomial coefficient C(2p-1, p-1) = 1 (mod p^3). Verified computationally for p = 5, 7, 11, 13. Connected to harmonic number divisibility.

title: Infinitely Many Wolstenholme Primes
description: Conjecture: infinitely many primes p satisfy C(2p-1,p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p⁴). Only 16843 and 2124679 are known. Formalizes the conjecture, proves the finite/infinite dichotomy, establishes conditional bounds, states the Bernoulli number characterization, and draws the parallel to Wieferich primes.

title: Wolstenholme Primes and the Mod 4 Question
description: A Wolstenholme prime p has C(2p-1,p-1) ≡ 1 (mod p⁴). Only two known: 16843 and 2124679, both ≡ 3 (mod 4). Proves small primes are not Wolstenholme, both known WPs are ≡ 3 (mod 4), and formalizes the open question of whether a WP ≡ 1 (mod 4) exists.

title: Yang-Mills Existence and Mass Gap
description: Formalization infrastructure for the Yang-Mills Millennium Prize Problem. Defines gauge groups, field strength, lattice gauge theory, and mass gap. The core open conjecture (4D mass gap existence) remains unproven.

title: Yang-Mills: 2D Exact Solution (Migdal Formula)
description: Exact solution of 2D Yang-Mills theory via the Migdal formula. Proves the area law, computes string tension, and establishes the mass gap for SU(2) and SU(3) using Casimir operator calculations and heat kernel expansion.

title: 2D Yang-Mills Heat Kernel Techniques for 3D/4D Extension
description: Proves that 2D Yang-Mills heat kernel terms decay exponentially with area, Wilson loops satisfy an exact area law, and the SU(2) string tension is explicitly computable (sigma = 3g^2/16). The partition function decays monotonically from Z(0) = 14 to trivial representation dominance. These exact 2D results contrast with 3D (topological/Chern-Simons) and 4D (Millennium Prize) where no closed-form solutions exist.

title: Casimir Scaling: Exact in 2D, Approximate in 4D
description: In 2D Yang-Mills (Migdal formula), Casimir scaling holds exactly for all r: the potential ratio equals C₂(R)/C₂(fund). In 4D, exact Casimir scaling fails due to string breaking—after r_break, the adjoint potential saturates while the fundamental grows linearly, so the ratio decreases. The 4D approximate conjecture is axiomatized as open.

title: Yang-Mills: Lattice Gauge Theory
description: Lattice formulation of Yang-Mills theory with proven plaquette gauge invariance, action bounds, Wilson loops, strong coupling expansion, and Creutz ratio diagnostics.

title: Yang-Mills: Finite-Volume Mass Gap (Transfer Matrix)
description: Proven finite-volume mass gap for lattice Yang-Mills via transfer matrix formalism and Perron-Frobenius theory. The mass gap equals log(lambda_0/lambda_1)/a > 0 when the two largest transfer matrix eigenvalues are distinct.
